text:
看到小姑娘的建议，稍微补充一下：

1. 临时的新加坡本地网络和电话有两种，一种是只有流量的，基本都是 esim 这种不需要 KYC ，但也不能打电话和收短信，只能提供流量，总的来说就是没有 +65 的功能。

另一种就是游客卡，主要就是短期的，需要 KYC ，可以在 7-11 等买，或者直接在机场买也可以，可以获得 +65 的功能。

对于部分小伙伴来说，买一个然后注册一些网站是可以的，这种卡一般最多用30天。

推荐用 Singtel 的游客卡，大概 10新币（53人民币不到）、7天有效期、500GB 新加坡/马来西亚/印尼/泰国/香港流量，5G，并包含本地无限通话和短信。实体 SIM 和 eSIM 都有。

非常适合在新加坡以后想要去马来西亚的小伙伴，可以不用换卡了，直接就能在马来西亚用。

2. 入境卡一定要填写，非常快，很好写，基本上填好后 30 分钟内就能收到邮件，收到邮件就可以过关了，新加坡过关效率很高，不用担心。

新加坡过海关不需要小费，没有任何的人工检索通道（小黑屋除外），都是自动机器，非常快。

3. 新加坡入境不能带电子烟，千万别带，电子烟在新加坡是违法的，最好也不要带烟，新加坡烟草管制非常严格，从来不存在一个人可以带 X 支烟这样的说法，哪怕带一根都需要申报。

我知道会有小伙伴会说自己每次都偷偷带，对，不被发现是没事，但如果被发现就会比较麻烦，尤其是带多了点就会当走私处理了。

另外进入新加坡可以带酒，一般来说 500ML 的白酒可以带两瓶，威士忌可以带 1L ，喜欢喝酒的小伙伴出来海关酒可以看到卖酒的，价格还算可以，如果有打折的话当年茅台大概是 230 多新币，没打折的话大概小 300 新币吧。

新加坡买烟在超市也可以买，但烟不会摆在外边，需要自己和售货员说，然后才能买，我不抽烟，所以也不知道都有什么品牌，听说基本都是万宝路。

4. 新加坡换钱挺容易的，汇率也还算过的去，在牛车水（中国街）有很多换汇公司，甚至可以从微信换成新币，也可以把人民币寄回中国，但听说偶尔会出现冻卡。

我个人建议来新加坡还是要带一些现金的，因为并不是所有地方都可以刷信用卡，尤其是小贩中心或者食阁，如果没有新加坡本地的支付方式，现金是最好的。

汇率大概是不到 5.3 元人民币换 1 新币，一般来说小贩中心或者亚坤这类的吃吃一个人大概要 15 新币左右，如果是食阁的话，一碗面大概是 6 新币，一份蛋炒饭大概是 5.5 新币，一份海南鸡大概是 8 新币。

另外新加坡的地铁可以直接用 VISA 和 Mastercard卡，刷了就可以走，应该是按距离收费的，起手点应该是 1 新币左右，我基本做一站都是 1.0X 新币左右。

5. 很多短视频都有介绍新加坡的规矩特别多，动不动就罚款，也对，也不对，确实规矩很多，但也不是非常容易被罚款，一般来说第一次发现都是会警告一下，比如室外没有在规定的地方抽烟。

对，新加坡地铁，公交和出租车上都不能吃东西和喝水，有时候出租车还好，但公众交通如果被发现，对方还是较真的人，确实是挺麻烦的。

总的来说自己都认为不是好事的，就别做，那就肯定没错了。

6. 新加坡的打车其实非常容易，但刚刚来新加坡可能会觉得不方便，首先是打车不能扬招，其次打车都需要去打车点（pickup point），没有在的话，就要自己找，另外新加坡打车基本上有 3 分钟的等待时间，超过时间就要扣超时费。

新加坡最好用的还是 Grab ，尤其是从机场出来的时候，Grab 的性价比要高于出租车，Grab 可以绑定信用卡，而且在新加坡还可以用 USDT 充值（我不记得游客是否可以了），总之 Grab 是挺好用的。

如果看到司机是华人面孔可以尝试说中文，大多数都会讲中文，如果是看到印度裔等那就只能说英文了。

7. 在新加坡大多数的路边店是没有什么“服务”概念的， 尤其是吃饭的时候别指望能有多周到的服务，但相比香港还是强多了，当然也会有部分服务员素质不高的情况，能不吵架尽量就别吵架。

一般的饭店都有 10% 的服务费 和 9% 的税，都含在账单里的，所以不用给小费。新加坡几乎没有小费文化。

8. 如果在新加坡有什么问题，而且恰好你又有我的联系方式，可以联系我，力所能及的帮忙还是没问题的。

还有什么是我遗漏的？

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场

text:
散户怎么和庄斗？

“妖币”为什么第一时间看 OI？因为 OI 才能看到交易所真实的深度

如果你做过 MM（也就是做市商）你会知道你可以毫秒级挂单，同时毫秒级撤单，所以有时候你看着盘口很多订单但是自己永远成交不了

所以一些妖币看他是不是真的“火爆”只需要几个指标：

1️⃣ 成交量：刷量英文是 wash trading，类似于洗钱是需要成本的，超高的成交量就要付出超高的成本，这个庄家不愿意

2️⃣ 未平仓 OI：大部分人都不知道什么是 OI，其实就是大家合约开仓了但是没有平仓的仓位，这个做不了假，真金白银的压在那里还容易爆仓，所以成交量可以伪造 OI 伪造不了（即便庄有钱也是极高的成本）

3️⃣ 总户数：大户可以提供高交易量高 OU，但是散户才是市场的基石，所以抓住大多数散户的才能赢得市场

比如说各个交易所都在说自己的交易量非常高，但是切换成 OI 就是币安断层第一，是第二名的 4 倍，因为这个需要真金白银压在账户里

你就把以上这段话发给 Codex or Claude 做一个监测器，每次有一个币你想要检测的时候喂给他就可以给你最准的结果

The core joke of this Meme is “bringing trading terminology into everyday life.” It takes professional day-trading jargon and applies it directly to mundane daily situations, creating a self-deprecating contrast.

Aiden is the name of the trader behind it. He is trying to express the everyday mindset of a trader: concepts such as screens, positions, stop-losses, and discipline have already permeated his daily life, but he also tries to ease that state of mind through lighthearted self-mockery.

He describes fixed daily habits as “positions that will never get stopped out.” He compares his trading performance with his neighbors, his cat, his monitor stand, and the bagels he eats in the middle of the night. He even uses trading terminology to describe the moments when he steps away from his screen.

By consistently using this style of “trader self-deprecation,” he acknowledges that he is constantly watching screens and making trading decisions, while using trivial details from everyday life to remind himself not to take everything so seriously. This style is close to the dark humor commonly found in trading circles, but his metaphors are more coherent and more closely connected to everyday life.

I find this concept interesting, but I think it still lacks an emotional element that could resonate with a much broader audience.

Dragonfly Capital Managing Partner Haseeb Qureshi  @hosseeb  said in an August 28 interview with  @Bankless   that ongoing token unlocks are hurting secondary-market confidence in some tokens, with many projects facing persistent sell pressure from multi-year unlock schedules. 

He said some strategic investors "dump their tokens the moment they get them," selling each batch as it unlocks throughout a four-year vesting period. text:
With Ethena expanding into the equity basis trade, I wanted to take a look at recent funding rate data across Binance and TradeXYZ.

(data from Sep 1st to Oct 1st)

Some takeaways from the image below:

· Of the 5 largest equity perps (sorted by OI on Binance), SK Hynix had the highest APY at 10.4% on Binance and 15.6% on XYZ

· An RWA basket (OI-weighted and comprised of equities >$10m in OI) averaged 5.25% APY on Binance and 7% on XYZ in this period

· In the same period, BTC delivered a 5.5%-8.8% APY and ETH 4.9%-10.2% APY (depending on the venue)

· The highest funding rates on pairs with OI >$100m were Circle, SK Hynix, DRAM, INTC and NVDA

· XYZ has consistently had higher funding rates than Binance. There are however benefits for Ethena to run this strategy on Binance including lower ADL priority, being able to use spot equities as collateral and higher OI on many of the pairs as of now. 

Perhaps Hyperliquid enabling spot equities as collateral would be enough for Ethena to move some of this strategy over there and capture the higher funding.

As we’ve been in a more bullish environment for crypto lately, funding rates on majors seem to match or even exceed those available through the equity basis trade currently.

In any case, it seems clear that there's a discretionary element in picking the right equities for this sort of strategy given the wide range in funding.

robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 ｜10 月 3 日数据更新

今天的数据确实有点难看，不过我发现，不只是 PONS 在跌，整个市场的交易量都在明显下滑。

1️⃣ Robinhood Chain 交易量继续下降

过去 24 小时，Robinhood Chain DEX 交易量约 $711M，已经跌至全链第四。

目前主要公链排名：
Solana：$2.1B
Ethereum：$756M
Base：$712M
Robinhood Chain：$711M

除了 Solana 还能维持每天 $2B 左右的交易量，其他几条链的交易量都出现了明显下滑，部分接近四成，Robinhood Chain和Base几乎没有差距。

2️⃣ PONS 平台数据

过去 24 小时：
交易量：$90M，下降 19%
协议收入：约 $16 万，下降 24%
新发射代币：约 4,400 个，下降 27%
Holders：102,589，增加约 300 人

交易量、收入和新币发行数量都在下滑，但持币地址反而还在增加。不知道是不是已经有人开始抄底了。

回购销毁方面，因为新的回购机制开始，销毁的速度开始提升，昨天链上大约销毁了 110 万枚 PONS，累计销毁比例从 31.85% 上升至 31.96%，目前回购链路中还有约 $2M 等待执行。

3️⃣ 回购机制和新功能

PONS 最近还公布了回购执行节奏和即将上线的新功能。

首先回购和销毁的执行本身已经自动化了，这次主要调整的是资金执行节奏：每 7 天自动领取一次资金，然后在接下来的 7 天内完成回购，再进入下一轮循环。

新界面会把资金分成两部分：正在执行回购的资金，以及留给下一周的资金。注意，这只是同一笔资金的不同阶段，并不是回购预算翻倍。

另外，PONS 还预告本周上线新的持仓管理功能，可以直接查看自己的持仓、收益和盈亏，并集中管理代币。

4️⃣ 我个人怎么看？

看到 PONS 交易量跌到 $90M 的时候，我第一反应也是PONS 是不是快凉了？

但转头查了一下 Robinhood Chain 的数据，发现整个链的交易量都在下降，Ethereum、Base 的表现也不算好。

这么一对比，PONS 的数据反而没有我最初想象的那么糟糕。

随着 PONS 价格一路下跌，唱空的人也越来越多了。不过我个人现在更关注的不是短期币价，而是它能不能继续守住 Robinhood Chain 上的市场份额。

只要市场份额没有明显丢失，我觉得 PONS 就还有继续观察的价值。当然，份额守住也不代表收入和币价一定能恢复。

现在 PONS 最大的问题，可能已经不在 PONS 自己身上了，而是 Robinhood Chain 的热度到底还能不能维持住。

如果整条链的交易量一直往下掉，PONS 就算守住市场份额，也很难独善其身。

text:
테라펩 X TSMC 썰 정리해봄.

테슬라, 스엑,인텔 주주들 읽어봐봐.

사건의 시작은 타이베이 기반 반도체 기자 팀 컬판(전 블룸버그 칼럼니스트)이 운영하는 Culpium이 독점으로 보도로 시작됨.

여기서 TSMC가 갑자기 등장함.

TSMC가 미래 공장을 직접 소유·운영하고, SpaceX/테라팹은 지분 참여나 생산량 일부 구매 보장, 혹은 둘 다를 하는 구조를 현재 테라펩의 유력한 시나리오로 설명.

그런데 머스크가 여기에 직접 반응하면서 논란 확대.

인텔 $INTC 쪽 지지자들 분노 폭발.

왜 분노 폭발이냐.

사실 인텔 리레이팅 서사가 애플 딜 기대와 테라팹이었음.

(인텔이 노골적으로 PR한 부분도 크고...)

로직은 TSMC, 패키징 일부는 인텔처럼 나눠 맡는 멀티 파운드리 구도도 언급 되면서 주주들은 상당히 심기가 불편함.

테라팹이 지금까지 뽑은 인력 대부분이 인텔 출신이라 더더욱.

하지만, 컬판은 협력 논의는 거의 확정적이며 세세한 경위까지 올리겠다고 반박한 상태.

그럼 왜 지금, 왜 TSMC인가.

사실 TSMC는 관세 때문에라도 지금 미국에 팹을 만들려고 했음. 

테라펩을 TSMC가 운영하면 잠재 경쟁자를 앵커 고객으로 바꾸는면서 미국 진입 가능함.

괜찮은 딜임.

여기에 일론도 시간과 수율을 TSMC가 운영하면서 깔끔하게 해결하면 부담이 덜함.

BofA는 테라팹이 풀가동해도 웨이퍼 원가가 TSMC 첨단 노드보다 30~50% 높을 수 있다고 봤음.

TSMC를 끌어들이면 머스크는 수년을 벌고 산업적 리스크를 크게 줄일 수 있다는 계산이 나옴.

테라팹이 자체 팹에서 수요를 담보로 한 캐파 조달 프로젝트로 성격이 바뀌는 중.

TSMC가 와주면 $SPCX $TSLA 는 자본지출 불확실성, 실행·수율 리스크에서 상당히 자유로워짐.

(아마 스엑 주가가 크게 반응한 이유가 이런 이유 때문인 듯)

text:
Chip design is basically a massive search problem.

Let's take a design with 500,000 standard cells and simplify the problem massively. Forget routing, timing, power, memory, architecture, basically everything else. Just imagine 500,000 cells and ask: how many different ways could I arrange them?

That's 500,000! Roughly 10^2,632,341 possibilities. The exponent alone is over 2.6 million.

Just for some sense of scale, the number of legal positions in Go is ~10^170, and the commonly cited estimate for its full game tree is ~10^360. Protein folding has estimates around ~10^300 possible conformations for a typical protein.

Obviously these aren't the same problems, and I'm not saying chip design is "X times harder" than Go or protein folding. It's just a way to get a feel for how quickly the numbers get ridiculous.

And real chip design is much messier than this toy example. You're making decisions about architecture, memory hierarchy, interconnect, precision, voltage, clocks, floorplanning, routing, timing, power, packaging, cost... and everything affects everything else. Improve timing and you might hurt power. Change the memory system and you've changed bandwidth, latency, area and cost.

Of course nobody brute forces this. EDA tools use hierarchy, constraints, heuristics and decades of optimization work to narrow the problem down. But we still only explore a tiny fraction of what could be built, and exploring each promising direction takes real compute, engineering time and money.

I think AI changes the economics of that search.

Search more of the space. Kill bad ideas earlier. Run more experiments. Try architectures we wouldn't have had the time or money to try before.

And if that loop gets dramatically cheaper and faster, I think we end up taping out more chips, not fewer. More architectures become worth trying. More workloads become worth building custom silicon for.

There's a lot of silicon we never even get the chance to explore today!!

text:
我记得半年前我说自己不怎么 Review PR 了，评论区很多人不认同，觉得这样不靠谱。现在再看，不 Review PR 的人越来越多。比如我刚看的这期播客，在 SpaceXAI 做 Grok Bot 的 Lauren Tan，一个月合并 2500 个 PR，也是不逐个 Review 的：晚上让 AI 自己检查、自己合并，第二天早上她再抽查。

不 Review 不等于不管质量，她靠另外两个办法来保证：
一是让 AI 能像真人用户一样把程序用一遍，自己发现问题；
二是给代码定下很多规矩，让 AI 很难写出烂代码。

她把自己这套做法写成了一组 Skill，公开了出来，叫 pstack。

顺便说一下，这期播客的主持人 Matt Pocock 原本是知名的编程课讲师，他公开的技能库在代码托管网站 GitHub 上有二十多万个星标，是最受欢迎的技能库之一，所以这期算是两位同行对谈。Lauren 之前在 Meta 做网页开发框架 React，今年 3 月加入 AI 编程工具公司 Cursor；Cursor 今年 8 月被 SpaceX 收购，并入旗下的 AI 部门 SpaceXAI。

根据播客的内容，我把 Lauren 的这套做法简单总结一下，我自己的点评在结尾处。

一、先让 AI 能检查自己干的活

Lauren 说，就算不用她的 pstack，每个人最该有的一项技能也是“验证”：给 AI “手和眼睛”，让它能把自己写的程序跑起来，像普通用户一样点一遍，看看结果对不对。

这是她吃过亏之后得出的结论。今年 4 月她在 Cursor 解决一个窗口卡顿的问题，一开始全靠手工：她自己去看各种性能数据，再把看到的转述给 AI，AI 改完她再去看。她形容自己成了 AI 和检测工具之间的“人肉中转站”。她在 Cursor 写的第一个技能就是验证。在这之前，AI 看不到自己改动的效果，只能等她来回传话；有了验证，AI 可以自己改、自己看结果、不满意再改，一轮一轮往下做，不需要她守着。现在她所在的团队里每个产品都配有这样的验证技能，全团队都在用。

做这个技能时她还总结出一条原则：工作里有的部分需要动脑判断，有的部分只是照章办事，照章办事的部分应该写成固定的程序，只把需要判断的留给 AI。起因是她发现，每个 AI 在检查前都要自己从头写一遍检查用的小程序，各写各的，有的能用有的不能用，用完就扔，又慢又浪费。她把这部分做成一个现成的工具，所有 AI 直接调用。

二、AI 反复犯的错，去改规矩，不去改 AI

Lauren 不喜欢“软件工厂”这个流行说法，她更愿意把自己的工作比作经营一家米其林餐厅的后厨。主厨不用亲手做每道菜，但要安排好整个厨房：食材什么时候进、怎么存，每个人用什么工具，菜按什么流程出。工程师现在也一样，不再亲手写代码，却仍然要对结果负责。她认为工程师现在最重要的工作就是把这个“厨房”布置好。没花时间布置的人，信不过 AI 的产出，只能盯着它一步步干，忙到没空改进工具，就像一直拿钝刀切菜。

她举了自己的例子。Grok Bot 最早几版的代码挤在八个巨大的文件里，每个至少一万行，AI 加新功能时就接着往里塞，越塞越乱。她后来定了规矩：每个功能必须放在自己单独的文件夹里，做一件事只允许一种写法，不合规矩的代码会被自动检查拦下来。这样 AI 加功能时不用多想，按规矩放就行。她的习惯是一直观察 AI 在哪里出错，每看到一次就问自己：能不能加一条规矩，让这种错以后根本写不出来。

不逐个检查，靠的也是这套办法。她说，开了几家餐厅的老板不可能尝每一道菜，只能抽查。她每天挑一些改动仔细看，如果只是偶然出错就算了；如果好几个 AI 都在走同一条捷径，说明该改的是规矩和工具。她的 pstack 里有一个全自动模式：每次改动都会派出一批专门负责检查的 AI，把程序打开到处点，找出问题就自己修，反复到没问题再合并。早上她翻一遍改动记录，发现不对就撤回，再补一条新规矩。

她说第一次让 AI 整夜自己合并代码时很害怕，担心半夜把线上产品弄坏，现在反而睡得更好。她也提醒，走到这一步很难，要花大量时间观察和调整，装上 pstack 并不能直接做到。Matt 问，如果改动是没法撤回的，比如会丢数据，或者是医疗、金融这类领域怎么办？她说这取决于工作成果能不能被程序自动检查，软件大部分可以，很难自动检查的领域就很难这样做，她自己也没有答案。

三、2500 次改动从哪来：她不再当传话的人

这 2500 次改动并不是她发起了 2500 次对话。用户反馈的问题散落在聊天工具、邮件和社交媒体上，以前要靠她自己去看，再转述给 AI。现在她让 Grok Bot 来盯这些渠道。Grok Bot 是 SpaceXAI 今年 8 月推出的产品，是能登录邮箱、聊天工具等各种应用、替人办事的 AI 智能体。它一发现新的问题反馈，就转给一个负责“协调”的 AI。这个协调者自己不写代码，只负责拆分任务、分派给其他 AI、盯进度，相当于她的后厨主管。

为什么不直接一个问题派一个 AI 去修？她说，一批反馈往往出自同一个根源，分开修会重复劳动，也看不出真正的毛病在哪，放在一起看才看得出来。她现在同时开着十多个这样的协调者，各管一摊。她一直在问自己一个问题：哪一步还卡在我身上，AI 为什么非得来问我？然后想办法教 AI 自己去拿到真实的信息。

她也说明，2500 次改动里新功能不占多数，很多是整理代码这类维护工作。

四、懂行的人更吃香，哪怕不会写代码

Matt 问，大家都靠 AI 了，专业知识是不是不值钱了？Lauren 的看法相反。模型越来越强，卡住人的已经变成你能不能把自己想要什么讲清楚。所以她认为，医生、律师这类在某个领域懂得很深的人，只要稍微懂一点技术、会用 AI 智能体，就能做出很好的产品。

两人都认为，技能没有什么神秘的，就是把自己的做事流程写成文字。Lauren 建议回头翻自己和 AI 的聊天记录，找出那些自己反复纠正、反复插手的地方，把它们写成技能或规矩。别人的技能可以拿来拼着用，但每个人最后都该有一套自己的，就像厨师换了餐厅也会带着自己的刀。

五、最后

很多人看完这期访谈会觉得，以后自己也可以像 Lauren 那样不 Review PR 了，装上她的 Skill，让模型帮忙验证一下就行。我自己现在的做法和她差不多，每天也有大量 PR，也不 Review。但我的建议是先别急着学她怎么做，先弄明白她凭什么能这么做。

1. 你能不能用上最好的模型，Token 够不够

在用上 Fable 和 Opus 5.5 之前，AI 写的代码我是不太放心的；用上之后，我才真的敢让 AI 去写而不怎么 Review。模型能力很重要，能力没到，就先别想这件事。

还有成本。像我这样没有大公司可以依靠的，得自己掏钱买 2 个 Claude Max 20x 账号，还得省着用。Lauren 在大公司，不用考虑 Token 消耗，全程用最好的模型、开最快的模式都没问题。

不过也别着急。Fable 这个级别的模型，也许半年以后就能像现在的 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 一样便宜，人人用得起。梁圣加油。

2. 不能完全依赖 AI 的验证

哪怕现在 GPT-6 操作电脑的水平已经超过真人了，让它去做验证，也只能替代一部分，不能真的全交给它，自己还是要看。

可以做的是把那些手动重复做的事情，一点点沉淀成 Skill 和自动化脚本，把体力活解放出去。

3. 方向得靠你自己的专业来指

再聪明的 AI，也没办法替你决定该往哪个方向走。就像给车子装上火箭发动机，也得你来告诉它往哪开，走偏了要及时调整，不然跑得再快也是南辕北辙。

做软件也一样。你不能指望一句提示词做出一个淘宝。你得先做一个能发商品、能浏览的小网站，再加上用户注册，还得区分买家和卖家，然后是支付和安全，功能做完了还要扛得住很多人同时用。稍微复杂一点的软件，都没法完全依赖 AI，要人去拆解、规划，分成一个个小版本、小里程碑，做完要验证，出现偏差要重新指方向。甚至做着做着，你自己的想法都变了，AI 不可能知道你真正想要的是什么。

所以就像播客里说的：模型越来越强，卡住人的已经变成你能不能把自己想要什么讲清楚。

4. 不一定要用他们的 Skill，但要学着把事情交给 Agent 去做

Matt 和 Lauren 的 Skill 都很受欢迎，但你不一定要用。

一方面，软件工程的基础知识，现在的模型已经学得很好了。Lauren 在播客里也说，去年的 Skill 还得写清楚具体该敲哪条命令，现在这些都可以删掉，只留流程步骤，Skill 会越写越短。

另一方面，他们的开发流程和环境，跟你的很可能不一样。Lauren 的 Skill 都是从她自己的工作里总结出来的：验证技能来自她当“人肉中转站”的那段日子；另一个叫 recall 的技能，来自她每次开新对话，都得把上一个对话里的背景再讲一遍。

所以更重要的是从你自己每天的开发流程出发。那些还要你手动操作的环节，尽可能交给 Agent 去做；Agent 做顺了，再把它的操作过程沉淀成 Skill，反复迭代优化。

如果不知道从哪里下手的话，可以参考 Lauren 的办法：翻自己和 AI 的聊天记录，找那些你反复纠正、反复插手的地方。这样迭代出来的 Skill 才真正适合你，用她的话说，每个厨师都该有一套自己的刀。

text:
The Most Degen Chain Becomes the Most Institutional Chain, Long live @solana 

Personally, I think @solana generated more buzz than any other protocol at this year’s KBW.

If I had to describe this KBW in one word, it would be “polarization.” Institutions and onchain perp traders were, in many ways, the two main characters of the week.

On one side, you had people in suits discussing regulation and financial infrastructure. On the other, you had traders literally operating their keyboards and mice with their toes while talking about leverage and PnL.

They’re basically the two opposite ends of the crypto spectrum.

And yet, what I found particularly interesting was that Solana managed to capture both extremes, not only through its products, but also through its presence and activities throughout KBW.

On the institutional side, Solana was working with the likes of Hanwha Asset Management, Shinhan Asset Management, Shinhan Bank, and Jeonbuk Bank on real financial use cases, including ETF tokenization and stablecoin remittance PoCs.

https://t.co/ohJFIfmXbI

On the degen side, they brought in @jadoodoo_  and basically took over the entire CT timeline for the week.

https://t.co/Zl3G9YZQhr

So at the same time, Solana is being recognized by institutions as an optimized venue for tokenization and payments, while being recognized by degens as one of the best chains to ape on.

I think that’s incredibly difficult to pull off.

Positioning yourself as a “general-purpose chain” can easily leave you stuck in the middle, not quite dominating any particular vertical.

But if you get it right, the upside is the exact opposite: you can bring virtually every sector of blockchain under a single ecosystem.

In that sense, I think Solana is currently showing us one of the best examples of what a successful general-purpose blockchain can look like.

Of course, none of this can be achieved by the chain alone.

It takes an ecosystem of partners actually building real use cases on top of the infrastructure and bridging completely different audiences from institutions to degens.

And I think much of what we saw during KBW was possible because of the work done by @SuperteamKorea and @SolanaFndn and the many other ecosystem partners behind the scenes.

text:
did Pumpfun pay out $15,000,000 to the right traders?

we announced Callout Rewards 2 months ago as part of our vision to make Pumpfun the most rewarding trading platform.

however, Callout Rewards V1 inadvertently rewarded the wrong behavior, which led to low quality spam & a reluctance to produce quality content

we later updated the reward algorithm to favor quality over quantity, meaning the more you callout each day, the more diminished your returns are, similarly to other social media platforms

I'm confident that we're heading in the right direction with each iteration, but as with any incentive program as lucrative as this, there's a lot of work we need to do to incentivize quality content that's scalable to the masses.

so far, we've rewarded everyone from the biggest accounts to accounts with <10 followers. no favoritism, no preferential treatment. completely equal opportunities for all.

the alpha is this: focus on calling out good tokens > traders begin to trust your callouts > they trade based on your confluence > you get rewarded for volume attributed to your callout

spamming callouts will not work. dumping on followers will not work.

the best time to start was 2 months ago. the next best time is now.

text:
Some reflections from four busy days at @Sibos:

✔️ There’s still a perception that getting privacy means running your own permissioned chain, cut off from the rest of the world. That’s no longer the case. With Tempo Zones, you can get privacy without giving up interoperability with the broader ecosystem.

✔️ There was a lot of discussion about interoperability between tokenized deposits and stablecoins. My takeaway is that I don’t think there’s enough urgency from banks yet. At the same time, I had many conversations with fintechs that are already using stablecoins to make their services faster and cheaper.

✔️ A year ago, we felt like the odd ducks at @tempo when we started working with banks on integrating ISO messaging with stablecoins. That feels much less odd now. ISO messaging gives financial institutions a practical path onchain. It simplifies integration while letting them maintain existing compliance standards. And it goes beyond payments: stocks, trade finance, and other workflows can follow the same path.

✔️ The range of capital markets use cases coming onchain was probably the most interesting part. Cross-border payments and card settlement seem to be emerging as consensus use cases, but the depth of what people are building across capital markets is much broader than I expected.

✔️ And the economics of stablecoins are changing quickly. A stablecoin sandwich used to add around 50 bps to a cross-border payment, which killed a lot of otherwise good use cases. With OUSD from @openstandard eliminating burn and mint fees, people are going back and revisiting business cases they had previously dismissed.

I’m sure I missed a few things. Looking forward to coming back to the next Sibos with real flows live.

text:
Major announcement in mathematical formalization!

Finally, after 3 months of very intensive, nonstop work by several AI agents (Codex and Claude Code), we have settled a classification of ALL 15,973 semigroups of order 6. Every one of the 15,969 that has a finite basis now has it written down explicitly, and the remaining 4 are proved to have none at all.

The whole list of bases is produced for the first time in history. Until now, for most of these semigroups, mathematicians only knew that a basis exists; nobody had ever written one down. The formalization in Lean, orchestrated with a multi-agent approach, reached more than 5 MILLION lines of verified Lean code, one of the largest auto-formalization projects to date. 

It's been an amazing joint work with @JanotaMikolas and @Jan_Hula, accompanied by senior experts in semigroup theory, João Araújo and Edmond W. H. Lee.

Our paper describing this project, "Proving at Scale for Universal Algebra", has been accepted at the MATH-AI workshop, NeurIPS 2026!

When we launched this project, we were a bit pessimistic: producing proofs for 15,973 semigroups seemed out of scope for the current technology. But with a careful setup (agents communicating through a mailbox we arranged, orchestrating the effort with a custom method of bootstrapping and auto-research), it has finally come to the finish line. The last 390 semigroups took 23 more days. The very last one needed a whole structural analysis before its proof could even be written.

text:
lauren（@poteto，简介写着 React Compiler 核心团队成员，曾在 Cursor、Meta、Netflix 工作）说，最近最常用的提示词之一是：“用你自己的话复述一下，你认为我的目标是什么、我要解决的问题是什么。”这条帖子有 1.1 万多次收藏。

原句是：restate in your own words what you think my goals are and what the problem i'm trying to solve is

lauren 在同一条线程里补了用法：先对着 AI 用语音聊上 10 分钟，再让它复述问题和你的目标。

作者更早写的 pstack（作者自己整理的一套 AI 编程工作流和技能包）指南里有个具体例子：有人在团队聊天工具 Slack 上报了问题，lauren 先让 agent（能自己读资料、改代码的 AI 助手）读完整个讨论串，用大白话复述底层问题是什么，然后才开始干活。作者说这样做有三个好处：

压缩。把一段嘈杂的对话整理成结构清楚的问题描述。

纠偏。agent 理解错了能马上看出来。如果它盯上了讨论里的一条无关线索，在写代码之前就能纠正。

不带偏。自己先不说假设和猜测，因为这些可能有错，也可能限制 agent 本来能做到的事。

作者把这叫“间接提示”：不把自己想要什么讲得很具体，而是先引导 agent 用自己的话讲出它理解的问题和目标。

我觉得这句话的价值在于便宜。多一轮对话，换来在动手之前对齐理解；不然可能要等它改了一堆文件，才发现理解有误。用 Claude Code、Codex 这类工具时，可以在让 AI 动手前先发这一句。

text:
绷哥观察｜宝拉，连接两个世界

这两天看宝拉，绷哥越来越觉得，有一个点值得拿出来好好讲讲。

持有宝拉，通过它的分配机制，能够获得泡泡玛特相关的RWA资产。

查到这会儿，已经累计有95次分配记录。这件事已经在发生，大家也有了可以看见的参与结果。

为什么绷哥觉得这个结合有意思？

先看看泡泡玛特。

大家喜欢一个小家伙，会去买、去收藏，摆在桌上，挂在包上，出门拍张照片，还要跟朋友分享。有人喜欢它的表情，有人喜欢它的故事，也有人就是看了一眼，觉得：这小东西怎么这么像我。

一个形象，就这样慢慢走进了很多人的生活。

你再看看Meme社区，是不是也有这种感觉？

大家围着一个形象做图、写故事、玩梗，把自己的情绪放进去。时间长了，它就有了性格，也有了一群认识它、愿意替它说话的人。

所以，潮玩和Meme，天然就有能聊到一起的地方。

泡泡玛特已经在现实世界里，把这种喜欢做成了一门生意。段永平后来也真金白银买入，2026年5月增持后成为它的第二大股东。不同的人，从不同的角度，开始认真看待这些小家伙背后的商业价值。

但对不少人来说，喜欢泡泡玛特很容易，参与港股却没那么方便。账户、渠道，都有门槛。

RWA就在这里，提供了一种新的连接方式。

宝拉用一个大家容易理解的形象，把人聚到社区里，再通过分配机制，让持有人接触到泡泡玛特相关的链上资产。

从喜欢一个角色，到参与一个社区，再到获得具体的资产分配，这几件事连起来了。

绷哥觉得，这个尝试挺好。

大家做内容、讲故事、让更多人认识宝拉；而持有这件事，也多了一个具体的理由。传播和资产之间，开始有了联系。

再往远一点想，泡泡玛特有那么多形象，谁会先火，谁能走出去，本来就带着偶然性。

可能是一张图，可能是一段故事，也可能是某个人把它带到了大家面前。很多时候，连创作者自己都没想到，大家会这么喜欢。

Web3也给了这些形象一个新的舞台。

如果宝拉能把这条路走通，就有机会让更多人注意到：原来潮玩来到链上，还能这样做社区，还能这样和现实资产连接。

一个宝拉出圈，也可能带动大家去认识更多形象，产生更多创作，吸引更多人参与进来。

这才是绷哥觉得值得继续观察的地方。

最后，再看X Layer正在做什么。

官方已经推出总额高达500万美元的RWA生态流动性激励计划，支持的方向里，就包括RWA与生态代币的交易对。这个方向，已经有了实际的生态投入。

宝拉正在做的，就是沿着这条路往前试。

现实世界里，大家把喜欢的小家伙带回家。

Web3世界里，大家围着它建设社区，也通过它接触现实资产。

两个世界，就这样有了一点新的联系。@bull_bnb @PolarCoinXlayer

text:
熊市还在努力营业的项目，只有两种：要么还想继续搞事情，要么还没“割”够，等风来。不管是哪一种，都值得关注。
反过来看，牛市里突然开始疯狂搞事情的项目，很多时候就是：发币 → 营销 → 收割 → 消失。
这次小晖晖参加韩国区块链周（KBW）以及大量周边活动，几个让我印象比较深的项目：
1、MemeCore $M
Meme公链 赛道｜市值约 24 亿美元｜FDV 约 105 亿美元｜流通约 22.8%
直接承包乐天世界，同时请来大量女团、男团、明星、DJ。
从品牌曝光、线下活动到娱乐化营销，预算明显不是小打小闹。

2、0G $0G
AI基础设施
这次 KBW 主会场最有存在感的项目之一，也是KBW 2026 最大赞助商之一，仅次于 Upbit 这种主办方级别的存在，现场曝光非常高。
除此之外，0G 在韩国还有大量周边活动。
这说明现在依然在持续投入：品牌 → 社区 → 开发者 → 韩国市场

3、Kite $KITE
AI 赛道｜约 3.9 亿美元市值｜FDV 约 15 亿美元｜流通约 25.6%
Kite AI 也是这次 KBW 期间比较活跃的项目之一。
除了主会场曝光，还办了多场有趣的周边活动。

4、Pudgy Penguins $PENGU
Meme赛道｜市值约 5.75 亿美元｜FDV 约 8.1 亿美元｜流通约 70.7%
胖企鹅这次在韩国的存在感也非常强，IP、社区、线下文化、消费场景。
各种周边活动都能看到它：匹克球、交易大赛、酒会等

5、RaveDAO $RAVE
音乐娱乐赛道｜市值约 0.52亿 万美元｜FDV 约 1.92 亿美元｜流通约 27%
基本上顶级活动周，都有RaveDAO 的身影。
这次，RaveDAO韩国活动的最大感受就是，活动规模明显比迪拜、新加坡小，场地没有那么夸张。

业界一直有这么一句话，“得韩国者、得天下”，韩国市场有一个非常明显的特点：疯狂 Fomo的本土用户、交易所上币效应、KOL、娱乐产业和Crypto的连接非常深等。
很多项目来到韩国，不只是为了办一场活动。
而是在争夺：韩国用户 + 韩国流量 + 韩国文化 + 韩国交易市场。
熊市最怕的不是价格跌，最怕项目连“营业”都懒得营业了。
所以小晖晖会特别关注那些：
币价跌了还在做产品，
 融资环境差了还在做生态，
 市场冷了还在办活动，
 甚至还在不断砸钱做品牌。

至于最后到底是“真想搞事情”，还是“还没割够”，时间会给答案。

text:
问了一下claude：有什么应该有软件解决方案、却没有人做的痛点/场景🤔 

- 照顾年迈父母的“家庭行政系统”：几个兄弟姐妹之间要协调父母的用药、复诊、医保报销、银行账户和水电缴费。现在大家靠微信群和记忆来维持，信息很散，责任也说不清。这件事刚需又高频，却没有一个好用的协作工具。

- 人去世后的“善后清单”：要注销账户、找出各种订阅和会员、处理社保公积金、变更房产车辆。流程又碎又折磨人，而家属正好在最没精力的时候。国外有零星创业公司在做，国内基本是空白。

- 个人资料“一次填写，到处授权”：办签证、入职、租房、孩子入学，同一套身份、学历、住址信息要反复手填、反复复印。如果有一个由个人自己掌控的资料库，按次授权给机构调用，能省掉大量重复劳动。难点在于政策和机构对接。

- 家庭物品档案：记录家里东西的购买凭证、保修到期日、说明书、召回通知和耗材型号（比如滤芯该买哪个）。现在都靠翻聊天记录和购物订单，没有人把它整合起来。

- 跨医院的病历自主携带：在国内换一家医院，检查往往要重做，过往病历也调不到。患者自己掌握一份完整、结构化的健康档案，价值很大，但卡在数据互通和监管上。

- 租房交接存证：入住和退租时，按房间逐项拍照录像，自动加上时间戳并生成双方确认的清单。押金纠纷绝大多数就是因为缺这份证据。

- 家长通知聚合：学校通知散落在班级群、钉钉、小程序和公众号里。可以自动提取其中的待办事项，比如交费、带材料、截止日期，再同步给夫妻双方。

- 自动续费总管：各平台的“连续包月”藏得很深，用户很难一眼看清自己每月被扣了多少钱、扣在哪里。需要一个工具能查看所有订阅，并一键取消。

- 老人防诈骗助手：对异常转账、陌生来电和下载可疑 App 发出预警，并通知家人。界面要按老人的使用习惯来设计，而不是做成监控工具。

- 装修隐蔽工程档案：记录水电管线的走向照片、防水范围、材料品牌和施工方。几年后要维修或打孔时，就不用靠猜。

- 慢病就诊摘要：把日常记录的症状、饮食、用药和睡眠整理成一页给医生看的摘要。门诊只有5分钟，患者往往说不清楚。

- 小区业主议事工具：用于维修基金使用、物业选聘这类事务的公开讨论和电子投票，并且保留合规的记录。现在业委会运作很不透明。

- 灵活就业者的财税社保一站式：自由职业者和零工要自己处理社保自缴、个税汇算和发票，规则复杂，也没有人帮忙提醒。

- 团队决策日志：自动从会议和聊天中抽取“我们决定了什么、为什么这么决定”，方便新人或半年后回查。会议纪要通常只记结论，不记理由。

- 宠物健康档案：疫苗、驱虫、过敏史和既往病历能在不同宠物医院之间带走。现在换一家医院基本就要从头问起。
author: antoniayly

text:
亲历三轮加密牛熊周期，我早已不再因单一币种的涨跌而轻易兴奋。 真正能让我为之触动的，是看见一种前所未有的事物，从无到有地破土而生。

BTC 第一次让互联网拥有了原生货币， ETH 第一次让互联网跑起了无需许可的金融机器。

这一轮市场都在寻找 AI、RWA、DePIN 之后的下一块叙事拼图， TapeOut 交出的答案却格外反直觉： 它想把 Token 变成生产原材料，把电路变成链上资产，把计算变成可交付的终端产品。

这是一条从未有人踏足的全新路径，探索的过程注定不会一帆风顺。 市场会有周期波动，产业会有磨合调整，所有创新的经济模型，也都需要在真实场景中持续迭代与验证。

但如果有一天，我们看见越来越多人采购 NAND，不是因为 NAND 会涨价； 制造 矿机，不是为了获取更多 BEM； 购买 矿机，也不是为了转手卖给下一个人； 而仅仅是因为—— 真的有人需要这份计算能力。

那一刻，TapeOut 才真正跨过了它最重要的那条界线： 从加密圈层内部的价值流转，走向一个有人生产、有人消费、有人真实付费的实体数字经济。

所以我此刻研究 TapeOut，真正押注的从来不是某一个币。 我在观察一场更宏大的实验： Token 除了代表钱、股权、债权和数字藏品之外，能不能第一次大规模成为「生产资料」？

如果答案最终是 Yes， 那么加密下一轮最大的故事，也许就不只是「发行什么资产」。 

而是： 我们终于开始用链，生产东西。

虽然 @Aptos 这轮周期确实很拉垮，但传出Aptos 6个月内要停链的言论就过分哗众取宠了。

Aptos 链上资金大撤退、链上TVL 暴跌， $APT 币价也是跌跌不休，但基于这样的基本面推导出Aptos 要停链的人非蠢即坏。

Aptos 是主权独立的L1 链而非L2，不能像 @blast 这样的L2 一样，官方把排序器停了就没法出块了。

L1 停链的难度要比L2 高出一个数量级，像Aptos 这样的PoS L1，要有超过1/3 的验证者下线无法达成共识出块才能停机。并不是项目方按下一个关机键就能把链关掉的。

拿Luna 死亡螺旋大崩盘的Terra 链为例，时至今日，Terra Classic 仍在持续出块。哪怕链上仅有100万美元的TVL。

text:
From the AI Agent narrative to an ecosystem with real revenue feedback. I think this is the most fitting way to describe $Agency

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

Agency has now reached a peak market cap of $24M. If we look at price alone, this is a typical AI Agent narrative-driven rally. But I think what is really worth examining is that the market is starting to reprice AgencyPad’s economic model, rather than simply chasing the AI Agent concept.

When I first researched Agency, my biggest question was: AgencyPad allows AI agents to conduct research, execute strategies, and manage funds autonomously, but what value do these activities ultimately bring to the platform token?

At the time, the platform already had a product and some activity, but its token value capture mechanism was unclear. Now, that has fundamentally changed.

I believe this rally has been driven by five main factors.

1. The tokenomics change is the most direct fundamental catalyst

This is what I consider the most important development.

Following AgencyPad’s economic model upgrade, 15% of the fees generated by eligible agents are used to periodically buy back and burn Agency. In other words, ecosystem activity no longer just generates platform revenue and resources for agents to operate. It now also creates direct buying pressure for the platform token.

This has changed market expectations.

Previously, growth in AgencyPad activity did not necessarily mean Agency would benefit. Now, as fee generation increases, the buyback amount could theoretically grow alongside it.

However, I don't think the market is pricing in the actual amount already burned.

What is really driving expectations is how many agents can consistently generate fees in the future, and whether this mechanism can create stronger buying pressure as the ecosystem expands.

There is a fundamental difference between the two: one is economic activity that has already happened, while the other is the market pricing in potential future growth.

2. AgencyPad is starting to produce genuinely revenue-generating runners

Even the best tokenomics mean little without real activity behind them.

This is another key development in the recent rally.

Agents on AgencyPad are starting to generate meaningful fees. In my earlier research, runners such as CLAUDIA, Aiden, and shoggoth had already demonstrated some revenue-generating ability. Individual agents generating tens of thousands of dollars in fees within a short period have shown the market that AgencyPad is not simply a platform for creating AI Memes with little ongoing activity.

The trading logic is straightforward: if the platform can consistently produce agents with trading volume, fee generation, and sustained activity, ecosystem revenue could evolve from occasional spikes into a more stable source of income.

More importantly, the market is no longer just betting on the success of one agent. It is betting on whether AgencyPad can repeatedly produce successful ones.

One runner performing well may just be a temporary trend. But if the platform can produce several revenue-generating runners at the same time, the market may begin to value the entire ecosystem differently.

However, fees are not the same as profit, nor are they equivalent to direct cash flow for the platform token. We still need to monitor whether these runners can sustain their revenue and whether their activity is driven by short-term trading hype.

3. WWW opened the door to attention, and Agency captured part of the capital rotation

Another important external factor behind this rally is WWW.

WWW attracted significant attention during the earlier AI Agent narrative, helping shift the market's focus from traditional Memes toward the AgencyPad ecosystem and related projects.

But once a narrative becomes widely discussed, capital naturally starts looking for other opportunities within the same space.

Agency was in a good position to benefit.

On one hand, it belongs to the same ecosystem and could capture some of the attention that had already formed. On the other hand, its own economic model was evolving, giving the market a new reason to pay attention.

This means Agency is not simply a token following a trend. It has the potential to become another independent trading opportunity within the ecosystem.

I don't think capital from WWW automatically flows into Agency. A more accurate way to look at it is that WWW helped open the door to attention for the broader narrative, while Agency attracted more interest through its own tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem activity.

This rally is the result of narrative expansion and capital rotation working together.

4. Actual buying from the market moved the rally beyond discussion and toward capital validation

Social media discussions can generate attention, but real buying activity can further shape market expectations. It shows that some market participants are no longer just discussing the project. They are willing to take on actual price risk.

This creates two effects.

First, it generates real spot demand and pushes the price higher.

Second, it creates a degree of social proof. When the market sees experienced traders building positions, more people start researching the same token, further expanding its visibility.

5. The team keeps shipping, preventing the narrative from losing momentum too quickly

AgencyPad's product narrative has moved beyond its original AI agent creation functionality.

From browser capabilities and research tools to Treasury actions, AI Influencers, and the buyback-and-burn mechanism, the team continues to expand what agents can do.

Not every update directly creates demand for the token, but continuous development gives the market new things to discuss and gradually reinforces the perception that AgencyPad is building a real product.

For a token that depends heavily on attention and expectations, continuous delivery helps extend the narrative cycle.

However, adding features is not the same as creating product value. Actual usage, user retention, and fee generation still need to validate the impact of these updates.

I believe the market is currently betting on two mutually reinforcing flywheels.

The first is the economic flywheel: more agent activity generates more fees; part of those fees is used to buy back and burn Agency; if the ecosystem continues to expand, the scale of buybacks could grow as well.

The second is the attention flywheel: projects such as WWW bring attention to the broader narrative, while Agency attracts capital through its own tokenomics improvements and runner performance. More capital and discussion then encourage the market to look for new opportunities within the AgencyPad ecosystem.

At the moment, the second flywheel is clearly moving faster.

The market has already started pricing in the potential scale of the ecosystem, but whether the economic flywheel can expand sustainably still needs to be proven over time.

This is what I see as the core tension surrounding Agency right now: expectations are growing faster than the economic value that has actually been realized.

As for the fundamentals, my assessment is that they have strengthened, particularly in two areas: token value capture and ecosystem activity.

Initially, AgencyPad had product capabilities but lacked a sufficiently clear mechanism for capturing value for its token. Now, the platform has established a buyback-and-burn mechanism and has runners that are actually generating fees.

This is not just narrative packaging. It represents real progress in both the economic model and ecosystem activity.

However, I would not say that the $24M valuation is fully supported by fundamentals yet.

There are still three key questions:

Can runners sustain their fee revenue rather than relying on short-term trading activity?
Can buyback-and-burn volume grow significantly alongside the ecosystem?
Can the platform consistently create new agents rather than relying on a handful of top-performing runners?

If these questions are gradually answered, the fundamentals will have a better chance of catching up with the current valuation.

What could drive the next leg higher?

The next things I plan to watch are developments and data that can materially change market expectations. I believe the next major catalysts could emerge from these areas.

First, more high-revenue runners emerge.

If AgencyPad can consistently produce multiple agents with sustainable fee revenue, the market may shift from trading individual runners to valuing the growth potential of the entire platform.

This would be the most important signal of ecosystem expansion.

Second, fees and buyback volume continue to grow.

The buyback-and-burn mechanism is already in place. The next key question is scale.

I will continue tracking actual buyback amounts, the number of tokens burned, and whether buyback frequency increases alongside ecosystem activity.

If fee growth turns out to be temporary, the mechanism will provide limited valuation support. On the other hand, if buyback volume continues to expand, the market may raise its long-term expectations for AGENCY.

Third, AgencyPad becomes a sustained narrative within the AI Agent ecosystem.

WWW has already demonstrated that the market has an appetite for this sector. If AgencyPad continues to launch agents that attract attention or introduces new ecosystem mechanics, attention could flow back into the platform.

However, these catalysts are highly uncertain. Ecosystem hype should not be equated with token value.

Fourth, the team continues delivering products that genuinely increase usage.

I care more about updates that drive real usage and revenue than simply adding more features.

If new capabilities help agents operate more consistently, improve task execution, or create new sources of fee revenue, they could become meaningful fundamental catalysts for the next leg higher.

Risks: The market may already be pricing in too much of the future

The biggest risk for Agency is not that it lacks fundamentals entirely, but that its current valuation may already reflect highly optimistic growth expectations.

1. A mismatch between valuation and fundamental progress

After climbing from a much lower market cap to $24M, the market has already reacted significantly to the tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem expansion narrative.

If runner numbers, fees, and buyback volume fail to keep growing, the market may reassess those expectations.

2. Runner revenue may not be sustainable

Agent fees are still largely tied to trading activity.

If the revenue of a few runners comes from short-lived trends, or if the platform cannot consistently reproduce successful cases, the ecosystem revenue we see today could be highly volatile.

3. Attention rotation can reverse quickly

The AI Agent narrative still depends heavily on market sentiment.

When new trends emerge, capital may leave the AgencyPad ecosystem. Even if the product continues operating, the token may not be able to maintain its previous valuation.

4. A working mechanism does not automatically establish long-term value

Buybacks and burns can create buying pressure and reduce token supply, but they do not automatically generate sustainable business growth.

Ultimately, AgencyPad still needs to establish consistent activity, revenue, and user demand.

From here, I see two possible scenarios for the next phase of the market.

If runner numbers continue increasing, fees remain strong, buyback-and-burn volume expands, and market attention does not fade significantly, the rally could still be in the expectation-building phase of ecosystem expansion, leaving room for further valuation re-rating.

But if the price keeps rising while fees and buyback data stagnate, and the rally becomes increasingly dependent on KOL discussions and capital rotation, then it would look more like sentiment-driven valuation expansion. Once attention cools, the risk of a sharp pullback would increase.

For that reason, I would rather wait for further fundamental validation than simply chase a market cap breakout.

The three things I will focus on next are:

Whether AgencyPad continues producing new high-revenue runners.

Whether actual Agency buyback-and-burn volume grows alongside ecosystem activity.

Whether capital and attention remain concentrated in AgencyPad instead of quickly rotating into the next AI Agent trend.

The core change in Agency is that it is evolving from an AI Agent token with a product concept into a project with an initial economic feedback mechanism and real ecosystem activity.

That makes it much more interesting than when I first researched it.

But from a trading perspective, what will truly determine its next phase is not the tokenomics upgrade that has already happened, but whether the growth the market is expecting can continue to materialize.

What I am trading from here is whether AgencyPad can turn this mechanism into a continuously operating ecosystem.

The core catalyst behind $Agency sudden surge is the launch of a new fee-based buyback-and-burn mechanism announced by the official team

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

This change has prompted the market to reassess Agency value-capture potential and has given its existing AI Agent narrative a more clearly defined economic logic.

Our previous analysis concluded that the market had primarily been betting on whether the autonomous financial agent model could work and whether it could generate sustained trading activity and capital flows.

However, the latest announcement adds a new layer to that narrative: Agents can not only manage funds and make investments, but also convert a portion of the fees generated by their respective tokens into buying pressure for Agency, with all purchased tokens subsequently burned on-chain.

According to the rules announced by the team, 15% of the fees generated by each token on the platform will be used to buy Agency every hour, and all purchased tokens will be burned on-chain. The remaining fees will be used to keep Agents running and support their investment activities.

This mechanism connects ecosystem activity directly to the platform token. Trading activity across the platform generates fees, part of those fees creates buying pressure for Agency, and the purchased tokens are burned. Previously, the market was focused on whether AGENCY could enable AI to manage funds autonomously, develop strategies, and execute on-chain operations. Now, the market has another metric to watch: whether these autonomous economic activities can consistently generate real demand for AGENCY.

This is also the most direct catalyst behind the latest surge. Compared with simply adding another AI feature, a buyback-and-burn mechanism is easier for traders to understand and gives the token a new reference point for expectations. However, the 15% refers to the proportion of fees allocated, not 15% of the platform’s total trading volume. The actual buyback volume still depends on fee revenue, the number of active projects, and whether the mechanism is consistently executed.

From a product perspective, AGENCY’s core concept has not fundamentally changed. It still revolves around autonomous financial Agents. Each token has its own AI mind and treasury. Agents can observe the market, set missions, and execute investments or buybacks, while remaining subject to code-enforced rules and permission controls. Unlike ordinary AI tools, AGENCY does not simply provide recommendations. Its AI can carry out real on-chain economic activities within predefined limits.

The significance of this update is that it adds a platform-level value-recycling mechanism on top of the existing autonomous execution capabilities. If more Agents remain active and generate real trading activity and fees, the platform could develop a cycle in which ecosystem activity generates fees, those fees support Agent operations and investments, and part of them provides buyback funds for Agency. Whether this cycle can actually take shape will determine whether AGENCY has the potential to evolve from a novel AI product into a platform with sustained economic activity.

The website also presents several ecosystem metrics worth watching. At the time of the screenshot, it showed 61 Minds currently thinking, approximately $110,890 in cumulative fees, 162 live programs, and 814 creations that day. It also displayed 188 coins. These figures indicate that the platform has already reached a certain level of product activity, but they cannot be directly equated with recurring revenue or high-quality user growth.

In particular, the number of creations mainly reflects activity at the platform’s entry point. What really matters is whether these tokens can continue trading after launch, generate fees, and support the long-term operation of their corresponding Agents. If a large number of projects quickly lose trading activity, even high creation numbers will struggle to sustain consistent buyback demand.

The market may therefore be betting on three main developments.

First, improved token value capture. Previously, the relationship between AGENCY’s product capabilities and its native token was relatively indirect. Now, a portion of ecosystem fees is explicitly allocated to buying and burning Agency. The market can directly observe whether this mechanism generates actual buying pressure.

Second, ecosystem scalability. If active Agents, the number of tokens with sustained trading activity, and platform fee revenue all grow together, buybacks and burns could expand alongside the ecosystem. The market is not simply betting on the number of newly created tokens, but on the platform’s ability to turn new projects into sustained activity.

Finally, increased attention toward the autonomous financial Agent sector. AGENCY combines AI decision-making with real capital operations. Different Agents can act according to their own objectives and rules, and those actions themselves could become material for social distribution. If representative investment or treasury-management cases emerge, the platform may attract attention beyond the broader AI narrative.

However, sector-wide enthusiasm does not automatically translate into a competitive advantage for the platform. Autonomous financial Agents have considerable potential, but whether AGENCY can consistently attract creators, retain users, and build a product experience that is difficult to replicate still needs to be demonstrated through real data.

From a fundamental perspective, this update strengthens AGENCY’s mechanism design and token value-capture logic, but it is too early to conclude that the platform’s profitability has improved at the same time.

On the one hand, fee-based buybacks and burns introduce a clearer source of demand for the token. On the other hand, it remains uncertain whether the platform has enough sustained trading activity to support meaningful buybacks. Fee revenue is also not the same as net profit. Agent operating costs, capital allocation, and fee distribution all affect the platform’s actual economic performance.

Furthermore, buybacks and burns can only change the supply side. They cannot independently create long-term demand. Even if tokens continue to be burned, the price impact may remain limited if buybacks are small relative to the circulating market cap or if selling pressure outweighs the buying activity.

The latest surge may also contain a significant short-term speculative component. The expectations created by the new mechanism could attract capital that was already interested in the AI Agent narrative, as well as short-term traders looking for buyback-and-burn catalysts. These two groups may have very different holding periods. Therefore, increased trading volume and a rapid price rise do not, by themselves, prove that long-term capital has developed lasting confidence in the project.

Going forward, AGENCY’s development will depend primarily on several key variables.

First, whether buybacks and burns can reach meaningful scale. The team has officially announced the mechanism. The next step is to monitor its actual execution records, including hourly buyback amounts, cumulative purchases, tokens burned, and buyback volume relative to trading volume and market cap. If buybacks continue to grow, the market may have a basis for reassessing Agency based on real capital flows. If the actual amounts remain limited, the expectations created by this upgrade may gradually fade.

Second, whether the platform can turn token creation into sustained revenue. The number of newly created tokens is only the starting point for ecosystem growth. More important are project retention, sustained trading activity, and whether Agents can continue operating with the support of fee revenue. Only if these metrics improve can the platform establish stable economic activity rather than relying on a constant stream of new projects to maintain the appearance of growth.

Third, whether AGENCY can produce autonomous investment cases with strong distribution potential. AGENCY’s differentiation lies in enabling AI to execute real capital operations under predefined rules. If representative treasury-management, investment, or risk-control cases emerge, they could both demonstrate product capabilities and attract more developers and users. However, a single successful trade cannot prove that an Agent has long-term investment consistency. Repeatability and risk management matter just as much.

Fourth, whether the platform can evolve from a token launchpad into infrastructure for autonomous financial Agents. If AGENCY can continue attracting creators and establish stable cycles of Agent operations, treasury management, and fee generation, its long-term positioning could extend beyond that of a single AI token launch platform. This would create a larger potential valuation narrative, but it would also require continuous product development, user retention, and sustained economic activity.

Alongside these growth opportunities, several risks should not be overlooked.

First, ecosystem fee revenue may not grow consistently. Tokens launched on the platform tend to have strong speculative characteristics. If trading activity declines, fee revenue and buyback funds may fall accordingly. Second, Agent operations and investment activities involve risks related to fund security, program execution, and strategy decisions. Even with permission controls and independent signing mechanisms, software vulnerabilities and execution failures cannot be completely ruled out. Finally, high short-term trading activity may amplify price volatility. When large amounts of capital concentrate around a new mechanism, the token may face significant pullback pressure once the catalyst has been fully priced in.

Therefore, the most useful data to monitor going forward is not any single price or trading-volume metric, but a set of indicators that can be cross-checked against one another: daily fees, actual buyback amounts, tokens burned, active Agent counts, 7-day and 30-day project retention, holder concentration, and large capital flows.

Among these, the relationship between fee growth and buyback volume is particularly important. If platform activity continues to increase but buyback amounts do not grow accordingly, it suggests that ecosystem expansion has not yet translated into meaningful token demand. Conversely, if fees, buybacks, and burns all grow consistently while the market also maintains demand independent of the buyback mechanism, then Agency’s value-capture logic will have stronger evidence behind it.

Overall, this surge reflects more than market enthusiasm for the AI Agent concept. It represents a reassessment of AGENCY’s economic model. The newly announced buyback-and-burn mechanism creates a more direct connection between the native token and platform activity. This is the clearest fundamental development in the current situation.

However, there is still a significant gap between a more complete mechanism and a mature business model. What can currently be confirmed is that AGENCY has introduced a potential new path for value to flow back to the token. What remains uncertain is whether this path can generate substantial capital flows and whether the platform can consistently expand real usage demand.

AGENCY’s core investment thesis is whether the autonomous economic activities of AI Agents can generate platform activity at scale and convert that activity into actual demand for Agency through sustained fee-based buybacks and burns.

If future data shows that this cycle is taking shape, the latest surge could mark the beginning of a broader market reassessment of AGENCY. If buyback volumes remain limited, project retention is weak, or ecosystem activity depends primarily on short-term speculation, the current rally may instead reflect expectations being priced in ahead of actual fundamental growth.

The significance of this update is that it adds a platform-level value-recycling mechanism on top of the existing autonomous execution capabilities. If more Agents remain active and generate real trading activity and fees, the platform could develop a cycle in which ecosystem activity generates fees, those fees support Agent operations and investments, and part of them provides buyback funds for Agency. Whether this cycle can actually take shape will determine whether AGENCY has the potential to evolve from a novel AI product into a platform with sustained economic activity.

The website also presents several ecosystem metrics worth watching. At the time of the screenshot, it showed 61 Minds currently thinking, approximately $110,890 in cumulative fees, 162 live programs, and 814 creations that day. It also displayed 188 coins. These figures indicate that the platform has already reached a certain level of product activity, but they cannot be directly equated with recurring revenue or high-quality user growth.

In particular, the number of creations mainly reflects activity at the platform’s entry point. What really matters is whether these tokens can continue trading after launch, generate fees, and support the long-term operation of their corresponding Agents. If a large number of projects quickly lose trading activity, even high creation numbers will struggle to sustain consistent buyback demand.

The market may therefore be betting on three main developments.

First, improved token value capture. Previously, the relationship between AGENCY’s product capabilities and its native token was relatively indirect. Now, a portion of ecosystem fees is explicitly allocated to buying and burning Agency. The market can directly observe whether this mechanism generates actual buying pressure.

Second, ecosystem scalability. If active Agents, the number of tokens with sustained trading activity, and platform fee revenue all grow together, buybacks and burns could expand alongside the ecosystem. The market is not simply betting on the number of newly created tokens, but on the platform’s ability to turn new projects into sustained activity.

Finally, increased attention toward the autonomous financial Agent sector. AGENCY combines AI decision-making with real capital operations. Different Agents can act according to their own objectives and rules, and those actions themselves could become material for social distribution. If representative investment or treasury-management cases emerge, the platform may attract attention beyond the broader AI narrative.

However, sector-wide enthusiasm does not automatically translate into a competitive advantage for the platform. Autonomous financial Agents have considerable potential, but whether AGENCY can consistently attract creators, retain users, and build a product experience that is difficult to replicate still needs to be demonstrated through real data.

From a fundamental perspective, this update strengthens AGENCY’s mechanism design and token value-capture logic, but it is too early to conclude that the platform’s profitability has improved at the same time.

On the one hand, fee-based buybacks and burns introduce a clearer source of demand for the token. On the other hand, it remains uncertain whether the platform has enough sustained trading activity to support meaningful buybacks. Fee revenue is also not the same as net profit. Agent operating costs, capital allocation, and fee distribution all affect the platform’s actual economic performance.

Furthermore, buybacks and burns can only change the supply side. They cannot independently create long-term demand. Even if tokens continue to be burned, the price impact may remain limited if buybacks are small relative to the circulating market cap or if selling pressure outweighs the buying activity.

The latest surge may also contain a significant short-term speculative component. The expectations created by the new mechanism could attract capital that was already interested in the AI Agent narrative, as well as short-term traders looking for buyback-and-burn catalysts. These two groups may have very different holding periods. Therefore, increased trading volume and a rapid price rise do not, by themselves, prove that long-term capital has developed lasting confidence in the project.

Going forward, AGENCY’s development will depend primarily on several key variables.

First, whether buybacks and burns can reach meaningful scale. The team has officially announced the mechanism. The next step is to monitor its actual execution records, including hourly buyback amounts, cumulative purchases, tokens burned, and buyback volume relative to trading volume and market cap. If buybacks continue to grow, the market may have a basis for reassessing Agency based on real capital flows. If the actual amounts remain limited, the expectations created by this upgrade may gradually fade.

Second, whether the platform can turn token creation into sustained revenue. The number of newly created tokens is only the starting point for ecosystem growth. More important are project retention, sustained trading activity, and whether Agents can continue operating with the support of fee revenue. Only if these metrics improve can the platform establish stable economic activity rather than relying on a constant stream of new projects to maintain the appearance of growth.

Third, whether AGENCY can produce autonomous investment cases with strong distribution potential. AGENCY’s differentiation lies in enabling AI to execute real capital operations under predefined rules. If representative treasury-management, investment, or risk-control cases emerge, they could both demonstrate product capabilities and attract more developers and users. However, a single successful trade cannot prove that an Agent has long-term investment consistency. Repeatability and risk management matter just as much.

Fourth, whether the platform can evolve from a token launchpad into infrastructure for autonomous financial Agents. If AGENCY can continue attracting creators and establish stable cycles of Agent operations, treasury management, and fee generation, its long-term positioning could extend beyond that of a single AI token launch platform. This would create a larger potential valuation narrative, but it would also require continuous product development, user retention, and sustained economic activity.

Alongside these growth opportunities, several risks should not be overlooked.

First, ecosystem fee revenue may not grow consistently. Tokens launched on the platform tend to have strong speculative characteristics. If trading activity declines, fee revenue and buyback funds may fall accordingly. Second, Agent operations and investment activities involve risks related to fund security, program execution, and strategy decisions. Even with permission controls and independent signing mechanisms, software vulnerabilities and execution failures cannot be completely ruled out. Finally, high short-term trading activity may amplify price volatility. When large amounts of capital concentrate around a new mechanism, the token may face significant pullback pressure once the catalyst has been fully priced in.

Therefore, the most useful data to monitor going forward is not any single price or trading-volume metric, but a set of indicators that can be cross-checked against one another: daily fees, actual buyback amounts, tokens burned, active Agent counts, 7-day and 30-day project retention, holder concentration, and large capital flows.

Among these, the relationship between fee growth and buyback volume is particularly important. If platform activity continues to increase but buyback amounts do not grow accordingly, it suggests that ecosystem expansion has not yet translated into meaningful token demand. Conversely, if fees, buybacks, and burns all grow consistently while the market also maintains demand independent of the buyback mechanism, then Agency’s value-capture logic will have stronger evidence behind it.

Overall, this surge reflects more than market enthusiasm for the AI Agent concept. It represents a reassessment of AGENCY’s economic model. The newly announced buyback-and-burn mechanism creates a more direct connection between the native token and platform activity. This is the clearest fundamental development in the current situation.

However, there is still a significant gap between a more complete mechanism and a mature business model. What can currently be confirmed is that AGENCY has introduced a potential new path for value to flow back to the token. What remains uncertain is whether this path can generate substantial capital flows and whether the platform can consistently expand real usage demand.

AGENCY’s core investment thesis is whether the autonomous economic activities of AI Agents can generate platform activity at scale and convert that activity into actual demand for Agency through sustained fee-based buybacks and burns.

If future data shows that this cycle is taking shape, the latest surge could mark the beginning of a broader market reassessment of AGENCY. If buyback volumes remain limited, project retention is weak, or ecosystem activity depends primarily on short-term speculation, the current rally may instead reflect expectations being priced in ahead of actual fundamental growth.

Let's discuss $Agency. In essence, this project shares a highly similar core narrative with $WWW.

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

Both are attempting to transform tokens from passive trading assets into economic entities with independent AI minds, funds, and autonomous action capabilities.

However, their product directions differ. WWW focuses on autonomous AI browsing, exploration, memory, and content generation, while AGENCY focuses on AI fund management, decision-making, and on-chain execution.

WWW's innovation lies in giving every newly launched token its own independent AI mind and computing treasury. Creator fees generated by trading are used to pay for model inference and cloud browser operating costs. When funds are sufficient, the AI can automatically wake up, browse the web, record discoveries, and retain memories. 

When funds run low, it goes dormant. This makes trading activity directly influence whether the AI can continue operating. Its core value proposition is to build an autonomous exploration network composed of different AI minds.

AGENCY builds on a similar mechanism but adds fund management and execution capabilities. Each token has its own AI and treasury. The AI can monitor markets, read holdings, conduct research, and execute buybacks, burns, rewards, locks, tasks, and other operations within predefined rules. 

Its fee distribution mechanism allocates more funds to the token's treasury as cumulative fees increase, allowing the AI not only to keep thinking but also to accumulate funds and take action.

From a product presentation and distribution perspective, AGENCY's behavior may be easier for traders to understand. WWW showcases AI browsing websites, searching for information, and compiling research notes. 

These activities have sharing potential but do not necessarily demonstrate direct economic outcomes. AGENCY's buybacks, rewards, and on-chain operations, by contrast, can generate more tangible events and on-chain records, showing the market that AI is actively using funds to take action.

This could be one reason behind the short-term performance difference between the two projects. WWW's core story is about how AI can continue to exist, while AGENCY goes a step further by demonstrating how AI can use funds to act. 

The latter offers the market a new dimension of potential and may attract some early attention from traders rotating out of WWW or similar projects.

However, on-chain activity does not automatically create economic value. Buybacks, rewards, and tasks can attract short-term attention, but they do not necessarily generate sustained demand. Although AGENCY has a more extensive fund execution mechanism, platform revenue and value capture by the native AGENCY token must still be evaluated separately. 

Each token's treasury primarily serves its own AI and token economy. The fact that the platform earns a share of fees does not mean that holders of the native AGENCY token necessarily receive those benefits.

From a market-cycle perspective, AGENCY has been live for a relatively short time, so its early narrative and trading momentum may not have faded yet. New projects typically benefit from greater novelty, while their communities actively explain and promote the mechanics. 

Early traders may also participate in a concentrated manner, helping sustain short-term price performance. By comparison, WWW has already undergone an initial phase of narrative-driven valuation. 

The market is beginning to shift from pricing its initial innovation toward evaluating actual usage, activity, and token value capture. When subsequent data fails to meet initial expectations quickly enough, early capital may take profits or rotate into other projects.

Therefore, AGENCY's ability to maintain a market cap of around $2 million may be related to its narrative freshness, the visibility of its action mechanisms, early trading activity, and holder distribution. 

But this does not mean it already has stronger fundamentals. Market cap is simply the token price multiplied by circulating supply; 

it does not represent an equivalent amount of capital actually invested. Maintaining a certain market cap over a short period also does not prove that the token has established strong underlying support.

The key validation points for the two projects are also different going forward. WWW needs to prove that its AI can consistently produce valuable research, attract external users who return repeatedly, and encourage developers to actually use its API. 

More important than the number of newly launched tokens are the number of active minds, average operating time, research quality, treasury income relative to computing costs, and user retention.

AGENCY, meanwhile, needs to demonstrate that AI fund management and on-chain actions can generate real value. Key indicators include whether market cap and liquidity remain stable after trading activity cools, whether AI can consistently execute rational and effective financial operations, and whether those actions generate genuine user demand rather than relying on frequent buybacks or rewards to maintain short-term attention.

Both projects face the same fundamental issue: ecosystem growth does not necessarily translate into value capture by the native token. Each WWW mind has its own treasury, and trading fees primarily fund its own operations. Although AGENCY receives a share of platform fees, whether its native token can capture direct economic value from ecosystem expansion still requires a clearly defined mechanism and verifiable data.

My view is that WWW was among the first to combine autonomous AI browsing, artificial life, and the Meme economy, establishing early recognition for the Living Tokens narrative. AGENCY builds on a similar narrative but emphasizes AI fund management and real-world actions. This may make it more attractive to the market's short-term attention. It could help explain why AGENCY can maintain a market cap of around $2 million while WWW is pulling back, but it does not establish that AGENCY has greater long-term value.

Going forward, the most important things to monitor are AGENCY's price and liquidity behavior as trading volume declines, whether its AI begins producing meaningful on-chain actions, and whether WWW continues to grow its active minds and external usage.

WWW shows the market how AI can continue to exist, while AGENCY shows how AI can use funds to take action. The long-term potential of both ultimately depends on proving that autonomous behavior has genuine utility, establishing a sustainable economic cycle, and translating that demand into value for their respective native tokens.

text:
新兴RL环境类公司，2年多即做到8位数盈利

除了之前讲过的给AI/机器人公司提供专家数据，或模拟数据（如之前介绍过的4Dlabs @4Dlabs_Official 和 Axis Robotics
@axisrobotics），还有一类RL环境类公司（下面的图是目前这类公司的市场地图），你说他是数据公司也好，RL环境公司也对。因为核心都是给头部实验室提供训练数据和训练环境的。

这类公司在美国市场现金流都不错。今天又看到一家，公司只有不到10个人，但已经做到盈利。他最开始做的RL环境是之前不好量化的金融知识工作环境。

Halluminate 做的是金融知识工作的「考场 + 训练场」

公开互联网语料和代码题已经很难再把模型往前推一截。

投行、PE 那种活又长、又依赖判断、又很难自动打分：扫邮件、翻 data room、建模型、改合同、出 pitch、跟到交割。他们的做法是先用真实交易改编出一套很难的卷子，看前沿模型在哪翻车，再把这些失败模式做成可重置、有可验证奖励的强化学习环境，

卖给模型实验室做 post-training。

特点大致是这几条：

垂直，而且是金融优先。

自称 verticalized data research lab。第一站是金融服务，后面才扩咨询、保险、运营。

逻辑是：教 agent 做银行/PE 尽调，和教它写代码不是同一类环境。

先卖卷子，再卖补习班。Westworld Finance Diligence Bench 是公开基准：88 个任务，来自匿名化的真实私募交易，由从业交易人员写和审。智能体在动态桌面里走完整并购尽调，轨迹可以到几百步。

7 个前沿模型最高平均分大约只有 51%。卷子证明缺口，环境用来补缺口，客户主要是实验室，不是买方自己。

长周期、可验证，不是单轮问答。环境里要扫收件箱、拼 data room、建模型、出交付物，奖励由 agentic、离散、二元验证器混合打。

这比「答对一道题」更接近真实工作，也比在真网站上训 agent 更安全、可并行、可复现。

商业上极瘦身。约 9 人，2024 年成立，YC S25。A 轮 3000 万美元、Oak HC/FT 领投，累计 3850 万美元。公司称美国前五大闭源实验室里有四家是付费客户，年化收入到八位数中段且盈利。Anthropic、OpenAI、Meta 研究员个人跟投。

PNUT을 시작으로 밈코인이 크게 떴었는데 하루종일 밈코인만 했었음. 3개월 정도 하다가 겨우 한 2-3개 크게 먹어서 통산 10K 정도 수익이었던 듯. 소액으로 여러개 참여하는 식으로 했던 것 같음.

5. 야핑 (+$40K)
대야핑시대에 이만한 꿀통이 없었음. 물론 약 6개월 정도 24시간 야핑만 했지만 그만한 가치가 있었다. 다양하게 벌었지만 바운드리스로 특히 많이 벌었음 16K 정도

6. 바운드리스 노드작 (+$10K)
바운드리스 노드작 외주(?)로 맡겼음.수익의 30%가 수수료였는데 그래도 꽤 많이 남아서 만족함. 바운드리스가 잘 될거라는 확신이 있어서 좀 과감하게 다양하게 투자함. 업빗썸 펌핑도 잘 나와서 크게 먹은 듯.

7. 팔콘 세일/따리 (+$10K)
$FF 세일도 참여했고, 추가로 매수해서 따리 참여했는데 업빗썸 펌핑이 매우 잘 나와서 10K 정도 수익 났던 듯. 거의 한 10배 펌핑이었던 걸로 기억하는데, 상승장에선 따리 기대값이 진짜 개꿀이었음.

8. 라이터 에드 (+$10K)
그렇게 막 열심히 참여하진 않았고 초기에 한 500달러 정도 엣지엑스랑 양빵으로 태운게 대박나서 10K 정도 수익이 났음. 마곤님 글 보고 했었는데 감사합니다. 좀 더 태울 걸;;

9. 디파이앱 게임 꿀통 (+$5K)
디파이앱에서 새로 게임이 나왔었는데 이게 기댓값이 개꿀이었음. 그냥 계속 게임하면 돈복사. 바이브코딩으로 자동사냥 만들어서 한 일주일 정도 조졌는데 5K 정도 수익이 났음. 동타니가 알려준 꿀통 (동타니 채널에도 올렸었음 ㄷㄷ)

10. 캐시캣 (+$20K)
5M 정도 평단으로 500달러치 정도 샀음. 다양한 밈코를 봐온 경험으로 잘 될 요소가 너무 많아서 과감한 투자를 했음 (평소 밈코 100달러치밖에 안사는데 5배를 산거임) 100-200M은 쉽게 갈 재료라고 보고 180M쯤 다 매도한듯.

11. 마스코인 (+$5K)
200K에 샀는데 20M쯤 다 팔았었음. 잘 팔았다고 생각했는데 200M 가는거 보고 눈물 개흘림. 100배를 먹었으나 금액이 좀 작아서 큰 수익까진 아니었음. 이렇게 큰 두개 말고 나머지 밈코들은 다 플마해서 사실상 수익 없었던 듯.

느낀 점
생각해보면 큼직한 기회들은 거의 다 챙긴 것 같긴한데, 위험 관리하느라 그렇게 큰 수익을 얻지도 못한 것 같음. 그래서 오래 살아남았나 싶기도하지만 부자되려면 좀 더 확신을 가지고 크게 때리기도 해봐야할 것 같음. 이번 상승장에서는 반드시 졸업하고 말 것.

text:
浅谈无监督学习模型应用在量化交易中的「坑」

许多量化新手容易被PCA（主成分分析）、聚类（K-Means）等无监督学习方法吸引，因为它们看似能自动从市场数据中挖掘隐藏模式、降低维度，甚至创造超额收益。然而，这些方法在实际应用中存在一些不易察觉的风险，若不加以警惕，很容易导致模型在回测中表现出色、实盘中却悄然失效

无监督学习 vs 有监督学习：本质差异与潜在风险

无监督学习（如 PCA / K-Means）
1. 你学到的是什么？ → 数据当下的内部结构（例如相关性、分群结果）
2. 新数据进来时怎么办？ → 你必须用这个「旧结构」去理解新数据。若市场结构已变，你的理解框架就可能过时

关键在于：无监督学习试图捕捉「世界当前长什么样」，但金融市场是持续变动的，这个「样子」并不恒定

有监督学习（如 SVM / XGBoost）
1. 你学到的是什么？ → 从特征（X）到目标（y）之间的映射规则
2. 新数据进来时怎么办？ → 你沿用同一套规则，从新特征预测新目标

关键在于：有监督学习试图学习「当世界呈现某种状态时，结果会如何」的规律，规则本身固定，但其适用性仍取决于市场状态是否持续符合训练时的分布

为什么无监督学习的「坑」更隐蔽？
有监督学习的失效往往表现为预测准确率下降，讯号相对明显；而无监督学习的失效则更为隐蔽：

1. 结构漂移不易察觉
PCA 降维后的主成分、K-Means 的分群中心，都是基于历史数据的静态快照。当市场进入不同阶段（如牛市转熊市、波动机制改变），这些结构可能已无法代表当前市场，但模型不会主动报错，只会继续输出看似合理、实则误导的特征或分组

2. 从结构到交易信号的逻辑断层
这是将无监督学习用于交易的根本性挑战。假设K-Means将股票分成5个群组，哪一组该做多？哪一组该做空？ 或者，PCA第一主成分得分高的股票，未来是涨还是跌？ 这个「从结构到交易信号」的映射，通常需要透过在样本内进行事后分析来确定（例如，回看发现「群组3」在过去平均收益最高，所以未来就做多「群组3」）。这一步引入了巨大的过拟合风险，相当于用样本内数据为无监督结果「贴上了一个脆弱的预测标签」

3. 缺乏明确的监控指标
没有像分类准确率或回归误差那样直观的指标来判断无监督模型是否已经「失准」。你只能透过下游任务（如策略收益）的恶化间接推测，而此时损失可能已经发生

4. 时间序列中的资料泄漏风险
若不小心在整个时间序列上一次性拟合无监督模型（例如用全部历史数据计算 PCA 主成分），等于让模型偷看了「未来资讯」。这会使回测结果过度乐观，却在实盘中因无法取得未来结构而表现崩溃

如何降低无监督学习的应用风险？

1. 滚动更新与定期重训
以滑动窗口的方式定期重新拟合无监督模型，确保其结构捕捉的是最近期的市场状态

2. 设计稳定性检验指标
例如监控主成分方向的变化、分群结果的一致性，设定阈值以触发模型重新训练

3. 避免全域拟合，严格区分样本内外
在时间序列中必须严格按时间顺序划分训练与测试数据，禁止使用未来数据拟合无监督转换。对于上述「信号逻辑断层」的风险，对策是必须将「结构发现」和「信号生成」两个阶段严格在样本外分开。例如，用2010-2015年数据发现结构（分群），然后用2016-2017年数据来观察各群组的表现，独立地确定交易规则，最后再用2018年后的数据进行策略测试

4. 理解你提取的是什么，而非盲目使用
理解每个主成分、每个群集的经济或市场含义，并观察其解释力是否随时间延续

补充一个具体的「坑」：PCA用于因子合成的静态权重陷阱

场景：用PCA从一堆相关性很高的技术指标（如不同周期的动量、波动率）中合成一个「综合动量因子」。
坑：PCA给出的权重是固定不变的，它基于历史协方差矩阵最大化解释变异。但在市场不同阶段（如趋势市 vs. 震荡市），不同周期动量的有效性会变化。静态权重无法适应这种变化，可能在趋势市结束时，仍然给长周期动量过高的权重，导致因子失效。
进阶思路：可以考虑引入动态因子模型（DFM）或状态空间模型，允许因子载荷（权重）随时间演化

无监督学习是强大的探索性工具，能够帮助我们从高维市场数据中提取结构、发现模式。然而，在量化交易这样一个动态环境中，必须警惕其「静态拟合、动态失效」的潜在风险。真正的关键不在于完全避免使用这些方法，而在于清楚识别其限制、建立监控机制，并将其置于不断适应市场变化的框架之中。唯有如此，无监督学习才能从一个看似自动化的「黑盒子」，转化为可靠且透明的策略组成部分

text:
Ethereum's validator exit queue just hit its highest level of 2026, and I think it's one of the better stress tests we've had.

By 2 October, about 850,000 ETH was waiting to leave the validator set, according to Validator Queue data from https://t.co/Wwt9NipaKV.

The estimated wait to exit was close to 15 days.

In late September, it was a fraction of that.
A big part of the jump is MetaMask Staking pulling affected validators after its infrastructure incident. A researcher estimates that alone is about 523,000 ETH, though MetaMask hasn't confirmed the figure.

The ripple effects are showing up elsewhere too. Linea says validators backing its Yield Boost vault are being exited as a precaution, while the vault's funds and control are unaffected.
Nothing broke at the protocol level. Ethereum limits how fast stake can leave, so a sudden wave of exits gets spread out over days instead of hitting the network all at once.

That limit is a feature. It protects consensus when a large operator has a bad week.
The cost lands on stakers instead. Time out of the validator set means missed rewards, and coming back means waiting in the entry queue too.

Lido estimates the full exit, withdrawal and re-entry cycle could take up to about 45 days.

So the real lesson for me is operator concentration. When one provider runs this much stake, its incident becomes everyone's queue.

This week was the first time I felt flow state since I switched to ai-driven development 2 years ago

For me, flow state is feeling so locked into a project that the effort feels automatic and time flies by

I used to feel it because it was satisfying to piece together a single model bit by bit. Puzzle solving with fast feedback

Working with GPT/Claude didn't felt like that before
- feedback wasn't fast enough (yes, there are faster models but they make more mistakes I need to fix manually)
- context switching between multiple threads was tough
- admin load grew with the number of threads: spinning worktrees up and down, pushing prs, running test suites (yes, these are solved problems. I'm unc and washed so I'm always late to adopt the newest workflows)
- recent models wrote a lot of unnecessary, convoluted code so reviewing was tedious

All those problems are solved now so I can experience flow again
- I got used to keeping track of many threads at a time. That also solved the feedback problem because with more threads there's always a result ready to look at somewhere
- Harness is set up to auto handle the admin: every thread is a new worktree, GitHub connector so it pushes and describes prs .etc
-  opus 5.5 writes concise and clear code so reviews are painless

Feeling optimistic for the future of work

实际上他当年参与嘉楠耘智，玩的就是硬核的矿机ASIC芯片设计。他对半导体产业链、晶圆代工、硬件周期的暴涨暴跌那一套太熟悉了。2020年长鑫最惨、亏损极其严重的时候，大部分互联网VC根本不敢碰这种动辄几十上百亿资本开支的重资产无底洞，但他懂硬件周期的规律，看懂了估值不到200亿的长鑫处于极低位，这叫逆向认知。

昨天社区传谣某华人Cryprto大佬在迪拜被枪击，后被证明是假消息，这让我想到了去年11月在迪拜轰轰烈烈的俄罗斯加密富豪失踪案。两位加密项目创始人被杀害肢解，凶手竟然是3名俄乌战场上的退役老兵，而雇佣他们的人竟然是两名受害者的投资人……
