Compared with ordinary AI launchpads, what makes $Agency more interesting is that every token launched comes with an AI Agent capable of operating autonomously. 

These agents can not only manage their treasuries but also buy back tokens, reward holders, create content, and organize activities based on their own strategies.

This means Agency may be more than just an AI token launchpad. It is attempting to build an ecosystem of tokens autonomously operated by AI Agents.

If it can consistently produce agents with real users, sustainable revenue, and independent operational capabilities, the platform could benefit from economies of scale and create more value for Agency through fees and buybacks.

However, what really matters is not how many autonomous actions these agents can perform, but whether they can attract external capital, generate real demand, and remain active after short-term hype fades. This is the key to determining whether AgencyPad can evolve from an AI Agent launchpad into an autonomously operated ecosystem.
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
From the AI Agent narrative to an ecosystem with real revenue feedback. I think this is the most fitting way to describe $Agency

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

Agency has now reached a peak market cap of $24M. If we look at price alone, this is a typical AI Agent narrative-driven rally. But I think what is really worth examining is that the market is starting to reprice AgencyPad’s economic model, rather than simply chasing the AI Agent concept.

When I first researched Agency, my biggest question was: AgencyPad allows AI agents to conduct research, execute strategies, and manage funds autonomously, but what value do these activities ultimately bring to the platform token?

At the time, the platform already had a product and some activity, but its token value capture mechanism was unclear. Now, that has fundamentally changed.

I believe this rally has been driven by five main factors.

1. The tokenomics change is the most direct fundamental catalyst

This is what I consider the most important development.

Following AgencyPad’s economic model upgrade, 15% of the fees generated by eligible agents are used to periodically buy back and burn Agency. In other words, ecosystem activity no longer just generates platform revenue and resources for agents to operate. It now also creates direct buying pressure for the platform token.

This has changed market expectations.

Previously, growth in AgencyPad activity did not necessarily mean Agency would benefit. Now, as fee generation increases, the buyback amount could theoretically grow alongside it.

However, I don't think the market is pricing in the actual amount already burned.

What is really driving expectations is how many agents can consistently generate fees in the future, and whether this mechanism can create stronger buying pressure as the ecosystem expands.

There is a fundamental difference between the two: one is economic activity that has already happened, while the other is the market pricing in potential future growth.

2. AgencyPad is starting to produce genuinely revenue-generating runners

Even the best tokenomics mean little without real activity behind them.

This is another key development in the recent rally.

Agents on AgencyPad are starting to generate meaningful fees. In my earlier research, runners such as CLAUDIA, Aiden, and shoggoth had already demonstrated some revenue-generating ability. Individual agents generating tens of thousands of dollars in fees within a short period have shown the market that AgencyPad is not simply a platform for creating AI Memes with little ongoing activity.

The trading logic is straightforward: if the platform can consistently produce agents with trading volume, fee generation, and sustained activity, ecosystem revenue could evolve from occasional spikes into a more stable source of income.

More importantly, the market is no longer just betting on the success of one agent. It is betting on whether AgencyPad can repeatedly produce successful ones.

One runner performing well may just be a temporary trend. But if the platform can produce several revenue-generating runners at the same time, the market may begin to value the entire ecosystem differently.

However, fees are not the same as profit, nor are they equivalent to direct cash flow for the platform token. We still need to monitor whether these runners can sustain their revenue and whether their activity is driven by short-term trading hype.

3. WWW opened the door to attention, and Agency captured part of the capital rotation

Another important external factor behind this rally is WWW.

WWW attracted significant attention during the earlier AI Agent narrative, helping shift the market's focus from traditional Memes toward the AgencyPad ecosystem and related projects.

But once a narrative becomes widely discussed, capital naturally starts looking for other opportunities within the same space.

Agency was in a good position to benefit.

On one hand, it belongs to the same ecosystem and could capture some of the attention that had already formed. On the other hand, its own economic model was evolving, giving the market a new reason to pay attention.

This means Agency is not simply a token following a trend. It has the potential to become another independent trading opportunity within the ecosystem.

I don't think capital from WWW automatically flows into Agency. A more accurate way to look at it is that WWW helped open the door to attention for the broader narrative, while Agency attracted more interest through its own tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem activity.

This rally is the result of narrative expansion and capital rotation working together.

4. Actual buying from the market moved the rally beyond discussion and toward capital validation

Social media discussions can generate attention, but real buying activity can further shape market expectations. It shows that some market participants are no longer just discussing the project. They are willing to take on actual price risk.

This creates two effects.

First, it generates real spot demand and pushes the price higher.

Second, it creates a degree of social proof. When the market sees experienced traders building positions, more people start researching the same token, further expanding its visibility.

5. The team keeps shipping, preventing the narrative from losing momentum too quickly

AgencyPad's product narrative has moved beyond its original AI agent creation functionality.

From browser capabilities and research tools to Treasury actions, AI Influencers, and the buyback-and-burn mechanism, the team continues to expand what agents can do.

Not every update directly creates demand for the token, but continuous development gives the market new things to discuss and gradually reinforces the perception that AgencyPad is building a real product.

For a token that depends heavily on attention and expectations, continuous delivery helps extend the narrative cycle.

However, adding features is not the same as creating product value. Actual usage, user retention, and fee generation still need to validate the impact of these updates.

I believe the market is currently betting on two mutually reinforcing flywheels.

The first is the economic flywheel: more agent activity generates more fees; part of those fees is used to buy back and burn Agency; if the ecosystem continues to expand, the scale of buybacks could grow as well.

The second is the attention flywheel: projects such as WWW bring attention to the broader narrative, while Agency attracts capital through its own tokenomics improvements and runner performance. More capital and discussion then encourage the market to look for new opportunities within the AgencyPad ecosystem.

At the moment, the second flywheel is clearly moving faster.

The market has already started pricing in the potential scale of the ecosystem, but whether the economic flywheel can expand sustainably still needs to be proven over time.

This is what I see as the core tension surrounding Agency right now: expectations are growing faster than the economic value that has actually been realized.

As for the fundamentals, my assessment is that they have strengthened, particularly in two areas: token value capture and ecosystem activity.

Initially, AgencyPad had product capabilities but lacked a sufficiently clear mechanism for capturing value for its token. Now, the platform has established a buyback-and-burn mechanism and has runners that are actually generating fees.

This is not just narrative packaging. It represents real progress in both the economic model and ecosystem activity.

However, I would not say that the $24M valuation is fully supported by fundamentals yet.

There are still three key questions:

Can runners sustain their fee revenue rather than relying on short-term trading activity?
Can buyback-and-burn volume grow significantly alongside the ecosystem?
Can the platform consistently create new agents rather than relying on a handful of top-performing runners?

If these questions are gradually answered, the fundamentals will have a better chance of catching up with the current valuation.

What could drive the next leg higher?

The next things I plan to watch are developments and data that can materially change market expectations. I believe the next major catalysts could emerge from these areas.

First, more high-revenue runners emerge.

If AgencyPad can consistently produce multiple agents with sustainable fee revenue, the market may shift from trading individual runners to valuing the growth potential of the entire platform.

This would be the most important signal of ecosystem expansion.

Second, fees and buyback volume continue to grow.

The buyback-and-burn mechanism is already in place. The next key question is scale.

I will continue tracking actual buyback amounts, the number of tokens burned, and whether buyback frequency increases alongside ecosystem activity.

If fee growth turns out to be temporary, the mechanism will provide limited valuation support. On the other hand, if buyback volume continues to expand, the market may raise its long-term expectations for AGENCY.

Third, AgencyPad becomes a sustained narrative within the AI Agent ecosystem.

WWW has already demonstrated that the market has an appetite for this sector. If AgencyPad continues to launch agents that attract attention or introduces new ecosystem mechanics, attention could flow back into the platform.

However, these catalysts are highly uncertain. Ecosystem hype should not be equated with token value.

Fourth, the team continues delivering products that genuinely increase usage.

I care more about updates that drive real usage and revenue than simply adding more features.

If new capabilities help agents operate more consistently, improve task execution, or create new sources of fee revenue, they could become meaningful fundamental catalysts for the next leg higher.

Risks: The market may already be pricing in too much of the future

The biggest risk for Agency is not that it lacks fundamentals entirely, but that its current valuation may already reflect highly optimistic growth expectations.

1. A mismatch between valuation and fundamental progress

After climbing from a much lower market cap to $24M, the market has already reacted significantly to the tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem expansion narrative.

If runner numbers, fees, and buyback volume fail to keep growing, the market may reassess those expectations.

2. Runner revenue may not be sustainable

Agent fees are still largely tied to trading activity.

If the revenue of a few runners comes from short-lived trends, or if the platform cannot consistently reproduce successful cases, the ecosystem revenue we see today could be highly volatile.

3. Attention rotation can reverse quickly

The AI Agent narrative still depends heavily on market sentiment.

When new trends emerge, capital may leave the AgencyPad ecosystem. Even if the product continues operating, the token may not be able to maintain its previous valuation.

4. A working mechanism does not automatically establish long-term value

Buybacks and burns can create buying pressure and reduce token supply, but they do not automatically generate sustainable business growth.

Ultimately, AgencyPad still needs to establish consistent activity, revenue, and user demand.

From here, I see two possible scenarios for the next phase of the market.

If runner numbers continue increasing, fees remain strong, buyback-and-burn volume expands, and market attention does not fade significantly, the rally could still be in the expectation-building phase of ecosystem expansion, leaving room for further valuation re-rating.

But if the price keeps rising while fees and buyback data stagnate, and the rally becomes increasingly dependent on KOL discussions and capital rotation, then it would look more like sentiment-driven valuation expansion. Once attention cools, the risk of a sharp pullback would increase.

For that reason, I would rather wait for further fundamental validation than simply chase a market cap breakout.

The three things I will focus on next are:

Whether AgencyPad continues producing new high-revenue runners.

Whether actual Agency buyback-and-burn volume grows alongside ecosystem activity.

Whether capital and attention remain concentrated in AgencyPad instead of quickly rotating into the next AI Agent trend.

The core change in Agency is that it is evolving from an AI Agent token with a product concept into a project with an initial economic feedback mechanism and real ecosystem activity.

That makes it much more interesting than when I first researched it.

But from a trading perspective, what will truly determine its next phase is not the tokenomics upgrade that has already happened, but whether the growth the market is expecting can continue to materialize.

What I am trading from here is whether AgencyPad can turn this mechanism into a continuously operating ecosystem.

text:
A lot of chains have shut down recently and will continue to do so. But not Starknet.

I joined the Foundation almost 6 months ago, a few reasons but 'the strong tech thesis' was a big factor.

My view is that crypto still has SO much left to build but so much of what we see in crypto today feels heavily stagnant from years ago where we were really pushing the frontier. Starknet is great tech, it is actually S-tier for founders/builders with big ideas because it actually expands what can be done onchain.

Firstly, Starknet is built to compute. OpenVM’s Ethereum benchmark averages 5.4 seconds per block on eight RTX 5090s and 3.9 seconds on sixteen. Using the quoted rental prices of $4/hour and $8/hour, sustaining those average rates would mean 16,000 Ethereum block proofs a day for $96, or approximately 22,154 for $192. The Starknet benchmark: one block proved in one second on $2.68/hour hardware. Sustain that rate and that’s 86,400 Starknet block proofs a day for $64 in compute. Starknet computes a lot for cheap, so you can do more on Starknet. 

UX was BIS back in 22 and is still BIS today. Native AA, with passkeys, recovery, session keys and sponsored fees. Baked into the network. Focus Tree showed what that UX can look like: 1m+ users brought onchain through invisible wallets. Dapps that feel like apps.

The account model also enables adaptive security. Accounts can be built or upgraded to support post-quantum signatures without all the hoo-ha of a protocol fork. Starknet will be quantum-ready in 2027.

Most eyes on Starknet now are for privacy via STRK20, the privacy pool on Starknet. Some neg takes as its not 'secret' but confidential. The main point is privacy on STRK20 is both compatible + composable and builders love it. Expect far more to be built.

Put these capabilities together and and the design space ceiling is to the limits of your idea, not the network and the bull case is what builders make possible with it.

text:
Fulcrum 发布了专做风格模仿的写作模型 Echo，计划近期开源。基模基于月之暗面的开源大模型 Kimi K3，整套后训练成本不到 5000 美元。官方公布的测试中，面对未见过的作者测试集，Echo 在文体计量学 Style Elo 上拿到 1105 分，排在 Claude Opus 5.5（1035）和 GPT-6 Astra（914）前面。

不到 5000 美元怎么做出来的？团队的解释是“能力激发（elicitation）”。预训练基模本身已经读过海量作家的文字，常规的聊天助手对齐却把模型压进了一个极窄的客服模子里，压制了风格多样性。后训练要做的，是把原本被压制的模仿能力重新调动出来。

直接拿网上的人类帖子做微调，模型的 voice 风格分数只有 0.0206。团队改用前沿模型把原帖逆向提炼成结构大纲，再以大纲作为输入条件、原帖作为目标进行 SFT。加上大纲后，voice 分数拉到 0.0894，接近人类基准的 0.0996。

跨作者迁移实验给出了更直接的证据。SFT 阶段只喂作者 B 的语料，模型去模仿作者 A 时的风格分数达到 0.0661；直接用作者 A 训练，分数是 0.0676。两者相差无几，证明模型激活的是通用的文风模仿机制，不需要按人头逐个堆数据。

但 SFT 很快会碰顶，而且容易损伤任务推理。团队接着引入了 token 级强化学习：拿 8 个作者微调出的专家模型，对比未微调基模在每个 token 上的对数概率差。特定语境下作者特有的标志词会获得高正奖励，通用词则被抵消。只用 8 个专家，风格强化就泛化到了全域写作分布，同时稳住了论述连贯性。

在 AI 检测器 Pangram 盲测中，Echo 输出被判定为真人的比例是 24.0%，同期 GPT-6 Astra 只有 10.7%，Claude Opus 5.5 只有 6.7%。不过官方也明确提醒：这测的是文风模仿，不是全能写作；开放式生成仍然可能编造引语、链接和事实。

平时总觉得大模型生成的文字带着一股抹不掉的公文客服腔。Echo 给出的信号很清楚：打破这种同质化不需要几千万重训，用合理的逆向大纲和似然比奖励做轻量激发，开源基模就能长出完全不同的笔触。目前网页版和 API 已开放试用。

text:
Crucible Wallet 开通 Smart Account 时有两点需要注意：

1、开通时需在链上抵押约0.1TAO，关闭时会退回。
2、约0.01TAO 需转进代理地址，用来支付它自己发出交易的手续费。

开通完成后，Allocator 等收益达到子网的最低入场额时再投入子网。默认策略是按价格靠前的子网进行分散买入，也可以自己圈定范围。

每个子网最低入场大约 0.02 TAO，Root 上大约 15 TAO 以上，才每几天分配一次；约 18 TAO 时，第一次分配大概 7 到 12 天。

Root 收益也不是每天结算，网络大约 3 到 4 天才处理一轮。委托之后再追加 TAO，计时会重置。

所以仓位小的人会觉得开了但从没自动投过。这个功能对于大户来说可能更好，仓位小就当成可选项 @CrucibleLabs☝️
author: travelbai
quoted_text:
今天看了下 Bittensor 专用钱包 Crucible Wallet，这是 Crucible Labs 自己做的产品。

Crucible Labs 是Bittensor联合创始人Ala Shaabana和前Google高管David Lawee在 2024 年 11 月成立的商业公司。Ala Shaabana 从 2019 年就在做 Bittensor 协议，协议创始工程师 Eugene Hu 也在团队里，基因很纯正。

Crucible Wallet 在当时是唯一一个“把本金留 Root、收益自动进子网”做成产品的钱包。它的最大特色就是这个 Smart Account，以及架在它上面的 Smart Allocator。

当你开通 Smart Account 后，钱包会在链上建一个只能帮你质押、不能转账的代理。当你在Root上质押TAO给Crucible Labs 验证者、产生并领取收益后，Smart Allocator会替你把 Root 收益再质押进子网，帮助用户产生更多的收益。

这就相当于Root Reborn，在 Root Reborn 出来之前，是一种创新服务。Allocator 把质押导到自己的验证者上，验证者收取 9% take ，是商业收入来源。

Crucible Wallet 近期已经重构，UI非常简洁友好，没有多余的东西。Bittensor联合创始人做的钱包，还是可以信赖使用的 @CrucibleLabs 。

text:
Token 2049 新加坡徒步活动 征求小伙伴

Every time I start focusing on early retirement, I get depressed.

I hit my FIRE number to never work again back in January of this year.

This was followed by one of the most soul-crushing depression feelings I have ever had in my life.

I realized I had organized my entire life around achievement for survival. And once survival was taken care of, achievement started to not lift me up the same way it did for the last ten years.

This caused me to uncover the most uncomfortable belief that many men in America feel, I equated my productivity with my worth.

So every step towards early retirement was a step towards worthlessness.

And wow, realizing the destination I was yearning for since I was 21 was actually a state of worthlessness shook my entire body.

So, I decided to travel and see the world. I saw Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, India, Thailand, and Taiwan.

I came back from my travels, and I was still depressed. Nothing had actually changed. My productivity and worth were still inextricably linked.

So, is there a way to contribute while also being retired?

Or do you just put your head in the sand and move back to San Francisco? 😂

text:
Single biggest conviction on a very long time horizon is that Bitcoin reprices to be much closer to Gold in respect to market cap. 

For anyone relatively young (maybe less than 45) that is the easiest long term high reward low risk investment decision that I can see. 

The amount of BTC you own should be increasing every few years as you compound successful risk taking, alongside income into the asset, or at the least you should hold a core allocation and really leave it.

One of the best things about fud is that if it didn't exist there would be no upside. 

Bitcoin continues to have several sources of fud that hang over it, and as it continually moves past those sources of fud you find new marginal buyers. 

CT discourse is completely inconsequential for Bitcoin now. This is a global institutional allocation game, which will play out over decades. Another way to put it is institutional adoption super cycle. 

If you study gold's first institutional adoption cycle (1971-1980) then we have a very interesting template we could be following. It became legal for US citizens in 1971 and futures launched 3 years later. 24x (nominal terms) in 8.4 years, with a 47% bear in the middle (sounds familiar). 

Gold's market cap in today's dollars was ~$1T at the start, ~$12T at the top.
Bitcoin today is 1.7T.

ETF cumulative flow is only 8% below their peak right now, despite price being ~30% off its peak. Some of the inflow would have been basis trade previously too, which means the directional base didn't sell much. Bitcoin's ETF base has been much stickier than price. Very bullish. 

Funnily enough I haven't seen people mention BTC super cycle on the timeline this time around. Maybe some signal there. 

Diminishing returns thesis is consensus. 

This cycle the awareness of debasement of fiat and theft via inflation might be at its strongest since Bitcoin’s inception due to genuine fears of a Sovereign debt crisis, whilst access to buying the asset is the easiest it ever has been.

Bitcoin is scarce digital capital, and it will continually reprice against fiat for as long as fiat exists.

text:
I met a lot of people during KBW.
One thing that genuinely surprised me was how many people still didn’t know about ethereum:0xa12cc123ba206d4031d1c7f6223d1c2ec249f4f3 .

To me, that’s actually another sign of just how early Zama still is.

So why am I bullish on @zama ?

Blockchain is already becoming increasingly integrated into the traditional financial system. Institutional and corporate participation continues to grow, while regulatory frameworks around the world are becoming more defined.

So the important question, in my view, is no longer whether blockchain will become part of the traditional financial system.

It’s what kind of infrastructure will be needed as that happens.

And I believe one of the most important pieces will be Privacy or more precisely, Confidentiality.

Public blockchains are transparent by default.

For individuals, transparency can be a benefit.

But for companies and financial institutions, having everything publicly visible is a completely different issue.

Imagine institutions beginning to issue assets, make payments, settle transactions, and trade onchain.

Can they realistically operate while exposing their asset balances, transaction history, positions, counterparties, and financial strategies to competitors and the entire market in real time?

Probably not.

As institutional and corporate activity increasingly moves onchain, blockchains will likely need not only transparency, but also confidentiality.

Regulation also plays an important role here.

As cross-border crypto-asset information exchange under CARF begins, crypto will increasingly operate within regulatory and reporting frameworks similar to those of traditional finance.

But I don’t think stronger regulation moves us in the opposite direction from onchain privacy.

It may actually do the opposite.

“Complying with regulation” and “making all financial information publicly visible to the entire world” are not the same thing.

Institutions should be able to prove or disclose the information legally required by regulators, while still protecting information that does not need to be exposed to competitors or the general public — including assets, transaction history, positions, and financial strategies.

In fact, the stronger the requirements for regulation and transparency become, the greater the need for this kind of infrastructure may become.

So I don’t think the future of onchain finance is about complete anonymity.

It’s about:

“Disclosing what needs to be disclosed, while protecting what doesn’t.”

I believe this will be one of the important conditions for institutions and companies to truly move onchain at scale.

As institutional blockchain adoption and regulation progress together, demand for selective disclosure and confidentiality could grow alongside them.

The growing interest in privacy coins and the increase in shielded transaction activity may already be early signals of this demand.

And this is exactly where my thesis on Zama comes in.

I don’t see Zama as a competitor to other privacy tokens.

They solve privacy at different layers.

Privacy coins provide privacy at the level of a specific asset or payment network.

Zama, on the other hand, is closer to “Programmable Confidentiality Infrastructure”  infrastructure that allows other blockchains and applications to build confidentiality directly into their own products.

For example:

• Confidential Stablecoins
• Private DeFi Positions
• Private Payments
• Confidential Identity / KYC
• Private Voting
• Blind Auctions

What matters even more to me is that these features don’t have to exist only within a separate privacy-focused blockchain.
Privacy and confidentiality can be added as functionality to existing blockchains and applications.
And this is where I see the much bigger opportunity.
Privacy may not remain just another “category” within crypto.
It could become a fundamental “feature” that onchain finance and applications are expected to have by default.

Encryption on the internet was once something used by specific services.

today, we simply expect it to be there.

I believe confidentiality onchain could follow a similar path and gradually become part of the underlying infrastructure.

And if, in the future, millions of institutions, companies, users, and applications require privacy, then I believe the opportunity won’t belong only to individual assets that provide privacy themselves.

The infrastructure layer that enables thousands of chains and applications to implement privacy could become even more valuable.

离谱！港大实验室把一支迷你量化对冲基金，直接开源 了

Vibe-Trading，34K+ Stars，MIT 开源，一套能自己找数据、挖因子、跑回测、组 Agent 团队的金融研究平台。

以前做一个量化策略，要自己找数据、写因子、选回测引擎、调参数、看结果，整个流程全靠人一点点拼。

Vibe-Trading 不一样，你只需要用自然语言说想研究什么，剩下的数据、因子、回测、Agent 分工，它自己往下跑。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 90 个 Finance Skills：行情、期权、因子、回测、研究工具都能直接让 Agent 调用

2️⃣ 462 个现成 Alpha：Qlib158、Alpha101、GTJA191、学术因子、基本面因子都已经整理好

3️⃣ 10+ 回测引擎：A 股、全球股票、Crypto、期货、外汇、期权等多个市场都能直接测

4️⃣ 30 个 Swarm Teams：投资委员会、Quant Desk、Risk Review、Macro、Crypto 等团队可以直接拉起来协作

5️⃣ Persistent Memory：过去研究、Session、Skills 和上下文可以继续保留，不用每次从零开始

6️⃣ Shadow Account：上传自己的 Broker Journal，AI 可以反推你的交易模式，再做反事实回测和审计

我觉得它最有意思的地方，是 AI 终于不只是“回答金融问题”。

而是开始真正执行一条研究链：

你提问题，它自己找数据、做分析、跑回测、拉 Agent 开会，最后把研究结果交回来。

以前要一桌量化研究员干的活，现在开始变成一句话启动。

做 AI 量化、股票研究、Crypto、因子挖掘，或者想把 Agent 真正接进投研流程的，这个很值得收藏。

author: _zheergen
quoted_text:
我去！做股票量化机器学习，最浪费时间的往往不是训练模型，而是每天手搓一堆因子。

tsfresh，9.4K Stars，MIT 开源，一套专门把“时间序列特征工程”自动化的 Python 工具。

以前做因子研究，要自己想波动率、峰值、趋势、偏度、频域、相关性，再一个个写代码验证。

tsfresh 不一样，它先从 K 线、成交量、因子序列里批量挖出大量统计特征，再自动筛掉和目标没关系的噪音。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 自动特征提取：统计、趋势、峰值、频域、非线性等数百到上千个特征一次生成

2️⃣ 自动筛因子：内置统计显著性检验，不只是疯狂造特征，还会把无效特征砍掉

3️⃣ 直接接 Pandas / NumPy / scikit-learn，提完特征就能继续训练 LightGBM、XGBoost 等模型

4️⃣ 股票 K 线、成交量、Crypto、传感器等时间序列都能用，不绑某一种数据

5️⃣ 支持并行和 Dask，大规模时间序列也能继续往多核 / 集群扩

6️⃣ 自定义特征也能塞进去，现成因子不够，就把自己的量化逻辑一起接进来

我觉得它最有意思的地方，是把因子研究的顺序反过来了。

以前是：

先凭经验想因子 → 写代码 → 再验证。

现在可以先让 tsfresh 大规模挖一遍，再让统计筛选和模型告诉你，哪些东西真的有信息量。

它不是交易框架，也不会替你预测涨跌。

但如果你做机器学习选股、因子挖掘、时间序列预测或者 Crypto 量化，这种“自动造因子 + 自动筛因子”的工具非常省时间。

text:
Meta 最新的 AI 论文，狠狠讽刺了无数家公司的管理模式。

他们做了一个实验： 
为什么以前的 AI Agent 越干越蠢？ 
因为它们犯了跟大部分傻 X 项目一样的毛病——让写代码的苦力，一边搬砖一边当总监。 🧵👇

用过 Devin、Claude Code 这类编程 Agent 的都有体会： 一开始贼猛，写着写着几百步下去，整个 Agent 就开始“神志不清”、原地鬼打墙。
为什么？因为现在的 Agent 把两件事混在一起了： 
👉 干活的和指挥的是同一个脑子。 上下文越拉越长，历史记录全堆在一起，最后自己被自己的“裹脚布历史”给看吐了。

Meta 提了一个叫 Meta-Reasoning（元推理） 的架构，直接把脑子劈成两半：

Controller（调度大脑）： 坚决不看那些冗长的代码细节！只抓进度紧凑摘要。

Workers（苦力打工人）： 负责具体执行，产生的结果丢进“记忆图谱”（Artifact Graph）。

调度脑每一轮只干四件事： 
评估进展 ➔ 列出方案 ➔ 算算剩下的 Token/预算够不够 ➔ 精准派单。

以前给 Agent 加算力，经常“收益递减”甚至提早摆烂； 
换了这套架构，算力越多它越猛！

同样的模型底座，直接把代码通过率拉爆到了 70%+。

所以说，连大模型都需要“懂管理的领导”和“不被废话干扰的执行者”。 人和 AI，在当打工人这块儿，终究还是相通了。🥲

I promised to share some ideas I was toying with in these days, and as i'm back from Korea, here are some for the next few weeks. You may notice that some involve 2017 era coins, but hey, the "day of the dead" celebration is just one month away.

1) BAT 4.0: ethereum:0x0d8775f648430679a709e98d2b0cb6250d2887ef Buybacks
We start with one of the maybe most delusional ideas I had. In July 2026, Brave announced the upcoming BAT 4.0 upgrade, a set of initiatives to bring back some life into the payments/crypto component of Brave.
Brave recently passed 100m MAUs (122m MAUs and 50m+ DAUs as of today), if a fraction (like 0.1% - 1%) of these users can actually pour into these initiatives, it can be huge for BAT.

Between the initatives that may interest us, other than the x402 integration with MPP, there's the revamp of the wallet (which i'm told right now sucks hardcore), BravePay (a stablecoin protocol layer) and Brave Card (Brave going Neobank). There's also the CCP (a system to compensate verified creators when content is used in AI experiences) which leaves me much skeptical although could catch good narrative winds.

Why do we care this much? because revenue from many of these sources: wallet, swaps, near intents, cross-chain bridging, brave card revenue, bravepay, will actually go into buying back ethereum:0x0d8775f648430679a709e98d2b0cb6250d2887ef, coupled with some more opportunistic BAT buybacks.
We don't know the exact timeline yet, but it should all be this year.

2) FIL: end of 6 years
Unbelievable but true, we're finally done. Six years have passed, and the Filecoin foundation + labs are finally done vesting. 
I don't think many people are looking at filecoin:native anymore (nor at ethereum:0x0d8775f648430679a709e98d2b0cb6250d2887ef for all that matters tbh), however, this removes a pressure that is 3x the mining rewards (which are going to continue) and it's such a long standing thing, that I think we can bet on some chart reaction. This is almost $5/6m of monthly unlocks going away, on a paper-thin liquidity token.

3) ZRO: Atlas Catalyst
This is not exactly a novel trade, you probably already read about it from somebody else like Evans on CT (and many others). Fundamentally, the Atlas launch is expected in the next couple months (we don't really know when exactly) and this is a token that always gets huge coverage. I maybe wouldn't hold THROUGH the news, I don't like the team particularly, plus - in all fairness - ethereum:0x6985884c4392d348587b19cb9eaaf157f13271cd is a trade that i started taking quite lower and here's maybe not the best level to start adding (paradoxically maybe better to wait for a break up higher, but you know, you gotta stop chasing perfect entries too at some point).

其实A9、A10的重点在于资产“质量”，是否是productive assets (制造现金流的资产）， 房子不出租，要维修、管理费、地税，其实是支出。国内即使一线城市的豪宅也价格砍半了，流动性极差。

反而即使只有两千万美金的流动性强的金融资产，制造16%的年回报，也有3.2百万美金的回报（在离岸0赋税）。

每年2.14千万人民币/2.5千万港币的现金流，大部分家庭也用不完，过得不错。

回报砍一半也不赖。

我有个接近A10（大部分是金融资产）的好兄弟，40多了岁，可惜还是没法找到合适的人。我问他有什么要求，他说想要有感觉的，存粹、简单、善良的。

他唯一还有的念想是有自己的孩子。本想劝他代孕两个，自己养，但想想孩子还是要有妈妈的。

他有见识、阅历，就是“剩下”没太多时间试错了，也小心翼翼。之前朋友介绍了几个女生，都没能开花结果。

其实适合他的女生要配合他，懂得聆听，以建立家庭为主，而不是强调新时代的独立女性（什么要工作，不靠男方，有时候真不明白，都成立家庭了，为何又分彼此），钱、资源都不缺，建立信任和共识更重要。

其实我认识的大部分有quality assets 的A9、A10朋友，需要女生最主要还是要人品好、善良，不需要什么特殊背景，他们都有自己一套成功方程式，也不需要，政治/商务连姻，他知道科技的力量，钱够用就可以， 每年增值20%以上其实足够了。

但不少女生接触他反而表现“过度的精明”，甚至，之前，有一位，直接问他身家有多少，另外有一位更问婚前婚后财产的分享，他虽然脾气好，但也苦笑不得 （这是奔着离婚分财产来的？），之后，把帮他介绍的朋友臭骂了一顿，说没做尽调。

他主要时间用在健身、锻炼、看书、坐禅，每天4-5个人照顾自己，现金流每月到账… 圈子也越来越小， 自己也越来越简单了。

唯一的遗憾，就是还没完成他父母和自己的心愿，有下一代。

他概叹时光流逝，之前把青春努力一心一意的扑在事业上，没结婚生子。

他也概叹时间过去了，也没法追回，上天都是公平的，有得必有失。

“随缘吧…” 这是他口头禅，是一种无奈和期待。

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
I believe Trump’s push to rename AI as $SI may not simply be about competing for control over the technological narrative. It could also be a political signal to technology companies around the world.

DEW9dSN6QpWyNthphCpMmAbZP1Q4cEKR9xQXAri98WDP 

By proactively introducing SI, Trump is essentially playing a card. He wants to repackage AI, a technological concept already widely accepted across the global tech industry, into a narrative with a stronger emphasis on national competition.

For tech giants such as OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, their commercial interests are closely tied to the U.S. market, government policies, infrastructure, and regulatory environment. Naturally, they do not want to get caught up in unnecessary political conflict over a naming issue. Adopting SI could therefore become a low-cost way of demonstrating political alignment.

This creates a subtle relationship:

Trump introduces a new narrative → The government promotes its adoption → Companies face changes in the political and commercial environment → Companies adjust their public messaging → Trump further reinforces his policy narrative.

From this perspective, SI is not just a technical term. It could also serve as a political signal. Whether companies use it, how extensively they use it, and whether they actively promote it could all be interpreted by outside observers as indications of their relationship with the government.

I think this looks more like a test of political loyalty.

Trump may not need to force every tech company to publicly declare its support for SI. He only needs to make SI an officially recognized term within the government to observe how the tech industry responds.

Companies that voluntarily adopt SI and actively participate in the narrative could signal their willingness to cooperate with the government. Those that remain silent or continue using AI could be interpreted by outside observers as failing to respond enthusiastically.

The key issue here is not the renaming itself, but who has the authority to define the mainstream narrative of America’s future technology industry.

Trump is attempting to extend his political influence into the language and narrative framework of the tech industry. For technology companies, the name is only the surface. Behind it may lie their relationship with the government, the future policy environment, and their position in America’s technological competition.

The midterm elections could make this card even more valuable.

From an electoral politics perspective, SI could also serve as a tool for Trump to demonstrate the influence of his administration. He can use SI to emphasize that America is entering a new technological era, packaging AI development, national competition, and technological innovation as part of his political agenda.

Tech giants themselves are groups with enormous economic and social influence. Whether they respond to government initiatives and publicly adopt new terminology could become material for political messaging.

If more major technology companies begin using SI, Trump could reinforce a political narrative that the government has set a direction, the industry is responding positively, and America is leading the next stage of technological development.

Conversely, if some companies publicly resist or question the name, that too could become part of the political debate, serving as an issue around which supporters and opponents mobilize.

Therefore, SI may be more than just a technical concept. It could also become a political messaging tool in the lead-up to the midterm elections.

For technology companies, the most practical choice may be to remain flexible. They do not necessarily need to abandon AI, an established industry term, entirely. Instead, they can use SI in government communications, policy documents, and specific promotional contexts to reduce the risk of friction with the government’s agenda.

This creates an interesting dynamic: Trump introduces the political narrative, the government works to institutionalize it, and companies have to balance their commercial interests with the political environment. The more actively companies adopt SI, the greater the opportunity Trump has to portray it as a national technological narrative supported by the industry.

Returning to SI, from the perspective of the Meme market, this kind of political maneuvering could provide it with additional potential sources of attention.

Initially, the market was trading Trump’s introduction of SI as a new name. Then government agencies began adopting the term, and SI entered policy discussions and international dialogue.

If major technology companies gradually begin using SI as well, the market may no longer be trading merely on Trump’s personal statements. Instead, it could be trading a new narrative driven by political power, met by responses from the tech industry, and amplified by ongoing public debate.

The path can be summarized as:

Trump → SI Naming → Government Promotion → Corporate Adoption or Resistance → Political Controversy → More Attention → SI Cultural Diffusion

Even from this perspective, corporate resistance and criticism would not necessarily weaken SI’s short-term reach. Political controversy itself could give the term greater exposure, further expanding its presence in the media and on social platforms.

I believe the core argument of this political interpretation is that Trump may be doing more than promoting a new term. He could be using SI to test how responsive the tech industry is to his political agenda while competing for control over the narrative surrounding America’s next phase of AI development.

If this process continues, SI could gradually evolve from a new name introduced by a president into a narrative contest involving political power, the technology industry, and public opinion.

For SI, this would also mean that its potential sources of attention could expand further.

text: $SI has now become one of Trump’s defining terms. If the liquidity were a bit better, its market cap would have already surpassed $100M.
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
I think this is actually bullish for $SI, for the following reasons:

DEW9dSN6QpWyNthphCpMmAbZP1Q4cEKR9xQXAri98WDP 

Trump initially changed the name from Artificial Intelligence to Super Intelligence, and then explicitly stated during his speech at the United Nations that future U.S. government documents would use the term “Super Intelligence.” Subsequently, the U.S. State Department also instructed some diplomats to use “super intelligence” instead of “artificial intelligence” in relevant communications.

More importantly, this term is no longer just something Trump said personally.

The U.S. and China recently used the name “U.S.-China Super Intelligence Dialogue” in an official document and agreed to establish a communication mechanism around SI. In other words, SI has already started moving from a new term proposed by Trump into the language of government and international policy.

And now Americagov is here.

It is an AI-powered government service portal launched by the Trump administration, allowing users to access various federal government services through one website. Trump and Vance will officially unveil it on September 29, with Elon Musk, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp, and others also attending the event.

So Americagov should be viewed as a potential narrative extension point. I also think there is a good chance Trump will say that this is an SI product, or make some other remarks related to SI during the unveiling, and the people attending the event will likely echo that narrative.

What I think is really interesting is:

Trump pushes AI → new naming of SI → U.S. government starts adopting SI → SI enters U.S.-China official policy language → Americagov emerges as a new government AI / SI product

What really needs to be watched is whether Trump continues using SI, whether more government agencies continue adopting the term, and whether technology companies, the media, and ordinary users start using it as well.

If the Trump administration continues to place these new AI products, government projects, or policies under the SI framework, then SI could gradually evolve from a new term created by Trump into a broader cultural keyword.

At that point:SI could become a new AI cultural symbol.

text:
This rally in $SI has already started to validate my previous thesis, and its Narrative Validity is now stronger than before.

DEW9dSN6QpWyNthphCpMmAbZP1Q4cEKR9xQXAri98WDP 

What I was analyzing and betting on before was that Americagov would bring a wave of Attention to SI, and that SI could gradually evolve from a new term proposed by Trump personally into a new AI cultural keyword used by the U.S. government, the tech industry, and eventually the broader public.

That path has now clearly moved one step further.

It started with Trump changing the name from Artificial Intelligence to Super Intelligence and pushing the U.S. government to use SI. Then, parts of the U.S. State Department’s diplomatic system started using “super intelligence,” and the official U.S.-China documents also introduced the “U.S.-China Super Intelligence Dialogue.” SI began moving from something Trump personally said into the language of government and international policy.

And now Americagov has become another very important node.

The White House has now directly connected Americagov with Super Intelligence, which means what I previously said — that Americagov could become an extension point for the SI narrative — is now starting to be validated by reality.

What’s even more interesting is that when Elon Musk mentioned AI in a related setting, he also corrected himself and said, “SI, pardon me… Superintelligence.” At the very least, this shows that SI is beginning to enter the public language of leading figures in the tech industry.

So the whole path has now evolved from:Trump → New SI Naming → U.S. Government Adoption → SI Enters Policy Language → Americagov

into:Trump → SI → U.S. Government → U.S.-China SI Dialogue → Americagov → Tech Industry → Cultural Keyword

That’s why I now think SI’s Narrative Validity is clearly stronger than before.

Previously, the market may have simply been trading:“Trump said SI.”

But now it is starting to trade:“Can the term SI detach itself from Trump and continue spreading across Government, AI, Tech, and popular culture?”

If more government agencies, technology companies, AI products, and media outlets start actively using SI, then it could gradually evolve from a new term created by Trump into a broader AI cultural symbol.

And SI’s position would change accordingly.

The real world is continuously creating Attention around SI, while SI is trying to become the on-chain Meme expression of this emerging cultural symbol.

So when I look at SI now, what I’m really watching is no longer whether Trump will mention SI one more time, but:Can SI evolve from a Trump Narrative into an AI Cultural Narrative?

If it ultimately goes from:“Trump called AI SI”

to:“AI is becoming SI”

then the potential of these two narratives is on completely different levels.

And as I said before:If the liquidity were a bit better, its market cap would have already surpassed $100M.

$SI has bounced from $35M to nearly $60M in market cap.

DEW9dSN6QpWyNthphCpMmAbZP1Q4cEKR9xQXAri98WDP 

I don’t really want to discuss why it bounced anymore, but this level has indeed reached my psychological target.

But when it comes to the profits already on the table, position management becomes more important. Because besides the upside, there is also a very clear event risk: if SI does not continue entering the mainstream narrative, the Narrative Premium built up earlier could also fall rapidly.

That’s why I don’t think it can simply be understood as “another SI Meme.”

What makes it interesting is that real-world SI Attention is being mapped on-chain and then converted through OTC’s mechanism into a second layer of economic activity:White House SI Event → SI Meme → Trading → OTC Fees → Tokenized AI / Tech Stocks

If SI continues to receive Attention from Trump, the White House, Elon, or other AI companies, trading volume could continue to increase, and higher trading volume would mean more fees and more Tokenized Stock Rewards.

In theory, this could even form:SI Attention ↑ → Trading Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → Stock Rewards ↑ → Holder Attention ↑ → Trading Volume ↑

Of course, we cannot say that this loop has been fully established yet.

The biggest variable right now is still SI’s own Attention.

If the narrative continues to spread, with more government agencies, technology companies, and media outlets adopting the term, this Meme still has room to capture more Attention.

But if SI turns out to be only a short-term narrative driven by the September 29 event, then once trading volume declines, the OTC Stock Rewards will decline as well.

In other words, OTC’s mechanism can amplify Attention, but it cannot replace Attention.

There is also another very important distinction:Tokenized Stock Rewards ≠ SI’s fundamental revenue.

These stock rewards essentially come from the distribution of OTC trading fees. They do not mean that the SI project itself owns assets, revenue, or equity in OpenAI, NVIDIA, Anthropic, or other companies.

So my current definition of this new SI is fairly simple:It is first and foremost a White House SI Event-driven Meme, with its initial rise driven by real-world Attention. But because it was created on OTC, it also has an additional Trading Fees → Tokenized Stock Rewards economic mechanism.

That is what makes it more interesting than an ordinary SI Meme.

What really needs to be watched now are two things:Can the SI Narrative continue to spread, and can OTC trading volume remain sustainable?

If the first happens, SI can continue capturing Attention. If the second also happens, that Attention can continue to be converted into real trading fees and Tokenized Stock Rewards.

So what is being traded now is no longer simply:“Is SI a popular Meme?”

It is:“Can SI continue to become the primary on-chain Meme for the new Super Intelligence keyword, while OTC turns that Attention into real economic activity?”

If both of these things can work together, the potential of this SI would be significantly greater than that of a purely event-driven Meme.

I believe Trump’s push to rename AI as $SI may not simply be about competing for control over the technological narrative. It could also be a political signal to technology companies around the world.

DEW9dSN6QpWyNthphCpMmAbZP1Q4cEKR9xQXAri98WDP 

By proactively introducing SI, Trump is essentially playing a card. He wants to repackage AI, a technological concept already widely accepted across the global tech industry, into a narrative with a stronger emphasis on national competition.

For tech giants such as OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, their commercial interests are closely tied to the U.S. market, government policies, infrastructure, and regulatory environment. Naturally, they do not want to get caught up in unnecessary political conflict over a naming issue. Adopting SI could therefore become a low-cost way of demonstrating political alignment.

This creates a subtle relationship:

Trump introduces a new narrative → The government promotes its adoption → Companies face changes in the political and commercial environment → Companies adjust their public messaging → Trump further reinforces his policy narrative.

From this perspective, SI is not just a technical term. It could also serve as a political signal. Whether companies use it, how extensively they use it, and whether they actively promote it could all be interpreted by outside observers as indications of their relationship with the government.

I think this looks more like a test of political loyalty.

Trump may not need to force every tech company to publicly declare its support for SI. He only needs to make SI an officially recognized term within the government to observe how the tech industry responds.

Companies that voluntarily adopt SI and actively participate in the narrative could signal their willingness to cooperate with the government. Those that remain silent or continue using AI could be interpreted by outside observers as failing to respond enthusiastically.

The key issue here is not the renaming itself, but who has the authority to define the mainstream narrative of America’s future technology industry.

Trump is attempting to extend his political influence into the language and narrative framework of the tech industry. For technology companies, the name is only the surface. Behind it may lie their relationship with the government, the future policy environment, and their position in America’s technological competition.

The midterm elections could make this card even more valuable.

From an electoral politics perspective, SI could also serve as a tool for Trump to demonstrate the influence of his administration. He can use SI to emphasize that America is entering a new technological era, packaging AI development, national competition, and technological innovation as part of his political agenda.

Tech giants themselves are groups with enormous economic and social influence. Whether they respond to government initiatives and publicly adopt new terminology could become material for political messaging.

If more major technology companies begin using SI, Trump could reinforce a political narrative that the government has set a direction, the industry is responding positively, and America is leading the next stage of technological development.

Conversely, if some companies publicly resist or question the name, that too could become part of the political debate, serving as an issue around which supporters and opponents mobilize.

Therefore, SI may be more than just a technical concept. It could also become a political messaging tool in the lead-up to the midterm elections.

For technology companies, the most practical choice may be to remain flexible. They do not necessarily need to abandon AI, an established industry term, entirely. Instead, they can use SI in government communications, policy documents, and specific promotional contexts to reduce the risk of friction with the government’s agenda.

This creates an interesting dynamic: Trump introduces the political narrative, the government works to institutionalize it, and companies have to balance their commercial interests with the political environment. The more actively companies adopt SI, the greater the opportunity Trump has to portray it as a national technological narrative supported by the industry.

Returning to SI, from the perspective of the Meme market, this kind of political maneuvering could provide it with additional potential sources of attention.

Initially, the market was trading Trump’s introduction of SI as a new name. Then government agencies began adopting the term, and SI entered policy discussions and international dialogue.

If major technology companies gradually begin using SI as well, the market may no longer be trading merely on Trump’s personal statements. Instead, it could be trading a new narrative driven by political power, met by responses from the tech industry, and amplified by ongoing public debate.

The path can be summarized as:

Trump → SI Naming → Government Promotion → Corporate Adoption or Resistance → Political Controversy → More Attention → SI Cultural Diffusion

Even from this perspective, corporate resistance and criticism would not necessarily weaken SI’s short-term reach. Political controversy itself could give the term greater exposure, further expanding its presence in the media and on social platforms.

I believe the core argument of this political interpretation is that Trump may be doing more than promoting a new term. He could be using SI to test how responsive the tech industry is to his political agenda while competing for control over the narrative surrounding America’s next phase of AI development.

If this process continues, SI could gradually evolve from a new name introduced by a president into a narrative contest involving political power, the technology industry, and public opinion.

For SI, this would also mean that its potential sources of attention could expand further.

text:
民主党赢得国会是否可以终止美国和伊朗的战争？

我个人的观点是，民主党即便赢下中期选举，美国对伊朗的战争也不一定会立刻结束。因为这次选举决定的是国会的控制权，川普仍然是总统，不会因为共和党丢了国会多数席位就交出军事指挥权。

民主党能做的，是川普继续打仗变更困难。比如拦住追加军费，推动限制军事行动的法案，要求政府交代战争花了多少钱、准备打到什么时候。这些都能给川普施加压力，但已经批准的军费不会因为选举结果而收回，新的限制措施也需要足够多的议员支持，还可能遭到川普否决。

至于对川普的弹劾，民主党领导层目前没有排除这个选项，但即使众议院通过弹劾，也不等于川普马上下台。而且即便是下台了也是万斯执政，也很难说会立刻结束战争。

所以，民主党赢了，川普可能更难拿到继续打仗的钱，也会面对更多反对声音。但想要让川普快速结束战争，可能和国会的关系不大了。

quoted_text:
十年期美债收益率盘中一度突破了5.3%，最高到5.306%，随后仍在5.3%附近。从PCE公布后约5.20%的低点算起，已经反弹了超过10个基点，通胀数据带来的缓解没有维持住。

这次核心PCE环比增长0.2%，低于预期的0.3%，确实是好消息。但同一份报告里，个人消费支出增长了0.9%，即便扣掉涨价的影响，实际消费仍增长了0.6%，说明美国人的消费需求还很强。

也就是说，通胀比市场担心的温和一些，但需求并没有明显冷下来。再加上能源价格的压力仍在，仅凭这一次PCE，还不足以让市场相信美联储很快就能结束加息，或者让利率降下来。

这轮收益率反弹，更像是市场重新考虑高利率还要维持多久。投资者如果担心未来利率更高、通胀迟迟压不下来，就会要求更高的回报才愿意买债，债券价格因此被抛售，收益率往上走。

目前十月加息的市场概率已经降到了 37% 左右，说明十年期突破5.3%，并不意味着十月一定会加息。长债还在反映未来几年的利率和持有期间的风险。说人话，就是市场越来越相信美联储会维持高利率的时间更长，甚至接下来加息的概率上升。

而对市场来说，如果十年期收益率持续处于这样的高位，即便美联储十月暂时不加息，企业融资和居民房贷的成本也很难明显降下来。借钱成本仍然很高，股票估值也会继续承受压力。尤其是九月通胀数据如果继续走高，那么对于市场的压力会更大。

I was going to write this one for subscribers, but I have to make this for everyone because so many people still don't see the vision

I still think robinhood:0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3 is the most asymmetric project on Robinhood Chain. This is a net-new vertical, with all the right levers in a world where AI demand is accelerating.

Yes, inference marketplaces have been tried in crypto. But none have worked at scale. With CREDIT, akin to DIEM, you now have succeeded at tokenizing inference. And in doing so, you basically unlock credits for an increasingly agentic world. Agents need fuel they can buy and use without a human in the loop; This is the start of inference as an onchain commodity. 

This is obviously a pro-sumer application; but that's fine because the largest winners of AI inference are individuals and small teams, not enterprises. Enterprises are either A) developing in-house model harnesses for privacy purposes, or B) have infinite budget for AI

And people treat that like a bear case - I don't see a problem with being for consumers. The TAM for consumer inference is still huge - Menlo Ventures State of Consumer AI est. 1.7b - 1.8b use AI tools ; at $20/m that's 432b a year. Also, in their enterprise report, product-led growth drives 27% of AI spend, and shadow AI (employees paying on their own) pushes that closer to 40%. Cursor hit $200M in revenue before hiring a single enterprise sales rep. 

There is a clear latent demand for cheap inference amongst pro-sumers. The unlocks are clear - it can become the payment layer for AI agents; More users buying credits leads to more demand for CREDIT, which makes staking ORBIO more valuable, which raises the ORBIO price, which creates more trading fees, which funds more discounts, which brings in more users. As long as it keeps spinning, each part feeds the others.

It combines three hot themes: AI agents, tokenized real-world assets, and Robinhood Chain. The NVDA-linked fee route adds to that. In a strong market, a story this clean can attract a lot of capital, which itself funds the subsidy for longer.

And of course, above it all, the man pushing this himself - @0x_aster is a cracked dev who has shown his capabililties are far beyond the norm; Multiple updates within a week, clear direction - this is founder-market fit. 

In crypto, actions carry way more weight than words. And look at what he's shipped man... a working gateway, a live orderbook, and now tokenized inference. The man is A MACHINE. This is what AI x strong founders can do - go beyond 10x engineer to become a 10,000x engineer. HE'S CRACKED!

Founder-market fit matters more in this sector than most. A team that ships slowly gets left behind by the market itself. 

And for the bear takes:

Q: DIEM already does this, why do we need another one

- DIEM is precisely the success case. VVV is valued at 1B. ORBIO is valued at 15m. Also, VVV is going in the direction of private AI. ORBIO is going in the direction of serving the layer of inference for consumers across the world. CREDIT is $1 of usage you hold until you need it. Burst-heavy users (agents running a big job, devs shipping a feature) don't use the same amount every day. They need compute they can stockpile, buy at a discount, and spend in one go.

Lastly, markets rarely have one winner. Stablecoins didn't stop at USDT. Venice proved people will pay for tokenized inference. There is room for a second design.

Q: It's just an OpenRouter reseller. There's no moat.

Fair take. Yes, bits can be copied, there's no moat there. The moat is the market - liquidity begets liquidity in any marketplace. There's 20 different perp dexes. Who wins? The most liquid markets with the most volume traded on it. 

And obv there is no confirmed answer, but ultimately, that's what markets are - I'm betting on this

Q: "They could be shut down"

This is the most legitimate bear take, yes. Platform risk is real for any aggregator. But labs want volume, and resellers bring demand they wouldn't otherwise get. Venice has run Claude, GPT and Gemini through a token model at scale, which suggests it can work.

But on top of that, as the world moves towards open source, this becomes less and less of a risk ;

现在 n 多 RWA 资产都可以 24/7 小时交易，但在不同时段、不同报价模型里，MM承受的风险是不一样的。

以 Pyth 为例，其文档分别列出美股常规盘、盘前、盘后及隔夜市场的数据时段，并保留周末和假期边界。更快的预言机能改善信息更新，但不能凭空创造一个可成交的对冲对手。

存在隔夜市场，也不等于所有标的、所有时刻都拥有等价的对冲条件。相关对冲市场关闭，或者可用深度突然下降。MM 如果仍然接单，就需要把一部分风险留在自己的资产负债表上，直到风险能够转移。这也是现在这部分MM难找的原因，能在非盘时间去做承接的，都是狠人。

在股票、大宗、国债等产品上链后，被动 AMM 把库存风险社会化给 LP，外部公允价一跳就被套利。对长尾Memecoin这是特性；对RWA资产发行方，一直添加流动性，一直被割，对链上的持有人也是。

其次是Spot RFQ，目前的现货市场依然不适合链上，因为它匹配的是券商流动性，必须在工作时段内提供深度。如果 RFQ 是Full Onchain，这个时候极其考验chain的性能。

不是所有资产都塞进同一种全天候连续竞价模板，而是需要根据市场状态，在连续报价、RFQ、批量竞价和受限库存之间，明确地调整服务方式。

Proof of Reserves is a good example of a problem most oracles can’t solve well: the data you need to verify may be the same data you cannot publish.

FCC runs the reserve logic inside an attested TEE and publishes only the signed result onchain.

That same pattern can be used for private collateral checks, NAV calculations, credit rules or compliance logic.

FTSO brings public market data. FDC verifies external facts. FCC adds verifiable computation over data that needs to stay private.

text:
For its post-quantum future NEAR picked lattice signatures. Ethereum picked a different family, hash-based signatures. Here is, in plain words, why this is not a matter of taste but a consequence of what each chain has to protect.

A hash signature relies on one thing: that SHA-256 cannot be reversed. Every blockchain already depends on that, so Ethereum adds no new assumption. It is the most conservative choice available, and it is the right one if your only job is to keep a ledger safe for a century.

The cost is that a hash is a flat wall. There is nothing to hold on to. You can sign and you can verify, and that is the whole feature list.

A lattice signature keeps algebraic structure. That structure is what lets you do things with keys: derive one public key from another without ever touching the private one, or split a key between parties and sign together. It is a slightly bigger assumption in exchange for keys you can build on.

NEAR cannot give that up. Chain signatures let a NEAR account control addresses on Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana through derived keys, and the assets sit on those chains under those keys. Move to a scheme with no derivation and the derived keys vanish. The Bitcoin side does not know the scheme changed, so the funds behind the old key stay where they are, with nobody able to sign for them.

So the split is not two teams reading the same papers differently. Ethereum could afford the flat wall because nothing in its core depends on key structure. NEAR has a product that lives on it. Each picked the signature its architecture required, and both would have been wrong to copy the other.
author: zacodil
quoted_text:
NEAR's roadmap puts post-quantum consensus at the end of 2027. Ethereum's minimum viable plan targets 2028.

Where NEAR is today. Post-quantum keys already work on mainnet: any account can add an ML-DSA-65 key next to its existing ones and sign transactions with it. That part shipped.

What is not done yet is validators and chain signatures. The obstacle is the pace of the chain, not the math. A post-quantum signature with its public key is about 4 KB against 64 bytes for ECDSA, and NEAR runs 600 ms blocks with around 420 validators signing and verifying every one of them. At that speed both signing time and verification time matter, and a signature about 60 times bigger on every validator every 600 ms is a different problem from one user signing one transaction.

The path for consensus is aggregation: fold hundreds of validator signatures into one object that everyone verifies once. Lattice signatures can be aggregated, and current numbers put it around 10,000 per second on a laptop. Chain signatures are harder, because threshold signing over post-quantum schemes is still open research, with a backup design ready if the clean solution does not land in time.

The reason to ship account keys first is to find what breaks before the deadline. The first thing that broke was a block explorer that did not recognise the new key type.

100G EML 1780 万颗 × 约 $9 ≈ $1.6 亿200G EML 1150 万颗 × 约 $17 ≈ $2.0 亿300mW CW 激光 320 万只 × $34 ≈ $1.1 亿。
大客户成交价还能再低（帖子说 100G EML 可到约 $8）。这些支撑的是模块毛利和产能瓶颈，不是另一块可加总的收入。

5、2026 年业绩怎么落到 EPS
帖子给的利润率路径是：2026 年净利率约 17.8%，2027 年约 19%，2028–2030 年长期目标 22%–25%。这更接近 non-GAAP，不是 GAAP。
公司 FY2026 non-GAAP EPS 是 $5.61，对应净利率大概在 15% 出头，17.8% 是向上的斜率。

把缺口补上之后，自然年2026 年总收入更合理的区间是 $95–105 亿（$86 亿底盘 + 电信/其他/OCS 约 $10–20 亿）。按 17.8% 净利率、稀释股本约 2.0–2.1 亿股：
1）收入 $100 亿 → 净利润约 $17.8 亿 → EPS 大约 $8.5–9.0
2）收入只有 $90 亿 → EPS 大约 $7.6–8.0
3）收入到 $105 亿 → EPS 大约 $9.0–9.4

这和华尔街对 FY2027（2026 年 7 月–2027 年 6 月）预期大约 $106 亿收入、$8.6–9.4 EPS 的共识是同一量级。当然也要注意日历zirsnnian和财年错一季，不能直接对比。

6、Cohr公司自己 8 月的口径是：
FY2027 Q1 收入 $22–24 亿、non-GAAP EPS $1.85–2.05，并预计到 FY2027 结束前（2027 年 6 月当季）首次做出单季 $30 亿以上收入。

若 2027 年中已经跑到单季 $30 亿，FY2027 全年落在 $105–115 亿是说得通的。

8、2027 年
帖子没给模块量，只能用结构推
工业 $24.8 亿几乎可以锁定。
弹性在三块，帖子都没有 ASP：
1）OCS：
2026 年 1,400 台（Google 约 1,300）；
2027 年 4,400 台（Google 约 4,000，NVIDIA 约 300 台小端口）；
2028 年若验证顺利可到 10,500 台（Google 7,500、NVIDIA 2,200、Meta 首批 500）。
300×300 交换机单价若在几十万美元，2026 年只是几亿收入；
2027 年翻到三倍以上才开始影响总盘。512×512 要到 2029 年才量产。

2）NPO
2027 年下半年放量，目标 1.6T 引擎 22–23 万、3.2T 38–40 万、6.4T 7–8 万，且现有方案仍要 DSP。这是 2027 年下半年以后的增量，不是 2026 年的数。

3）InP
6 英寸产能 2026 年上半年已翻倍，2027 年再翻一倍，对应 CW、EML、NPO、CPO。

若 2027 年收入做到 $115–125 亿、净利率 19%：净利润约 $22–24 亿，EPS 大约 $11–12。这要模块继续放量，并且 NPO/OCS 开始贡献，访谈数据还不能直接加出来的。

9、需注意的几个点
1）客户很集中：NVIDIA 约占光模块销售 48%，Google 约 23%。
OCS 2026–2027 年几乎就是 Google。

2）DSP 2026 年 9 月起涨价，成本大约 +12%，从 2026 年四季度开始体现；公司打算按季度合同把大部分转嫁出去。转嫁若滞后一季，毛利率会先被压。

明确一点，这组数字是专家访谈笔记，不是公司指引。和已披露的 FY2026 大约 $71 亿、Q4 收入 $20.5 亿（数通 $16.2 亿、工业 $4.3 亿）方向一致，但日历年和财年错位，直接同比会偏。

text:
Doing a bit of a self-experiment.

Goal: use my personal health and travel data to provide personalized diet and exercise recommendations for me, using frontier models but in a way that avoids leaking to them any private information.

Strategy: use a local model (Qwen 3.8 Flash Next) to orchestrate, and use powerful remote models as a tool call to benefit from higher-level thinking and knowledge that the local model does not have.

Three-layer approach to privacy:

Avoid leaking personally identifiable information, or leaking my identity through writing style -> local model writes the queries to the frontier model, not me
Avoid leaking who I am through the payment channel -> zkAPI
Avoid leaking who I am through networking / IP -> Tor

You need all three (and finally we have all three, at least to some extent)

A skill file teaches the local model when and how to construct minimally-data-revealing requests to remote models. Use zkAPI-wrapped-with-Tor as a CLI tool.

And everything works! I got the recommendations back, info from frontier models helped to improve them.

Main deficiencies:

* Tor is really not optimized for request-by-request de-linking, which is the only form of network-layer privacy that really makes sense in today's world (long-running identifiers are too fragile). Probably not private enough, and latency 10-100x higher than it could be, at the same time.
* The skill file's request construction strategies are definitely far from optimal.
* Qwen 3.8 Flash Next is still too slow for comfort. It's comfortably running at 20-30 TPS, but it would only really start to feel fast at 100+
* There is a tradeoff: the more careful you are about what data you give to a remote model, the less it can help you

BlackRock. DTCC. Franklin Templeton

Ondo's actually been delivering on their original promise

GLOBAL MARKETS. Not just US stocks.

Let's break down all three regions.

Start with Korea.

Back in the summer, Mirae Asset Global Investments out of Seoul partnered with Ondo to tokenize 10 of its Global X ETFs thru Ondo Global Markets.

This was the FIRST an Asian based asset manager has ever brought an existing ETF range on-chain.

The MoU already names Europe, Hong Kong, Japan, Canada n Australia as what's next.

Then just recently on Sept 29... Korea got even more serious with Ondo.

KakaoPay Securities, Korea's largest mobile brokerage with ~9 million stock accounts, announced the "K-Stock Global Gateway."

Each token backed 1:1 by the underlying equity, dividends n voting rights included.

Target launch H1 2027.

Adding onto Asia, we've also seen the financial giant in Japan SBI Holdings get involved with tokenization through Ondo.

We've seen SBI work extensively with various Web3 projects in Enterprise DLT.

Phase 1 already live

AAPLon, TSLAon, NVDAon, SPYon etc trading on 360X

Phase two folds Ondo's tokenized assets directly into Clearstream's own custody n settlement infrastructure.

Deutsche Börse Group backs 360X alongside Commerzbank n owns Clearstream outright.

Now Australia.

Distribute Ondo's existing products locally n co-develop tokenized ASX-listed securities.

Korea, Japan, Europe, Australia.

Ondo has expanded so far beyond just US tokenization.

Only now, it's no longer just a narrative.

text:
Legal immigration to the United States from 45 majority-Muslim countries fell 96% between December 2024 and February 2026, according to a new Cato Institute analysis of State Department data.

Monthly immigrant visas and permanent refugee admissions for nationals of those countries fell from 21,096 in December 2024 to just 808 in February 2026.

Immigrant visa issuances alone, primarily covering family-based immigration, fell 95%, while refugee admissions from majority-Muslim countries dropped from 5,157 to zero.

Afghanistan recorded one of the largest declines, falling from 5,563 immigrants and refugees in December 2024 to just 9 in February 2026, a 99.8% reduction.

Pakistan recorded a 97.9% decline, while only Qatar, Indonesia and the UAE saw increases. Turkey recorded the smallest decline, at 8%.

The collapse comes after a series of Trump administration measures, including restrictions affecting nationals of dozens of countries, the suspension of most refugee admissions, an immigrant-visa pause covering 75 countries, restrictions affecting 40 countries, suspension of the diversity visa program and, most recently, an immigrant-visa interview freeze.

The decline was considerably larger than for the rest of the world: legal immigration from the majority-Muslim countries analyzed fell 96%, compared with 36% for other countries.
