text:
Compared with ordinary AI launchpads, what makes $Agency more interesting is that every token launched comes with an AI Agent capable of operating autonomously. 

These agents can not only manage their treasuries but also buy back tokens, reward holders, create content, and organize activities based on their own strategies.

This means Agency may be more than just an AI token launchpad. It is attempting to build an ecosystem of tokens autonomously operated by AI Agents.

If it can consistently produce agents with real users, sustainable revenue, and independent operational capabilities, the platform could benefit from economies of scale and create more value for Agency through fees and buybacks.

However, what really matters is not how many autonomous actions these agents can perform, but whether they can attract external capital, generate real demand, and remain active after short-term hype fades. This is the key to determining whether AgencyPad can evolve from an AI Agent launchpad into an autonomously operated ecosystem.
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
From the AI Agent narrative to an ecosystem with real revenue feedback. I think this is the most fitting way to describe $Agency

7VertkgF9KLhxxJXHX6uaWuoYZTP9LdGj2bWmVXVpump 

Agency has now reached a peak market cap of $24M. If we look at price alone, this is a typical AI Agent narrative-driven rally. But I think what is really worth examining is that the market is starting to reprice AgencyPad’s economic model, rather than simply chasing the AI Agent concept.

When I first researched Agency, my biggest question was: AgencyPad allows AI agents to conduct research, execute strategies, and manage funds autonomously, but what value do these activities ultimately bring to the platform token?

At the time, the platform already had a product and some activity, but its token value capture mechanism was unclear. Now, that has fundamentally changed.

I believe this rally has been driven by five main factors.

1. The tokenomics change is the most direct fundamental catalyst

This is what I consider the most important development.

Following AgencyPad’s economic model upgrade, 15% of the fees generated by eligible agents are used to periodically buy back and burn Agency. In other words, ecosystem activity no longer just generates platform revenue and resources for agents to operate. It now also creates direct buying pressure for the platform token.

This has changed market expectations.

Previously, growth in AgencyPad activity did not necessarily mean Agency would benefit. Now, as fee generation increases, the buyback amount could theoretically grow alongside it.

However, I don't think the market is pricing in the actual amount already burned.

What is really driving expectations is how many agents can consistently generate fees in the future, and whether this mechanism can create stronger buying pressure as the ecosystem expands.

There is a fundamental difference between the two: one is economic activity that has already happened, while the other is the market pricing in potential future growth.

2. AgencyPad is starting to produce genuinely revenue-generating runners

Even the best tokenomics mean little without real activity behind them.

This is another key development in the recent rally.

Agents on AgencyPad are starting to generate meaningful fees. In my earlier research, runners such as CLAUDIA, Aiden, and shoggoth had already demonstrated some revenue-generating ability. Individual agents generating tens of thousands of dollars in fees within a short period have shown the market that AgencyPad is not simply a platform for creating AI Memes with little ongoing activity.

The trading logic is straightforward: if the platform can consistently produce agents with trading volume, fee generation, and sustained activity, ecosystem revenue could evolve from occasional spikes into a more stable source of income.

More importantly, the market is no longer just betting on the success of one agent. It is betting on whether AgencyPad can repeatedly produce successful ones.

One runner performing well may just be a temporary trend. But if the platform can produce several revenue-generating runners at the same time, the market may begin to value the entire ecosystem differently.

However, fees are not the same as profit, nor are they equivalent to direct cash flow for the platform token. We still need to monitor whether these runners can sustain their revenue and whether their activity is driven by short-term trading hype.

3. WWW opened the door to attention, and Agency captured part of the capital rotation

Another important external factor behind this rally is WWW.

WWW attracted significant attention during the earlier AI Agent narrative, helping shift the market's focus from traditional Memes toward the AgencyPad ecosystem and related projects.

But once a narrative becomes widely discussed, capital naturally starts looking for other opportunities within the same space.

Agency was in a good position to benefit.

On one hand, it belongs to the same ecosystem and could capture some of the attention that had already formed. On the other hand, its own economic model was evolving, giving the market a new reason to pay attention.

This means Agency is not simply a token following a trend. It has the potential to become another independent trading opportunity within the ecosystem.

I don't think capital from WWW automatically flows into Agency. A more accurate way to look at it is that WWW helped open the door to attention for the broader narrative, while Agency attracted more interest through its own tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem activity.

This rally is the result of narrative expansion and capital rotation working together.

4. Actual buying from the market moved the rally beyond discussion and toward capital validation

Social media discussions can generate attention, but real buying activity can further shape market expectations. It shows that some market participants are no longer just discussing the project. They are willing to take on actual price risk.

This creates two effects.

First, it generates real spot demand and pushes the price higher.

Second, it creates a degree of social proof. When the market sees experienced traders building positions, more people start researching the same token, further expanding its visibility.

5. The team keeps shipping, preventing the narrative from losing momentum too quickly

AgencyPad's product narrative has moved beyond its original AI agent creation functionality.

From browser capabilities and research tools to Treasury actions, AI Influencers, and the buyback-and-burn mechanism, the team continues to expand what agents can do.

Not every update directly creates demand for the token, but continuous development gives the market new things to discuss and gradually reinforces the perception that AgencyPad is building a real product.

For a token that depends heavily on attention and expectations, continuous delivery helps extend the narrative cycle.

However, adding features is not the same as creating product value. Actual usage, user retention, and fee generation still need to validate the impact of these updates.

I believe the market is currently betting on two mutually reinforcing flywheels.

The first is the economic flywheel: more agent activity generates more fees; part of those fees is used to buy back and burn Agency; if the ecosystem continues to expand, the scale of buybacks could grow as well.

The second is the attention flywheel: projects such as WWW bring attention to the broader narrative, while Agency attracts capital through its own tokenomics improvements and runner performance. More capital and discussion then encourage the market to look for new opportunities within the AgencyPad ecosystem.

At the moment, the second flywheel is clearly moving faster.

The market has already started pricing in the potential scale of the ecosystem, but whether the economic flywheel can expand sustainably still needs to be proven over time.

This is what I see as the core tension surrounding Agency right now: expectations are growing faster than the economic value that has actually been realized.

As for the fundamentals, my assessment is that they have strengthened, particularly in two areas: token value capture and ecosystem activity.

Initially, AgencyPad had product capabilities but lacked a sufficiently clear mechanism for capturing value for its token. Now, the platform has established a buyback-and-burn mechanism and has runners that are actually generating fees.

This is not just narrative packaging. It represents real progress in both the economic model and ecosystem activity.

However, I would not say that the $24M valuation is fully supported by fundamentals yet.

There are still three key questions:

Can runners sustain their fee revenue rather than relying on short-term trading activity?
Can buyback-and-burn volume grow significantly alongside the ecosystem?
Can the platform consistently create new agents rather than relying on a handful of top-performing runners?

If these questions are gradually answered, the fundamentals will have a better chance of catching up with the current valuation.

What could drive the next leg higher?

The next things I plan to watch are developments and data that can materially change market expectations. I believe the next major catalysts could emerge from these areas.

First, more high-revenue runners emerge.

If AgencyPad can consistently produce multiple agents with sustainable fee revenue, the market may shift from trading individual runners to valuing the growth potential of the entire platform.

This would be the most important signal of ecosystem expansion.

Second, fees and buyback volume continue to grow.

The buyback-and-burn mechanism is already in place. The next key question is scale.

I will continue tracking actual buyback amounts, the number of tokens burned, and whether buyback frequency increases alongside ecosystem activity.

If fee growth turns out to be temporary, the mechanism will provide limited valuation support. On the other hand, if buyback volume continues to expand, the market may raise its long-term expectations for AGENCY.

Third, AgencyPad becomes a sustained narrative within the AI Agent ecosystem.

WWW has already demonstrated that the market has an appetite for this sector. If AgencyPad continues to launch agents that attract attention or introduces new ecosystem mechanics, attention could flow back into the platform.

However, these catalysts are highly uncertain. Ecosystem hype should not be equated with token value.

Fourth, the team continues delivering products that genuinely increase usage.

I care more about updates that drive real usage and revenue than simply adding more features.

If new capabilities help agents operate more consistently, improve task execution, or create new sources of fee revenue, they could become meaningful fundamental catalysts for the next leg higher.

Risks: The market may already be pricing in too much of the future

The biggest risk for Agency is not that it lacks fundamentals entirely, but that its current valuation may already reflect highly optimistic growth expectations.

1. A mismatch between valuation and fundamental progress

After climbing from a much lower market cap to $24M, the market has already reacted significantly to the tokenomics upgrade and ecosystem expansion narrative.

If runner numbers, fees, and buyback volume fail to keep growing, the market may reassess those expectations.

2. Runner revenue may not be sustainable

Agent fees are still largely tied to trading activity.

If the revenue of a few runners comes from short-lived trends, or if the platform cannot consistently reproduce successful cases, the ecosystem revenue we see today could be highly volatile.

3. Attention rotation can reverse quickly

The AI Agent narrative still depends heavily on market sentiment.

When new trends emerge, capital may leave the AgencyPad ecosystem. Even if the product continues operating, the token may not be able to maintain its previous valuation.

4. A working mechanism does not automatically establish long-term value

Buybacks and burns can create buying pressure and reduce token supply, but they do not automatically generate sustainable business growth.

Ultimately, AgencyPad still needs to establish consistent activity, revenue, and user demand.

From here, I see two possible scenarios for the next phase of the market.

If runner numbers continue increasing, fees remain strong, buyback-and-burn volume expands, and market attention does not fade significantly, the rally could still be in the expectation-building phase of ecosystem expansion, leaving room for further valuation re-rating.

But if the price keeps rising while fees and buyback data stagnate, and the rally becomes increasingly dependent on KOL discussions and capital rotation, then it would look more like sentiment-driven valuation expansion. Once attention cools, the risk of a sharp pullback would increase.

For that reason, I would rather wait for further fundamental validation than simply chase a market cap breakout.

The three things I will focus on next are:

Whether AgencyPad continues producing new high-revenue runners.

Whether actual Agency buyback-and-burn volume grows alongside ecosystem activity.

Whether capital and attention remain concentrated in AgencyPad instead of quickly rotating into the next AI Agent trend.

The core change in Agency is that it is evolving from an AI Agent token with a product concept into a project with an initial economic feedback mechanism and real ecosystem activity.

That makes it much more interesting than when I first researched it.

But from a trading perspective, what will truly determine its next phase is not the tokenomics upgrade that has already happened, but whether the growth the market is expecting can continue to materialize.

What I am trading from here is whether AgencyPad can turn this mechanism into a continuously operating ecosystem.

text:
convergence to the mean

when everyone looks at everyone else to decide what to make, we eventually stop making anything of our own.

we copy what works. borrow the language, the aesthetic, the features. we call it learning from the market, following best practices, staying competitive. together, everything starts to feel familiar. polished, interchangeable. nothing wrong. nothing alive.

the mean isn’t necessarily bad. it’s where everything lands when we remove the reasons for it to be different.

numbers are easier to compare than feelings, so we make things that produce numbers. we study what gets attention, then shape ourselves around it. eventually the feedback stops informing the work and starts authoring it. we’re no longer asking what we want to say. we’re asking what will be rewarded for saying.

ai makes this loop frictionless. it can draw from more references than we could see in a lifetime. but access to every perspective isn’t the same as having one. it hasn’t lived a particular life that makes one detail unbearable and another beautiful. when we ask it to choose for us without bringing any intention of our own, we get something plausible, easy to approve.

then we ship it, measure it, copy it, and feed it back into the next round. a tidal wave of mid.

this changes not just the work, but the people making it.

we describe ourselves in categories platforms can distribute and markets understand. designer. founder. creator. pick a niche. build a brand. be consistent. the parts that don’t fit become inconvenient, even when those contradictions might produce our most interesting work. we become easier to classify and harder to tell apart.

i think we need to approach making things more like artists.

an artist develops a perspective through the work. making, noticing, choosing, failing, returning. learning what matters even when nobody else cares. craft gives that perspective a form precise enough for someone else to experience.

the life outside the work matters too. the places you’ve lived, the people you’ve loved, the things you’re embarrassed to care about. these aren’t distractions from having something to say. they’re how you come to have something to say.

we understand this with music, paintings, photographs, movies. we expect a person to be present in the choices. we want to experience something we wouldn’t have encountered without them.

software can do this too.

a piece of software expresses beliefs about how life should feel. what deserves your attention. what you should be free to change. whether a task should feel like paperwork or play. even a small interaction can carry someone’s care, humor, or curiosity.

but we rarely talk about software as a medium. we talk about it as an industry. markets to capture, workflows to optimize, competitors to catch up with. we add a feature because someone else has it, without asking whether it belongs. products accumulate the same parts and lose what made them worth choosing.

underneath the branding, it’s all the same thing.

artists learn from others too. the question is whether you’re absorbing those influences into a point of view, or using them to avoid developing one.

what are you trying to let someone feel, understand, or do? why this particular shape? what have you noticed that the existing tools don’t seem to notice?

those questions don’t have answers you can borrow from a competitor’s roadmap.

if we can make almost anything, deciding what deserves to exist becomes more important, not less. speed gives us more chances to exercise judgment. it doesn’t remove the responsibility.

i don’t want a world where every person becomes a more efficient distributor of the same ideas. i want people to use these tools to go further into what they actually care about. to make things specific enough that we can feel someone behind them.

what is the point of everyone being able to make something, if we all end up making the same thing?

text:
我去！做股票量化机器学习，最浪费时间的往往不是训练模型，而是每天手搓一堆因子。

tsfresh，9.4K Stars，MIT 开源，一套专门把“时间序列特征工程”自动化的 Python 工具。

以前做因子研究，要自己想波动率、峰值、趋势、偏度、频域、相关性，再一个个写代码验证。

tsfresh 不一样，它先从 K 线、成交量、因子序列里批量挖出大量统计特征，再自动筛掉和目标没关系的噪音。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 自动特征提取：统计、趋势、峰值、频域、非线性等数百到上千个特征一次生成

2️⃣ 自动筛因子：内置统计显著性检验，不只是疯狂造特征，还会把无效特征砍掉

3️⃣ 直接接 Pandas / NumPy / scikit-learn，提完特征就能继续训练 LightGBM、XGBoost 等模型

4️⃣ 股票 K 线、成交量、Crypto、传感器等时间序列都能用，不绑某一种数据

5️⃣ 支持并行和 Dask，大规模时间序列也能继续往多核 / 集群扩

6️⃣ 自定义特征也能塞进去，现成因子不够，就把自己的量化逻辑一起接进来

我觉得它最有意思的地方，是把因子研究的顺序反过来了。

以前是：

先凭经验想因子 → 写代码 → 再验证。

现在可以先让 tsfresh 大规模挖一遍，再让统计筛选和模型告诉你，哪些东西真的有信息量。

它不是交易框架，也不会替你预测涨跌。

但如果你做机器学习选股、因子挖掘、时间序列预测或者 Crypto 量化，这种“自动造因子 + 自动筛因子”的工具非常省时间。

仓库：https://t.co/sb3SCCDlky
author: _zheergen
quoted_text:
TradingView 的 Pine Script 生态，终于有人整理成了一份真正能当导航站用的开源清单了

awesome-pinescript，1.9K Stars，MIT 开源，一份专门收集 Pine Script 指标、策略、工具和自动交易资源的仓库。

以前学 Pine 脚本，最烦的是东拼西凑：官方文档一套、社区脚本一套、指标合集一套、自动下单又是一套。

它不一样，从 2020 年维护到现在，把官方资源、社区、指标、策略、库、自动下单、开发工具、学习资料分门别类全收进去，每个还带一句话说明。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 官方资料：Pine Script v4 / v5 / v6 文档、语言参考、更新日志都整理好了

2️⃣ 指标合集：趋势、成交量、Market Profile、相关性、VIX、周期分析等大量公开指标

3️⃣ Screener：板块异动、超买超卖、批量股票扫描、TradingView Screener 工具都有

4️⃣ 策略模板：MACD、均线交叉、止盈止损、Portfolio Backtesting 等现成策略可以直接研究

5️⃣ 自动交易：整理了 Python、JavaScript、Webhook、Telegram、交易机器人等执行方案

6️⃣ 开发资源：Libraries、代码工具、Style Guide、Best Practices 和学习教程都集中在一起

它最值钱的是自动下单那一栏——大部分人卡在指标画出来了，但怎么接实盘这一步，这里把 Python / JS / PHP / Chrome 各种开源桥接方案都给你列好了。

找指标、找策略、找 Screener、找自动下单方案，先来这里翻一遍，能省不少时间。

做 TradingView、Pine Script、量化策略或者自动交易的，这个建议直接收藏。

text:
其实这个事没那么复杂。

币安从一开始就很清楚，Opinion 是来干嘛的。

和过往其他项目一样，万卉攒 Opinion 的目的很简单：出货套现，没打算运营。（上次看到有人埋伏 $OPN，就挺可爱的……人万卉早就奔着下一个项目去了，怎么可能还花钱拉盘。）

但预测市场这个赛道，币安又需要一个真正做事的项目。
所以 Opinion TGE 当天，YZi Labs 就宣布投资 https://t.co/T7qWs3mgIV，同时 pf 又把另一个预测市场并了进去。

 今天看到的一切，其实从最开始就已经写好了。
author: MysticXBT
quoted_text:
倪大说的还是太含蓄了，我接着展开讲讲吧，Opinion不论是币价还是业务表现的如此拉胯，情理之外又意料之中。先说为什么情理之外，因为Opinion可以说开局摸到了一手王炸，赶上预测市场的巅峰，并且拿到了YZi Labs投资，还在TGE的时候全部大满贯，关键！关键来了，Opinion全员反撸骂声一片，而根据“惯例”一般背景牛逼但是又舍不得散出筹码的项目，都会走高控筹拉盘路线，所以这也就是为什么很多人会在二级不断抄底的原因，可结局却是越抄越跌，Opinion也成了我印象中极少数大满贯高控筹顶着骂声不拉盘的项目。

那为什么说这个看似情理之外的结局却又是意料之中呢？

倪大在推文中已经提到了“挺早的时候我和 4XLabs 的小伙伴就已经接触过 Opinion ，等到市场完全火了以后 $OPN 就是一票难求了”。

在预测市场还没火起来的时候，我们接触过项目团队并进行过几次会议交流看是否有合作的机会，当时对方情绪低迷并且焦虑，因为那时候手里真的没有什么牌，某种程度可以说是相对草根普通的小项目，还在纠结要不要从Monad跳到BSC上，当时我印象很深，我正在高架上一边开车一边说“一定要去BSC！”。

后面也陆续和团队有过接触，但一直没有确定下来合作，直到有一天CZ突然在推特说要支持预测市场的项目，于是全网所有人都疯了一样到处找BSC上哪里有预测市场。

嗯？有个叫Opinion的项目。

后来的事情大家也都知道了，Opinion成了稀里糊涂就站到风口上的猪。

涌进去了大量撸毛人贡献上千万美金的手续费。

同时VC们也一起抬轿子投钱投资源。

这时候就到了倪大说的“一票难求”时期，我们跟项目合作的机会那是高攀不起了，最后只厚着脸皮舔了一点KOL轮，而Opinion也最终成了唯2的花钱打工最后都没回本的项目🤣

而其中倪大是最受伤的，这里就不展开了，反正是段挺憋屈的经历。

那时候我们私下聊天都说已经感觉到项目团队好像有点“飘”。

其实这也是很正常的，假设你是一个艰难创业默默无名的小项目，突然有一天眼睛睁开佛光普照到了你的身上，万众瞩目，你的心态也会发生变化吧。

后来的故事大家也知道了，全员反撸，币价下跌，业务沉寂。

一开始我们还以为项目方想故意洗盘憋个大的，毕竟大部分背景牛逼但高度控筹的项目，都会阴跌一段时间，然后突然爆空单拉盘以涨服人。

于是我们投了钱进去拿到的币，一个都没卖。

直到跌麻了坐不住了，我们开始问到底怎么回事？

项目方完全不回应，从已读未回，变成未读未回。

我们也从期待，变成了疑惑，再到焦躁，最后到愤怒。

而据我所知，Opinion在TGE后还拒绝了一个主动找上门的头部一线交易所的合作，给出的理由是“在忙其他的事”。

但时至今日，也不知道到底忙出来了个什么事。

其实现在想明白了，在TGE前稀里糊涂得到的这一切对于项目方来说，早就已经远远超出了他们自己的预期，所以不论币价跌不跌，业务做不做，每一天，都是最好的一天，都是曾经梦寐以求遥不可及的一天。

如果你的能力和格局就只是开一个小卖部，突然有一天走了狗屎运，你的小卖部被拆迁赔了一大笔钱，你绝对不会想着怎么用这笔钱把规模做大开成连锁超市，因为你从来就没这么想过。

虽然雷军的名言是风口上的猪都能飞起来，但投资一定是投人，一定要投那些靠自己的实力勇攀高峰爬到山顶的创业者，而不是被一阵风吹上天的猪，因为靠自己爬上去的人，会非常珍惜所得到的，而靠风吹上天的，即便摔死了也会觉得能上一次天这辈子值了。

1、油价方面：

美军护航部分油轮集中通过海峡，沙特阿美快速恢复每日通过东西输油管道输送约600万桶原油，约有450万桶/日的管道流量可用于出口。市场有实际出口能力正在恢复的预期。

同时G7领导人同意通过IEA协调释放1亿桶柴油和其他石油储备，川普也明确表态美国不会实施柴油出口禁令，如果未来两周柴油裂解价差明显回落，会比Brent单独回落更有利于Fed通胀路径。

2）但风险依然在
如1号推文聊到“伊朗应该还保有把某一批船打停的能力”，昨晚英国海上贸易办公室（UKMTO）就报告两艘油轮在海峡被袭击，也就说明了伊朗还有干扰南部航道的能力；
美军还在往中东部署第三支航母战斗群和第三支两栖陆战队远征军部队，威胁中期选举后动武；
同时沙特明显从前几周的“防御 + 空袭”往“准备改变地面控制线”推进。看路透社报道沙特开始认真筹划曼德海峡沿岸反攻计划。

这些都让昨晚油价出现V反、先跌再涨。
油价就在“航线可能恢复”和“战争升级”之间摇摆。

2、长债方面
油价又起来，然后长期资本成本、财政供给、期限溢价这些仍很高，所以美债收益率昨晚也是先跌后涨。

在现在这个位置上、长债收益率越往上市场压力也越大。

但另一方面，经纪名义GDP增速还可以，AI产业也还在继续快速进化（引用推文里有梳理最近一段时间产业上的进展），这种情况下基本面好盈利强劲业绩预期兑现节奏快的标的是能扛住宏观逆风的，而且稍有缓和就容易往上蹦。这也是有人感到最割裂的地方、看债市觉得摇摇欲坠、看道指、标普等权、罗素2000弱的一逼、但看纳指则是稳步震荡向上、核心就在这里。

所以这也是我在引用的推文聊的“当下市场最害怕的是收益率快上往上飙；
如果能稳住、市场也会缓缓；
现在的市场并不需要收益率大幅跌，只需要稳定小幅回落、那么那些业绩没问题股票就能起来，之前被收益率压制的板块也能起来。

所以综合起来就是：
1）当下收益率水平部分强势标的能扛住，如果长债收益率还要快速往上飙升，小盘股、价值股还得继续泄，AI和大科技也会被压制； 

2）如果us10Y不能稳定下来（当下位置震荡），那么AI半导体和大科技里逻辑最硬的标的还是能扛住，还能震荡向上，碰到有波动调整逢低买。

3）但如果5.2~5.3%开始成为新的均衡水平，在这个基础上如果能小幅回落，估值受到的边际压力会明显减弱，那么不仅AI科技板块继续走强，而且资金可能开始从少数半导体、AI科技龙头向银行、周期和部分中小盘扩散。 

当然更重要的点是10月下旬大科技的三季度财报陆续出来，市场应该会看到AI商业化进程还是远超预期的，美股基本面还是第一位的。

text:
The London Mathematical Society is currently surveying all editorial board members of all nine LMS journals (I am on the editorial board of two). This is part of a consultation on AI and publishing that will help determine changes to the LMS’s AI policy.

The survey has 36 questions and presents a range of positions on AI, including some fairly extreme ones—on issues such as how to treat papers predominantly drafted with the help of AI, or papers written by someone without expertise in the relevant research area, or how detailed AI declarations must be—and asks editorial board members to rate their agreement with each.

After the survey closes, there will be three online town halls for editorial board members to share and discuss their views on these issues.

I hope that, following the consultation, the LMS will adopt a sensible policy that is pro-AI and upholds Mertonian norms rather than the interests of a section of the mathematical community.
author: skominers
quoted_text:
As an editor of two prominent mathematics journals and a professor in a large mathematics department at a research-intensive university, I have a bird’s-eye view of how mathematicians are reacting to AI. 

My view is that the damage currently being done to mathematics is not due to AI, but to mathematicians’ reaction to it. Many of these reactions are self-serving and collectivist, and demonstrate a failure to think clearly about the future.

AI is a revolutionary technology unlike anything we have created before. Many claims made by AI sceptics, AI accelerationists and AI doomers alike are poorly evidenced; they pay insufficient attention to liberal epistemology and to the relationship between intelligence and power. AI could enormously expand what humans can know and do. To realize this promise, we need to be open to empirical evidence and be willing to solve difficult problems.

I will have an essay coming out tomorrow that goes into some of these ideas in more detail.

author: ZhanweiC
quoted_text:
看到小姑娘的建议，稍微补充一下：

1. 临时的新加坡本地网络和电话有两种，一种是只有流量的，基本都是 esim 这种不需要 KYC ，但也不能打电话和收短信，只能提供流量，总的来说就是没有 +65 的功能。

另一种就是游客卡，主要就是短期的，需要 KYC ，可以在 7-11 等买，或者直接在机场买也可以，可以获得 +65 的功能。

对于部分小伙伴来说，买一个然后注册一些网站是可以的，这种卡一般最多用30天。

推荐用 Singtel 的游客卡，大概 10新币（53人民币不到）、7天有效期、500GB 新加坡/马来西亚/印尼/泰国/香港流量，5G，并包含本地无限通话和短信。实体 SIM 和 eSIM 都有。

非常适合在新加坡以后想要去马来西亚的小伙伴，可以不用换卡了，直接就能在马来西亚用。

2. 入境卡一定要填写，非常快，很好写，基本上填好后 30 分钟内就能收到邮件，收到邮件就可以过关了，新加坡过关效率很高，不用担心。

新加坡过海关不需要小费，没有任何的人工检索通道（小黑屋除外），都是自动机器，非常快。

3. 新加坡入境不能带电子烟，千万别带，电子烟在新加坡是违法的，最好也不要带烟，新加坡烟草管制非常严格，从来不存在一个人可以带 X 支烟这样的说法，哪怕带一根都需要申报。

我知道会有小伙伴会说自己每次都偷偷带，对，不被发现是没事，但如果被发现就会比较麻烦，尤其是带多了点就会当走私处理了。

另外进入新加坡可以带酒，一般来说 500ML 的白酒可以带两瓶，威士忌可以带 1L ，喜欢喝酒的小伙伴出来海关酒可以看到卖酒的，价格还算可以，如果有打折的话当年茅台大概是 230 多新币，没打折的话大概小 300 新币吧。

新加坡买烟在超市也可以买，但烟不会摆在外边，需要自己和售货员说，然后才能买，我不抽烟，所以也不知道都有什么品牌，听说基本都是万宝路。

4. 新加坡换钱挺容易的，汇率也还算过的去，在牛车水（中国街）有很多换汇公司，甚至可以从微信换成新币，也可以把人民币寄回中国，但听说偶尔会出现冻卡。

我个人建议来新加坡还是要带一些现金的，因为并不是所有地方都可以刷信用卡，尤其是小贩中心或者食阁，如果没有新加坡本地的支付方式，现金是最好的。

汇率大概是不到 5.3 元人民币换 1 新币，一般来说小贩中心或者亚坤这类的吃吃一个人大概要 15 新币左右，如果是食阁的话，一碗面大概是 6 新币，一份蛋炒饭大概是 5.5 新币，一份海南鸡大概是 8 新币。

另外新加坡的地铁可以直接用 VISA 和 Mastercard卡，刷了就可以走，应该是按距离收费的，起手点应该是 1 新币左右，我基本做一站都是 1.0X 新币左右。

5. 很多短视频都有介绍新加坡的规矩特别多，动不动就罚款，也对，也不对，确实规矩很多，但也不是非常容易被罚款，一般来说第一次发现都是会警告一下，比如室外没有在规定的地方抽烟。

对，新加坡地铁，公交和出租车上都不能吃东西和喝水，有时候出租车还好，但公众交通如果被发现，对方还是较真的人，确实是挺麻烦的。

总的来说自己都认为不是好事的，就别做，那就肯定没错了。

6. 新加坡的打车其实非常容易，但刚刚来新加坡可能会觉得不方便，首先是打车不能扬招，其次打车都需要去打车点（pickup point），没有在的话，就要自己找，另外新加坡打车基本上有 3 分钟的等待时间，超过时间就要扣超时费。

新加坡最好用的还是 Grab ，尤其是从机场出来的时候，Grab 的性价比要高于出租车，Grab 可以绑定信用卡，而且在新加坡还可以用 USDT 充值（我不记得游客是否可以了），总之 Grab 是挺好用的。

如果看到司机是华人面孔可以尝试说中文，大多数都会讲中文，如果是看到印度裔等那就只能说英文了。

7. 在新加坡大多数的路边店是没有什么“服务”概念的， 尤其是吃饭的时候别指望能有多周到的服务，但相比香港还是强多了，当然也会有部分服务员素质不高的情况，能不吵架尽量就别吵架。

一般的饭店都有 10% 的服务费 和 9% 的税，都含在账单里的，所以不用给小费。新加坡几乎没有小费文化。

8. 如果在新加坡有什么问题，而且恰好你又有我的联系方式，可以联系我，力所能及的帮忙还是没问题的。

还有什么是我遗漏的？

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场

text:
$ZC From the Snowmoon Literary Narrative to a Repricing of the Ethereum Privacy Ecosystem

0x4e67db19044549ff420860834c91b45bad298722 

ZC rebounded from a previous market cap low of around $5M, climbing back above $25M and briefly touching nearly $30M. A rally of almost 5x is clearly more than a simple technical recovery.

I believe the most important change behind this rally is that the market is shifting how it values ZC.

Initially, the market was buying into the narrative surrounding Vitalik’s Snowmoon novel and the connection between Zipcoin in the story and the real-world ZC token. Now, however, the market is beginning to focus on the privacy payment products Zipcoin is building and whether it has the potential to become a connecting layer within the Ethereum privacy ecosystem.

The core of this rally is not the emergence of an entirely new narrative, but the fact that the original narrative is now gaining support from product development and external attention.

So we need to ask one question: What has actually changed during this rally?

I believe there are three developments worth paying attention to.

First, the product has gradually evolved from a literary concept into a set of usable privacy tools.

Zipcoin’s original product idea was to turn the concepts in Snowmoon—private money, anonymous payments, and publishing messages by burning tokens—into on-chain functionality.

Today, it is no longer just a simple conceptual demonstration. Users can deposit and withdraw assets through Privacy Pools, send private assets to zkmoney accounts, publish messages that remain permanently on-chain through Burn to Speak, and send messages to specific addresses or ENS names through Doorstep, with an economic cost attached.

More importantly, Zipcoin is attempting to connect private assets on Ethereum with Aztec’s private balance system.

This expands its product direction beyond simple anonymous transfers into private payments, message publishing, and private fund transfers.

Second, external attention is beginning to emerge.

Previously, zkmoney publicly mentioned Zipcoin’s use cases, including using Zipcoin to privately fund zkmoney accounts. Later, Trent Van Epps, who has been involved in work related to the Ethereum Foundation, publicly asked how to contact the team.

These developments should not be overinterpreted. A mention from zkmoney does not constitute an official endorsement. Trent’s interaction does not mean the Ethereum Foundation is involved with or supports ZC, and Vitalik has not endorsed the token either.

However, I still think these events matter.

They suggest that Zipcoin’s product direction is beginning to attract attention from people connected to the Ethereum privacy ecosystem, rather than remaining a topic discussed exclusively among Meme traders.

For a project still at an early stage, attention from potential users, developers, and ecosystem participants may be more valuable than exposure on social media alone.

Third, the product narrative is expanding from private transfers toward a broader privacy ecosystem.

On October 2, the team launched chatzipcoincash, an attempt to let users interact with AI models using private funds while incorporating payment privacy into the product.

This direction is worth watching because it extends Zipcoin’s private payment capabilities into AI use cases.

If AI Agents, individual users, and application developers eventually need to pay for services without exposing their complete wallet histories, private payments could become a broader infrastructure requirement.

However, this product is still experimental. Its actual user numbers and sustained usage have not yet been sufficiently verified. For now, it is more of a new narrative entry point than an established growth engine.

I believe the market is no longer betting solely on Vitalik’s literary narrative. Instead, it is beginning to price in three more specific expectations.

First, can Zipcoin become a connecting layer within the Ethereum privacy ecosystem?

Various privacy tools already exist on Ethereum, but there are still usability barriers between private funds, private payments, and real-world applications.

Zipcoin is attempting to connect 0xbow’s Privacy Pools, zkmoney, private AI payments, and on-chain messaging.

If it can make it easier for users to move funds between these systems while consistently attracting real users, it could evolve from a niche privacy application into a product with some degree of network effects.

The market may already be pricing in this potential positioning.

However, connecting different protocols does not mean inheriting their users, nor does it guarantee that Zipcoin will capture the economic value generated by those protocols.

Second, privacy demand could expand into new use cases.

Private payments are not just about hiding transaction histories.

For fund managers, on-chain traders, AI Agents, and commercial applications, protecting the origin of funds, payment relationships, and wallet histories can all have practical value.

In particular, the development of AI Agents could create new demand for private financial transactions. When Agents pay API fees, transfer funds to other Agents, or execute commercial tasks, they may not want every aspect of their financial activity to be publicly visible.

Zipcoin’s CLI and MCP tools already provide some capabilities for Agents, including private payments, anonymous message publishing, and fund transfers.

This gives its product direction the potential to intersect with the AI Agent ecosystem.

However, this remains a potential market opportunity rather than a proven source of demand.

Third, ZC could evolve from a narrative-driven token into an asset with real product usage feedback.

This is what I consider the most important—and also the most uncertain—part of the thesis.

Zipcoin’s product design includes token consumption, transaction taxes, and buyback-and-burn mechanisms. According to the official documentation, ZC has a fixed supply of 1 billion tokens with no minting capability. Part of the Stockereum transaction tax goes into the Treasury, with half allocated to buybacks and burns and the other half used for rewards, giveaways, and operating costs.

This means product usage has the potential to generate economic activity connected to the token.

But token consumption does not equal sustained external demand, and buybacks and burns do not automatically create stable value growth.

What really matters is whether users are willing to use ZC continuously to access the product’s functionality, and whether that usage can reach meaningful economic scale.

If product usage continues to grow, the token’s economic activity could gradually become less dependent on speculative trading.

On the other hand, if most demand still comes from traders speculating on the possibility of a future privacy ecosystem, ZC will remain an asset highly dependent on market sentiment.

Based on the information above, my assessment is that the product fundamentals are improving, but the certainty of token value capture has not improved at the same pace.

Compared with before, Zipcoin now has more usable products, a more complete set of private payment use cases, and growing attention from relevant parts of the ecosystem.

These are genuine product developments.

However, I would not equate an increase in product functionality with a mature business model.

According to the official documentation, Zipcoin’s own privacy pool remains relatively small. A small privacy pool limits anonymity based on the number of participants and the timing of transactions. Even when users employ zero-knowledge proofs, they may not achieve strong practical privacy.

This exposes Zipcoin’s most fundamental product challenge: the value of a privacy tool depends not only on whether the technology works, but also on how many people actually use it.

In addition, the team has previously changed how protocol fees are allocated. As shown in the screenshots, the original 10% protocol-fee buyback mechanism has been revised, with more funds now directed toward development, ecosystem growth, and privacy initiatives.

This means I no longer consider protocol-fee buybacks the most important part of the current bullish thesis.

Allocating funds toward product development and ecosystem expansion may benefit the project over the long term, but it also weakens the market’s previous expectation that protocol fees would directly support demand for the token.

It is important to distinguish between team-initiated burns, protocol-fee buybacks, and organic token consumption generated by users. These are not the same economic activity.

I care much more about organic demand generated by actual product usage than burns executed by the team.

So the question everyone cares about is: What are the potential catalysts for further upside?

I believe the next stage is less about expanding the narrative and more about concrete events that can prove demand is growing.

1. Significant growth in privacy pool deposits and transaction volume

This is the metric I care about most.

If Zipcoin’s privacy pool deposits can grow consistently from their current small scale and gradually form a larger anonymity set, that would provide stronger evidence of the product’s real value.

In particular, sustained usage from wallets outside the team would be more convincing than a short-term concentration of deposits.

If deposits eventually grow from dozens of transactions to hundreds or more, accompanied by consistent fund flows, the market may begin to reassess Zipcoin’s level of product adoption.

2. Real transactions through ZipTeller and private payments

Zipcoin’s ability to connect with zkmoney is an important differentiator from ordinary privacy Memes.

If we begin to see sustained private payments rather than merely demonstration transactions, the product could start developing real-world use cases.

I would pay particular attention to payment frequency, transaction amounts, active users, and repeat usage.

These metrics are more valuable than simply announcing new partnerships or integrations.

3. Real users for Private AI Chat

Private AI payments are a promising new direction, but there is still insufficient adoption data.

If the product can attract recurring users, generate consistent payment demand, and create real interactions with Zipcoin’s private financial infrastructure, it could become a new source of growth.

On the other hand, if its launch generates only short-term discussion without sustained usage, its contribution to ZC fundamentals will remain limited.

4. A concrete roadmap and execution from the team

Market expectations for Zipcoin have already expanded considerably.

The next roadmap needs to provide clearer delivery timelines, specific features, and details on how the revised protocol-fee allocation will be implemented.

I would not increase my long-term valuation expectations simply because the project announces an advisor. What matters is who the advisor is, what resources they can contribute, and whether those resources ultimately translate into product adoption or ecosystem partnerships.

5. Meaningful engagement from Vitalik or the core Ethereum ecosystem

Vitalik remains the most distinctive narrative variable for this project.

Since Snowmoon is part of Zipcoin’s cultural origins, any future discussion of the product or its technology by Vitalik could attract significant market attention again.

However, I would treat this as an additional potential catalyst rather than the core investment thesis.

ZC is not Vitalik’s token, and there is no official endorsement connecting the literary narrative to the real-world project. Sustainable value must ultimately come from the product and its users.

The biggest risk: The market may be paying in advance for adoption that has not happened yet

From a trading perspective, I believe the biggest risk for ZC right now is the gap between valuation expectations and actual product usage.

First, user adoption may fall far short of market expectations.

The product is becoming more complete, and the narrative continues to expand. But if privacy pool activity, private payment transactions, and Private AI user growth fail to improve meaningfully, the market may be overestimating the scale of the future ecosystem.

Second, privacy products carry technical and trust-related risks.

Zipcoin’s newly added contracts have not yet undergone independent audits. The Entrypoint proxy contract still relies on a trust assumption involving the Treasury key’s upgrade authority. The small size of the privacy pool also weakens practical anonymity.

For a project built around privacy, technical security and trust are especially important. A security incident would not only hurt the token price but could also undermine the product’s core value proposition.

Third, token value capture may lag behind product growth.

Even if Zipcoin’s products attract a large number of users, that does not mean ZC will benefit proportionally.

We still need to monitor the actual relationship between fees, token consumption, buybacks, and Treasury spending. If product growth primarily generates funds for ecosystem development rather than sustained demand for the token, product success and token appreciation could remain disconnected.

Fourth, the current rally may have already priced in too many future catalysts.

From around $5M to nearly $30M, the market has already assigned a significant premium to privacy product expansion, external attention, and potential ecosystem growth.

If adoption data fails to support these expectations, the market could enter a phase where expectations remain high but actual results lag behind.

This is especially risky in a relatively thin market, where a shift in attention or large-scale selling could trigger a sharp pullback.

I would not directly conclude that ZC has substantial upside simply because it has integrated with 0xbow and zkmoney or launched Private AI Chat.

These developments expand the market’s imagination, but the real drivers of a sustained valuation re-rating will still be users, transactions, and recurring economic activity.

If deposits continue to grow, private payments begin to see genuine demand, and the AI product attracts a stable user base, the market may shift from speculating on a potential privacy ecosystem to valuing an emerging network of privacy applications.

That transition could support a more sustainable next leg higher.

But if the roadmap continues to progress and product features keep expanding while actual user growth remains weak, ZC may still depend primarily on narrative and capital rotation to sustain its valuation.

So the thing I care about most next is not the next announcement. It is whether Zipcoin can prove that the premium the market is currently willing to pay for its privacy ecosystem can eventually translate into real users and sustained demand.

That will determine whether ZC is simply a successful narrative re-rating or has the potential to become an Ethereum privacy project with genuine long-term value.

ethereum:0x4e67db19044549ff420860834c91b45bad298722 has already delivered a 1x return since its first day of posting on X, and the project is gradually shifting from its early literary narrative based on Vitalik’s Snowmoon toward a privacy application narrative supported by a real product and external attention.

0x4e67db19044549ff420860834c91b45bad298722 

It is not Vitalik’s token, and Vitalik has not endorsed it. The project’s core idea is to turn the privacy payments and burn-to-send-message concepts of Zipcoin in Snowmoon into an actual product on Ethereum.

In terms of its product, ZC has already built several core features:

Zip / Unzip: Users deposit ZC into a Privacy Pool and then withdraw it to a new wallet using a zero-knowledge proof, reducing the direct link between the depositing and withdrawing addresses.

Burn to Speak: Users burn ZC to publish on-chain messages. The amount of ZC burned affects the message’s ranking.

Doorstep: Users send messages to ENS names or wallet addresses by burning ZC to get the recipient’s attention. They can also attach private transfers.

ZipTeller: Connects private funds with zkmoney and supports private fund operations for zkmoney accounts.

These features mean ZC is no longer just a Meme borrowing a literary concept. It is a literary narrative token backed by an actual product. However, having a working product does not mean its privacy capabilities are mature, nor does it mean the market has developed real demand.

The most important recent development is the emergence of external attention. zkmoney has publicly mentioned Zipcoin and discussed using Zipcoin to fund zkmoney accounts privately. Meanwhile, the team has expanded the fund flow to the 0xbow ETH Privacy Pool, attempting to use a larger ETH privacy pool and then convert the funds into private DAI on zkmoney.

This means ZC is extending from an independent privacy application toward an entry point that connects with existing privacy infrastructure. Compared with demonstrations published by the team itself, attention and integration initiated by external products carry greater validation value.

However, external mentions and actual adoption are two different things. Although the number of deposits in the Privacy Pool has increased from around 9 to around 19, and wallets outside the team have begun using Burn to Speak, the overall scale remains small. External transaction volume through ZipTeller is also insufficient to demonstrate stable demand.

In terms of token mechanics, ZC already has fee, buyback, and burn mechanisms. Trading fees can flow into the treasury to support buybacks, burns, and development. Operations such as Zip and Unzip also have their own fees.

The theoretical cycle is:Trading volume growth → More fees → Buybacks and burns → Reduced circulating supply.

However, growth in trading fees mainly reflects token trading activity. It does not directly prove that the product is attracting real users. Compared with buybacks funded by trading activity, user-initiated burns resulting from actual product use provide stronger evidence of product demand.

Previously, around 8.5% of the supply had been burned, while approximately 4% of the supply was held at the vitalik.eth address. Most of the large early burns came from the team and developers. The tokens sent to Vitalik’s address were also not purchased by him voluntarily.

Therefore, these figures reinforce the market narrative more than they demonstrate organic adoption.

The market narrative is changing. The first wave of price action mainly traded the connection between Snowmoon and Vitalik. Now, zkmoney’s public mention and product integration have provided ZC with a new signal of external validation.

If more privacy wallets, Ethereum developers, and applications actively integrate with ZC in the future, it could gradually evolve from a literary-concept Meme into a privacy ecosystem asset with practical use cases.

But if external attention does not translate into sustained product usage, the market may continue to rely primarily on narrative premiums.

After rebounding from a market cap of around $5M to the previous high range of approximately $18M–$20M, ZC has already completed a significant first revaluation. At this stage, it is not enough to focus only on a price breakout. Product usage data must also be considered to determine whether the market has new fundamental support.

In my view, the main risks remain user adoption, privacy security, and token value capture. The small number of Privacy Pool participants limits the actual anonymity set. Some new components have not yet been audited, and the Entrypoint can still be upgraded. Growth in product usage also does not necessarily translate directly into value for the ZC token.

In addition, if interest in Snowmoon and Vitalik-related topics cools down before external user growth picks up, ZC could return to being a narrative trade heavily dependent on market sentiment.

My core view: ZC has completed the first step from a literary concept to an actual product. The recent public mention and product connection with zkmoney represent an important development in moving from team-driven validation toward external attention.

However, it has not yet demonstrated that real user demand has reached a meaningful scale.

The first wave traded the story of Vitalik and Snowmoon. For the next stage to support a more sustained market revaluation, the key requirement is real growth in product usage.

The most important things to watch next are whether Privacy Pool deposits grow from a few dozen to dozens or even hundreds, whether wallets outside the team continue to use Zip, Unzip, and Burn to Speak, and whether ZipTeller can generate stable external payment activity.

External attention is the catalyst. Real user growth is the core variable for ZC’s next stage.

text:
CNN published a deeply misleading story and headline suggesting that my diplomatic work in the Middle East somehow benefited investments in Israeli defense companies.

But CNN’s own reporting says otherwise. Buried behind a paywall, it acknowledges: “CNN found no indication that Kushner’s actions as a diplomat directly affected the investments reviewed.”

Phoenix is not a defense company. It is one of Israel’s  largest publicly traded financial institutions, highly regulated and managing approximately $220 billion across thousands of investments. 

Think of Phoenix as the Israeli equivalent of Vanguard or Fidelity. It manages the retirement savings of millions of Israelis. The savers don’t choose the individual investments, and neither do I. I have no role in deciding what Phoenix buys or sells. It has performed very well for Affinity and our investors, up more than five times since our initial investment.

Affinity is an SEC-registered investment firm. Our investment in Phoenix is public and dates to before President Trump was re-elected and before I returned to public service. Affinity does not own the defense companies highlighted in CNN’s story.

Those facts make for a less provocative headline, but a much more accurate story.

Misleading stories will not distract me from the work President Trump asked me to do: help end wars, bring people together and pursue peace. That work is too important.

最近我把自己之前拿回来的 TORTILLA/frBTC LP 重新做了一遍资产配置。

这次我真正想测试的，不是简单的“哪个池子 APR 高”，而是一个更有意思的问题：

一笔已经在 Bitcoin 主网上的原生资产，能不能通过一个完整的协议飞轮，最终变成「回本后的长期零成本收益仓」？

我现在越来越觉得 https://t.co/wqTo7b5rH4 / CHEESE 这一套值得长期跟踪。

先讲清楚整个机制。

我手里的资产是 TORTILLA/frBTC LP。

把 LP 放进 CHEESE Vault 后，会发生三件事：

第一层：赚 SLICE。

整个 TORTILLA Vault 一共分配 650,000 SLICE，持续 52,500 个 Bitcoin blocks。

奖励不是最后一次性瓜分，而是每个区块持续释放，然后按照你的 weight 分配。

weight 的核心公式很简单：

净 LP × Lock Multiplier × FIRE Boost

目前几个档位：

3M：1x
6M：1.5x
1Y：2x
Burn：8x

这里最关键的一点是：

3M、6M、1Y 都有同样的 10% LP haircut。

既然进入成本一样，那么如果你本来就准备长期参与，长周期的资本效率其实明显更高。

Burn 更极端。

LP 永久不给你了，但直接拿 8x weight。

所以 Burn 不是传统意义上的锁仓，而更像拿一小部分本金购买协议未来的高杠杆 exposure。

我自己的思路不是 All-in Burn，而是：

大部分仓位用 1Y 获取更高 farming efficiency；

只拿小仓位 Burn，换取一点真正的 convexity；

同时始终留一部分 LP 在外面保持流动性。

第二层：SLICE 最后对应 CHEESE。

SLICE 不是单纯的 farming token。

按照目前机制，它最终是 CHEESE 的 claim。

CHEESE TGE 之后，SLICE 会在 18 个月里逐步成熟为 CHEESE。

基础关系可以理解成：

1 SLICE → 至少 1 CHEESE 的长期 claim。

如果有人提前兑换退出，没有完全成熟的那部分 CHEESE 不会跟着一起离开，而会留给继续持有 SLICE 的人。

所以对于愿意长期持有的人，最终兑换比例理论上存在超过 1:1 的可能性。

这就出现一个很有意思的结构：

短期你可以把一部分 SLICE 卖掉，用来收回本金；

长期则保留另外一部分 SLICE，让它继续变成 CHEESE exposure。

第三层，也是很多人容易忽略的一层：Referral。

https://t.co/wqTo7b5rH4 的邀请码并不是普通的拉人返佣。

当前有一套独立的 Partner Pool。

我的邀请码 LEO 已经在链上处于 active 状态。

而我现在操作 LP 的钱包本身又已经位于：

536 → LEO

这条 referral tree 下面。

也就是说，我自己的仓位在产生 Vault farming reward 的同时，还可以给上层 LEO 增加 Partner weight。

更重要的是，如果未来社区里真的有人通过我的入口长期参与 CHEESE Vault，那么这部分并不占用我的本金，却可以继续增加 Partner Pool exposure。

参与入口：
https://t.co/9HQjQq2pKX

邀请码：LEO

这也是为什么我现在不会只盯着“我这 $1,000 能挖多少”。

真正值得研究的是：

自有本金产生 farming yield；

farming yield 逐步回收本金；

Referral 把自己的内容和社区流量变成第二层收益；

最后留下 CHEESE / LP 的长期零成本仓。

如果最终能做到：

累计卖出的 SLICE + Referral 收益 ≥ 最初本金，

那后面剩下的 LP / SLICE / CHEESE，对我来说才真正进入“house money”阶段。

这才是我想测试的玩法。

当然这里绝对不是无风险套利。

最大的风险并不是 Bitcoin 手续费——现在一笔交易成本其实非常低。

真正需要承担的是：

10% Vault haircut；

锁仓期限；

CHEESE TGE / 协议执行风险；

SLICE、CHEESE 的价格风险；

以及未来更多资金进入以后 farming weight 被稀释。

所以我自己的做法不会是把全部资金无脑锁死。

我的目标只有一个：

先把真实现金流做出来。

我会持续记录：

投入多少 LP；

每天 / 每周实际拿到多少 SLICE；

Referral 给我贡献多少；

实际卖出了多少 BTC / USDT；

什么时候真正完成 100% 本金回收；

以及回本之后剩下的仓位到底还能产生多少收益。

如果这套模型最后真的跑通，我认为它会比单纯“买一个币等涨”有意思很多。

因为最终留下来的不是一个成本价越来越难看的 token 仓位，而是一套已经把本金拿回来的 Bitcoin-native yield position。

我准备长期把这条线公开跟下去。

非投资建议。我自己真金白银参与，也会把收益、亏损和机制变化都持续公开。

text:
Ich fliege heute nach San Fransisco und werde im Flieger sehr viel Zeit haben zu diskutieren :) Habe deswegen mal 12 Punkte aufgeschrieben, die ich als wichtige Herausforderungen unseres Landes verstehe:

1. Strom ist für die Industrie zu teuer. Wer viel Energie braucht, zahlt hier deutlich mehr als in den USA, in China oder in Frankreich und Skandinavien. Aus der Atomkraft sind wir ausgestiegen, bevor genug günstige und jederzeit verfügbare Alternativen standen. Hohe Netzentgelte und Umlagen kommen hinzu.

2. Arbeit ist teuer. Eine Stunde kostet Arbeitgeber im Schnitt rund 45 Euro, etwa 29 Prozent mehr als in der EU. Auch gemessen an der Produktivität liegen die Kosten über dem Schnitt vergleichbarer Länder. Derselbe Handgriff ist anderswo oft billiger. Deshalb entstehen viele Stellen nicht hier.

3. Genehmigungen dauern zu lange. Für größere Anlagen und Fabriken vergehen in der Praxis oft mehr Monate, als das Gesetz vorsieht. Wer nicht weiß, ob und wann er bauen darf, investiert eher woanders.

4. Die Gesellschaft wird älter. Es werden zu wenige Kinder geboren, und die geburtenstarken Jahrgänge gehen in Rente. Auf immer weniger Erwerbstätige kommen immer mehr Rentner und Pflegebedürftige. Beiträge und Abgaben derjenigen, die arbeiten, steigen dadurch weiter.

5. Wir brauchen Zuwanderung in den Arbeitsmarkt, bekommen aber oft nicht die, die sich schnell selbst trägt. Wer zum Arbeiten kommt und etwas kann, entlastet die Kassen. Viele Schutzsuchende kosten aber über Jahre mehr, als sie einzahlen, weil Sprache, Ausbildung und Beschäftigung fehlen. Der Fachkräftemangel ist real, und ungesteuerte Zuwanderung belastet Haushalte und Kommunen.

6. Die Bundeswehr war jahrzehntelang unterfinanziert. Das Nato-Ziel von 2 Prozent wurde lange verfehlt. Personal, Munition und einsatzbereites Gerät fehlen bis heute an vielen Stellen. Die Ausgaben steigen seit 2022 stark. Eine Armee, die das Land im Ernstfall schützen kann, ist damit noch nicht fertig aufgebaut.

7. Die Wirtschaft wächst seit Jahren kaum noch aus eigener Kraft. 2023 und 2024 ist sie geschrumpft, 2025 nur um 0,2 Prozent gewachsen. Die Industrie produziert weniger als vor einigen Jahren. Hohe Steuern, Abgaben und Energiekosten machen das Leben teurer und Investitionen unattraktiver. Sie sind nicht die einzige Ursache. Hinzu kommen schwache Nachfrage, Konkurrenz aus China und zu wenig neue Produkte.

8. Zu viele junge Menschen verlassen die Schule ohne das, was Beruf und Ausbildung brauchen. In Mathematik und beim Lesen erreicht etwa jeder Dritte mit 15 nicht die Grundstufe. Der Abstand zwischen Kindern aus armen und reichen Familien ist so groß wie seit Beginn der PISA-Tests nicht. Gleichzeitig fehlen Lehrkräfte, und viele Schulgebäude sind marode. Wer nicht lesen, rechnen und eine Ausbildung durchhalten kann, fehlt später als Fachkraft.

9. Straßen, Brücken, Schienen und Schulen sind über Jahre zu wenig erneuert worden. Der Investitionsstau der Kommunen liegt bei über 200 Milliarden Euro, Schulen allein bei rund 55 Milliarden. Züge und Lkw stehen im Stau, während neue Werke und Wohnungen auf Anschlüsse warten. Geld ist eingeplant, kommt aber langsam bei den Baustellen an.

10. Wohnen ist in den Städten zu teuer, und es wird zu wenig gebaut. Hohe Mieten fressen Lohn und machen Umzüge dorthin unattraktiv, wo Betriebe Leute suchen. Lange Genehmigungen, teure Auflagen und hohe Zinsen bremsen den Neubau.

11. Der Staat ist langsam, wo er digital sein müsste. Viele Anträge laufen noch auf Papier, Behörden tauschen Daten schlecht aus, und das Internet auf dem Land ist lückenhaft. Das kostet Firmen und Bürger Zeit.

12. Der Staat gibt immer mehr aus, ohne dass die Wirtschaft mitwächst. Rente, Soziales, Zinsen und nun auch Verteidigung und Infrastruktur konkurrieren um dasselbe Geld. Wenn die Schulden schneller steigen als die Wirtschaftsleistung, bleibt später weniger Spielraum für genau die Dinge, die den Standort stärken würden.

Bezahlen tun das am Ende die, die arbeiten.

Wdyt?

text:
Uber publicó cómo armó su infraestructura de MCP y hay varias ideas muy buenas acá.

imaginate una empresa con miles de servicios internos y muchos equipos conectando agentes a esos sistemas por su cuenta.

cuando eso empieza a crecer, terminás con tooling fragmentado, infra duplicada, distintas formas de exponer tools y poca consistencia en seguridad, discovery y operación.

por eso Uber hizo un MCP Gateway: una capa central entre los agentes y sus servicios internos.

el agente habla MCP y el gateway se encarga de routing, permisos, ejecución y de traducir las llamadas a HTTP, gRPC o TChannel según corresponda.

como Uber ya tenía miles de APIs internas, también hicieron AutoCrawler: recorre sus definiciones, detecta métodos y schemas y genera MCP tools automáticamente. incluso usan un LLM para mejorar las descripciones.

hoy tienen +800 MCP servers y +5000 tools. y ahí aparece otro problema: no podés cargar todas esas definiciones en el contexto del modelo.

para eso crearon Omni MCP. en vez de pasarle miles de tools al agente, este va descubriendo qué server necesita, qué tools tiene disponibles, carga el schema de la correcta y recién ahí ejecuta.

me parece un muy buen ejemplo de cómo cambia la arquitectura cuando los agentes pasan de usar unas pocas tools a trabajar con miles.

terminás necesitando algo muy parecido a un API Gateway para agentes.

text:
BTC为什么跌不下去？

明明市场并不缺利空。美债收益率高企、加息预期反复、宏观流动性并不宽松，市场情绪也远没有达到全民狂热的程度。

但奇怪的是：BTC就是跌不深。

这背后可能存在一个经常被忽略的原因：不是买盘特别强，而是卖盘已经不够强。

判断BTC还能不能跌，不能只看有没有利空

这是最近市场一个非常重要的变化。很多投资者习惯这样理解市场：

利空 → BTC应该跌 利好 → BTC应该涨

但真正决定价格短期怎么走的，还有另外一个变量：

到底有多少人愿意在当前价格卖出？

如果卖方非常充足：哪怕买盘一般，价格也可能持续下跌。

但如果卖方已经逐渐枯竭：即使买盘并不强，价格也可能：

跌不动 → 横盘 → 一旦出现增量资金 → 快速上涨。

这也是我最近比较关注的：BTC卖方衰竭指数

这个指标最有价值的地方，是看供应

今年8月当时BTC大约在：63,000美元附近。 

而卖方衰竭指数已经进入历史上的：极端衰竭区

从历史经验来看，当BTC处于熊市末期、卖方衰竭达到极端水平时，往往意味着：愿意继续低价卖出的筹码正在减少。
这并不意味着：明天一定上涨。

而是意味着：

继续大幅下跌需要越来越强的外部力量。

回头看，那个位置确实成为了本轮熊市非常重要的阶段性机会。

为什么卖方衰竭以后，BTC会越来越抗跌？

可以把市场简单理解成一个水池

熊市初期：池子里的水很多。想卖的人很多。所以只需要一点点卖盘，就可以把价格砸下来。

熊市后期：大量恐慌筹码已经卖掉。弱手已经离场。愿意在低价继续卖出的人越来越少。这时候：即使还有利空，也很难找到足够的卖盘。

于是出现一个很有意思的现象：

需求不强 → BTC横盘。 需求稍微增强 → BTC上涨。

这就是为什么有时候我们会看到：利空很多，但价格就是不跌。

这也是为什么最近BTC的抗跌值得关注

前段时间BTC回调到：75,000美元附近。

卖方衰竭指数再次进入相对弱卖压区域。
这个信号非常重要。因为它告诉我们的不是：
75,000一定是最低点。
而是：到了这个区域，继续向下寻找大量卖盘可能变得困难。

这和单纯看K线完全不同。

K线告诉你：价格跌了多少。 

而卖方衰竭指标试图告诉你：还有多少人愿意继续卖。 

两者结合起来，信息量会明显增加。

但是，这个指标不是抄底神器

这是最需要强调的一点。

卖方衰竭：≠ BTC一定上涨。

 因为BTC的价格不仅受到内部供需影响，还会受到外部冲击。

例如：

美联储政策突然转鹰 
美债收益率快速上升 
美元突然走强 
ETF出现持续净流出 
加密市场发生大型清算 大型机构突然减仓 
交易所或稳定币出现信用事件
 地缘政治或金融市场发生黑天鹅

 这些因素都可能突然增加卖压。
所以更准确的理解应该是：

卖方衰竭降低了BTC继续大幅下跌的“内生动力”，但不能消除外部冲击。

真正值得警惕的，反而是指标重新进入极端区
过去一段时间，这个指标反复进入绿色区域。

意味着：卖方相对弱。 但它并没有重新回到8月11日那种极端衰竭状态。

这其实透露出一个重要信息：

市场已经从寻找熊底，进入了上涨后的震荡与再定价。

一旦BTC已经走出熊底，卖方衰竭指标往往很难再次回到最极端的位置。

因此：等待一个和8月11日完全一样的信号再买，可能是一种危险的思维。

投资中最容易犯的错误：把下一次机会当成必然存在
这也是这次复盘让我感触最深的地方

当时可以有两种选择：

A：已经出现极端衰竭信号，先建立仓位。

 B：我再等等，下一次极端信号出现再买。

问题是：谁规定一定会有下一次？

市场不会因为你没有准备好，就重新给你一次同样的价格。

如果BTC真正进入新周期：

63,000美元可能不会再出现。

甚至：75,000美元，也可能成为以后回头看的低点。

所以：等待更完美的价格，本身也是一种风险。  这并不意味着现在应该无脑追涨

恰恰相反。卖方衰竭指标最适合解决的问题，不是：现在是不是马上买？

而是：当市场出现机会时，我是不是应该敢于参与？

我的理解是：极端衰竭区：主动建立仓位。

普通衰竭区：回调时增加仓位。

中性区域：持有为主，等待新的供需变化

卖方重新增强：降低风险，重新评估周期。

这样使用，比把指标当成简单的买/卖信号更有价值。

现在BTC真正值得观察的，不是还有没有利空

而是：利空还能不能制造新的卖盘。

如果未来继续出现：

加息预期→美元走强→美债收益率上升→市场风险偏好下降

但BTC依然：跌不深、快速收回、卖方衰竭指标维持低位

那么这个信号本身就非常值得重视。因为它意味着：市场正在表现出“利空钝化”。

而真正的大行情，很多时候不是从“利好越来越多”开始。而是从：利空越来越多，但价格已经不再下跌。

开始。因为投资中有一个经常被忽略的风险：

你不仅可能买错，也可能等不到下一次机会。

卖方衰竭指标给我的最大启发，不是预测BTC什么时候上涨。

而是让我重新理解：价格为什么有时候跌不动。

当卖方不断枯竭：需求弱，市场横盘；需求稍强，价格上涨；

一旦增量资金出现，上涨可能突然加速。

所以未来我更愿意关注的，不是：BTC什么时候还有一次完美的抄底机会？

而是：

当市场再次出现卖方衰竭时，我有没有准备好？

因为：有花堪折直须折，莫待花落空折枝。

真正的机会，最危险的地方，不是它太贵，而是你总觉得以后还会有更好的价格。

text:
I’ve started moving some of the work I was doing with Hermes directly to the OpenAI app.

Why? Because maintaining all of this by myself is kind of a pain.

I used OpenClaw before and at some point I had to migrate. During that process I lost some data, scripts and context.

Now I have Hermes, which is very powerful, but I still need to care about the storage, keeping things running and all the small things around it. It takes time.

With OpenAI I don’t have to worry about that right now. I can just continue the work there and keep the context.

Of course I am aware of the consequences. They have access to my data, I depend more on them, I have less control and so on. I would not move everything there.

But honestly, for many work things, keeping the context without having to maintain all the infrastructure is starting to make so much more sense.

And now OpenAI is adding durable sessions, sandboxes, computer use, subagents, scheduled work and this new thing they call Dots.

I still don’t know exactly what I will do with Dots, but I wonder how will I be able to use or integrate them in my everyday work.

It feels a bit funny after spending so much time building my own agent systems, but maybe for some things I just don’t want to maintain another system anymore.

quoted_text:
Doing a bit of a self-experiment.

Goal: use my personal health and travel data to provide personalized diet and exercise recommendations for me, using frontier models but in a way that avoids leaking to them any private information.

Strategy: use a local model (Qwen 3.8 Flash Next) to orchestrate, and use powerful remote models as a tool call to benefit from higher-level thinking and knowledge that the local model does not have.

Three-layer approach to privacy:

Avoid leaking personally identifiable information, or leaking my identity through writing style -> local model writes the queries to the frontier model, not me
Avoid leaking who I am through the payment channel -> zkAPI
Avoid leaking who I am through networking / IP -> Tor

You need all three (and finally we have all three, at least to some extent)

A skill file teaches the local model when and how to construct minimally-data-revealing requests to remote models. Use zkAPI-wrapped-with-Tor as a CLI tool.

And everything works! I got the recommendations back, info from frontier models helped to improve them.

Main deficiencies:

* Tor is really not optimized for request-by-request de-linking, which is the only form of network-layer privacy that really makes sense in today's world (long-running identifiers are too fragile). Probably not private enough, and latency 10-100x higher than it could be, at the same time.
* The skill file's request construction strategies are definitely far from optimal.
* Qwen 3.8 Flash Next is still too slow for comfort. It's comfortably running at 20-30 TPS, but it would only really start to feel fast at 100+
* There is a tradeoff: the more careful you are about what data you give to a remote model, the less it can help you

I believe the core driver behind $MASK recent rally is not simply that it is riding the privacy sector’s momentum.

HuAXPyDWDaMYFKuwQHpqL1oPnj93zdzWmtvFGzCeCUa7 

Rather, it has turned a familiar but historically difficult-to-use need into a straightforward product story: no need to switch wallets or change existing habits, just one click to bring privacy to on-chain transactions.

This is exactly what distinguishes it from many privacy projects that exist primarily as concepts. The market is not just buying keywords like ZK and private payments. It is betting on whether MASK can turn complex privacy technology into a tool that ordinary users are actually willing to use.

Looking at the recent price action, MASK started gaining momentum in late September and surged rapidly, with its market cap briefly exceeding $35M in early October. According to recent market reports, its October 2 rally coincided with a broader recovery in the privacy sector, with the token gaining more than 70% in a single day alongside a significant increase in trading volume. At the same time, one of MASK’s major liquidity pools uses a ZEC/MASK trading pair, creating a more direct connection to Zcash’s privacy narrative.

But what interests me more is this: What expectations is this rally actually pricing in? Can Nullmask’s product development support further valuation growth?

First, the privacy narrative has regained market attention.

Privacy has always been a long-standing need in crypto, but it does not become a market narrative that attracts capital in every cycle. Compared with AI, DeFi, or Memes, privacy products are often harder to promote through short-term metrics and user stories.

The recent recovery in attention toward the privacy sector has created a favorable market environment for MASK. Its product positioning is also relatively clear: transaction privacy across wallets and tokens, rather than a single feature built around one specific privacy asset.

As capital starts looking for opportunities in the privacy sector again, a small-cap project like Nullmask, with an easy-to-understand concept and a clear product direction, naturally becomes more likely to attract traders’ attention.

However, sector momentum can explain why capital starts paying attention to MASK, but it cannot fully explain why the token deserves a higher valuation. What really gives it differentiated upside potential is its product narrative.

Second, the one-click privacy experience creates a much larger potential user base in the market’s imagination.

MASK’s website emphasizes a core experience: users can continue using their existing wallets without creating new accounts or managing additional seed phrases, while protecting transaction privacy through a browser extension or application. The project aims to support native tokens, regular tokens, and NFTs, with plans to expand into multichain privacy, programmable privacy, and automated privacy workflows.

The appeal of this narrative lies in its attempt to solve a long-standing problem with privacy tools: the technology may be advanced, but users are often unwilling to accept high operational costs just to gain privacy.

If MASK can truly deliver a low-friction, low-cost, and reliable experience, its potential audience would extend beyond Zcash users to a much broader base of on-chain wallet users.

That would significantly expand the market’s expectations for its potential user base.

But it is important to distinguish between product vision and capabilities that have actually been delivered. The multichain expansion, automated workflows, and programmable privacy described on the website do not mean these features are all fully operational today. The market can price in the future ahead of time, but the fundamentals still need to be verified one by one.

Third, the ZEC/MASK trading pair strengthens its connection to the privacy sector.

MASK has a relatively unusual liquidity structure. Recent market data suggests that a considerable portion of its liquidity is concentrated in the ZEC/MASK trading pair, rather than relying entirely on SOL or stablecoin pairs.

This is not merely a trading decision. It also influences how the market perceives the token.

ZEC is one of the most representative assets in the privacy sector. When MASK forms a direct trading pair with ZEC, the market is more likely to compare it with other privacy-sector projects rather than treat it as an ordinary Solana Meme.

If the privacy sector continues to strengthen, this positioning could help MASK attract additional attention and capital inflows.

However, a trading pair does not automatically create demand. What really matters is whether more users and capital are willing to build sustained trading activity and use cases around MASK.

Fourth, early capital and trader participation amplified price discovery.

When a newly launched token has a relatively small market cap and limited liquidity, capital inflows can have a significant impact on its price.

Recent tracking data showed that MASK started from a market cap of around $1.6M and subsequently recorded a rally of nearly 20x. Some tracked wallets continued buying as the price climbed. This kind of trading structure can attract more short-term traders and further accelerate price discovery.

However, on-chain tracking data only reflects the behavior of specific wallet samples. It does not represent the entire market, nor does it prove that every purchase was made with a long-term holding strategy.

I would interpret it this way: early capital provided the conditions for the initial move, while the privacy narrative and product story gave subsequent buyers reasons to keep entering.

So what is the market really betting on now?

I think MASK’s current trading thesis can be divided into three layers.

The first is continued capital inflows into the privacy sector. As long as the market remains willing to pay a premium for privacy infrastructure, MASK has an opportunity to benefit from sector rotation.

The second is whether MASK can become a more accessible entry point for privacy. Assets like Zcash have already demonstrated that demand for privacy exists. But Nullmask is trying to solve a different problem: giving users transaction privacy without requiring them to change their existing wallet habits. If that experience works, its potential audience could be much broader than that of a single privacy asset.

The third, and most ambitious, expectation is that privacy could evolve from a standalone feature into a default capability for on-chain applications.

If DeFi trading, asset management, cross-chain transfers, and even financial interactions between AI Agents eventually need to take place without exposing complete transaction relationships, privacy could evolve from a niche requirement into an infrastructure-level demand.

MASK’s product direction aligns with this trend. However, this remains a long-term market assumption and should not be confused with user growth that has already materialized.

As for the fundamentals, my assessment is that the product positioning is attractive, but fundamental execution remains at an early stage.

Compared with Memes that rely purely on cultural symbols or community momentum, MASK at least has a clear product direction and identifiable use cases. Its website already provides access to its application and browser extension, along with a product roadmap covering existing wallets, one-click privacy, low fees, and future multichain expansion.

This gives the project a foundation for further validating its product value.

However, I would not say that its fundamentals have already strengthened significantly. The reason is simple: what we can currently confirm is its product positioning and some available product entry points, not large-scale adoption.

What I most want to see is not more feature descriptions on the website, but actual users, real transactions, repeat usage, and evidence that its privacy mechanisms work reliably.

Trust is especially important for privacy products. If users cannot be confident about asset control, transaction privacy, and contract security, even a simple user experience may not be enough to establish long-term usage habits.

Therefore, my current assessment of MASK’s fundamentals is that its narrative and product direction are attractive, product development has made some progress, but adoption metrics and long-term economic value remain insufficiently validated.

This is very different from a project that already has stable revenue or a clearly established token value-capture mechanism. At this stage, MASK’s price still depends heavily on the market’s expectations for the product’s future scale.

Now, the question everyone is interested in is: What catalysts could drive further upside?

1. Real user growth for the one-click privacy feature

This is the most important validation point in my view.

If we start seeing sustained growth in active wallets, privacy transactions, and repeat usage, the market will have a reason to shift from trading a product concept to pricing actual adoption.

What matters most is whether the privacy feature can genuinely serve ordinary users’ everyday transactions, rather than only a small group of early adopters who are already familiar with privacy tools.

2. Actual delivery of multichain functionality

The website has already listed multichain privacy as a future direction, mentioning plans to expand through proxy-based functionality to networks such as Solana and Bitcoin.

If verifiable multichain support becomes available and the privacy experience remains consistent across networks, MASK’s potential market could expand further.

However, multichain expansion also introduces greater technical complexity. For me, actual usability and security matter far more than the number of supported chains.

3. The launch of automated privacy workflows

MASK’s long-term potential is not limited to hiding a single transfer. It could also automate privacy-related transaction processes, such as swaps, cross-chain transfers, and routing.

If these capabilities are eventually delivered, users will no longer need to research how to protect privacy at every step. The product could evolve from a standalone tool into privacy infrastructure that users rely on continuously.

Such updates could attract renewed market attention, but whether they translate into token demand will still depend on actual usage and the token’s economic design.

4. Further expansion of the privacy sector and broader market attention for MASK

If privacy assets such as ZEC continue to strengthen, capital may start looking for smaller privacy projects that have not yet reached the same valuation levels.

MASK’s relationship with ZEC through its trading pair, combined with its clear privacy positioning, could make it one of the candidates during sector rotation.

However, this type of upside is highly dependent on market conditions. If the privacy sector cools down, MASK could lose an important source of external momentum.

The biggest risk is that the price has already moved ahead of product validation.

First, the valuation may have already priced in too much of the product’s future growth. MASK has rapidly climbed from an early low market cap to a valuation in the tens of millions.

At this stage, a large part of what the market is buying is future expectations. If product adoption does not grow at the same pace, the valuation could face a reassessment.

Second, concentrated token ownership makes the price vulnerable to large holders.

The top ten wallets hold approximately 53.4% of the supply, with the largest single wallet accounting for nearly 39%. These figures may be affected by how exchange wallets, liquidity accounts, and address ownership are classified, but they are still enough to warrant attention to the token’s holder structure.

With relatively limited liquidity, selling by large holders could create significant price pressure. Even if the project’s narrative remains unchanged, the price could experience a sharp pullback as a result of token distribution.

Third, transaction fees and the liquidity structure could increase trading costs.

The token has a 3% transfer fee, and part of its liquidity is concentrated among a limited number of liquidity providers.

This means traders need to pay attention not only to price movements, but also to actual trading costs, liquidity depth, and the impact of large orders on price.

Especially during a rapid downturn, the market cap shown on a chart does not represent the amount of capital holders could actually withdraw at anything close to the current price.

Fourth, privacy products carry security and regulatory risks.

The core value of privacy tools is protecting transaction information, but this also exposes them to technical scrutiny, changing regulatory policies, and trust-related challenges.

If a security vulnerability emerges, assets become inaccessible, or the product’s privacy claims fail to match its actual performance, the damage could extend far beyond a short-term price decline.

At the same time, the more complex the cross-chain privacy and automation systems become, the greater the security burden they must bear.

Fifth, the narrative may be stronger than the token’s actual value capture.

This is one of the easiest aspects for the market to overlook.

If Nullmask’s product succeeds, it could certainly generate user demand. But product success does not mean MASK will necessarily capture an equivalent amount of value.

We still need to understand what role the token actually plays in product usage, fee payments, protocol revenue, or other economic mechanisms. If the token lacks a clear value-capture path, then even if the product develops successfully, its valuation may still depend primarily on market expectations.

If the one-click privacy feature attracts real users, multichain capabilities are gradually delivered, trading liquidity continues to improve, and the privacy sector remains strong, MASK could still have room for another valuation expansion.

But if the price continues making new highs while product usage data shows little improvement, the rally will look increasingly like speculative expansion driven by attention, capital rotation, and expectations. Once the sector cools down or early holders begin selling, the risk of a sharp pullback will rise quickly.

So I will focus on three signals from here:

Whether MASK sees sustained growth in real privacy transactions and active users.
Whether product features move from roadmap descriptions to stable, verifiable capabilities.
Whether MASK’s liquidity and holder structure improve, and whether the token can establish a clearer value-capture mechanism.

My view on MASK is that it has a sufficiently intuitive product entry point and has entered the market at a time when the privacy sector is regaining attention. But right now, the market is more willing to pay for its potential user base than for proven commercial value.

What will truly determine MASK’s next stage of growth is not how big a privacy narrative it can tell, but whether it can turn “one-click privacy” into a habit that users adopt consistently.

If that transition happens, MASK could evolve from a privacy-narrative rally into a privacy infrastructure project worth following over the long term. Otherwise, it will remain a trade highly sensitive to sector momentum and market expectations.

A ZK privacy protocol project aiming to enable any existing wallet, chain, and token to support untraceable transactions with a single click.

Users do not need to switch to a new wallet, new seed phrase, or new address. They only need to add a “virtual network / custom RPC” to their existing wallet and sign once for authorization. After that, normal transfers and swaps are intercepted.

The protocol generates ZK proofs on the client side and submits shielded transactions through relayers, hiding the sender, recipient, and transaction amount. It supports:

Shielded deposits
Private transfers
Private withdrawals
Private swaps

It is currently mainly deployed on EVM chains, with Solana and multichain expansion in progress.

The project has a complete protocol design, using UTXO Notes + Poseidon2 Merkle Trees + zk-SNARK proofs. The wallet only signs standard EIP-1559 transactions, while spending authority always remains in the user’s wallet. Hardware wallets can also be used.

In terms of fees, the official documentation states that both shielding and unshielding charge 0.5%. Relayers pay the Gas upfront, and the fee is deducted from the shielded balance.

MASK is the protocol’s value-capture token. It is paired with ZEC, and 100% of protocol revenue is used to buy back MASK. MASK is paired with ZEC, and holders continuously receive ZEC airdrops.
