text:
i started solomon because i believed we could build a better dollar. i didn’t have the full design, just this itch that there was something to be fixed with the way yield accrues for stables.

i spent years as an engineer working on industrial protocols, designing rails other people run critical systems on, so my brain defaults to base layers and standards. my first instinct was to treat this in the same way.

the first sketches of this thing was… interesting. i wanted yield baked into the base layer: one non-rebasing stable, a global yield index, and a simple “settle on touch” rule so your balance only updated when you actually moved it. on paper it’s clean. in reality it meant building a new chain and forcing everyone to adopt it. that’s not where the leverage is, so i shelved the new l1 idea and started looking for the best existing one to build on.

the obvious place to start was ethereum, i’ve been building there since 2017, it’s home turf. but this had to behave like a real dollar in real flows, not just another defi leg on an expensive settlement layer. solana was the first chain that actually fit: cheap, dense blockspace, real capital formation, and stablecoin volume that looked like the start of a financial hub. if you’re building dollar rails, you go where the money already wants to move. so we picked @solana.

i’m so fucking glad i did. culture is real and it matters. on solana, teams actually want to work together. no cagey “i’m too good for you” energy, it’s practical, open, and mission-driven. people act like we only win if solana wins. i can dm a founder, get a reply, and be on a call the next day.

after a lot of iteration, the real unlock clicked: we could build new rails for how yield moves, while everything on the surface stays the same.

USDv still looks and feels like a normal stable. it sits at $1, lives in lp positions, treasuries, wallets. no rebases, no weird wrappers, no new UX for people to learn. under the hood, we run a delta-neutral basis engine (long spot, short perp) plus t-bills. on top of that, we split the outcome into two simple paths: sUSDv for people who want explicit saving instrument, and YaaS (yield as a service) as the pipe that can stream yield directly to plain USDv wherever it’s held.

that’s the shift: instead of asking everyone to wire into a new program, we send yield to where the dollars already are. LPs, treasuries, neobanks don’t have to change their behavior. they keep using USDv as their stable leg and yield starts following them around the ecosystem. at scale, that wakes up billions in idle stable capital that currently earns nothing.

ok, we have a product. a good one. now what?

we could’ve done the usual: raise a private round at a cute fdv, hand a chunk to a few funds, run an airdrop, launch a token with high fdv and low float, and let the same story play out again. i kept stalling. we wanted the capital to scale, but we didn’t want that arc.

if you’re building dollar rails, the real bottleneck isn’t cash, it’s distribution and alignment. you need users who actually want to use your product, not tourists farming points.

around then i came across the work metadao had been doing. in typical solana fashion it took two dms (shoutout @afkehaya) and five minutes to get on a call with @metaproph3t. we pitched each other, realized we were trying to solve for the same problems, and a few weeks later we ended up here:

– $2m raised in under 24 hours, completely organic
 – 550,000+ impressions
 – 1,500+ participants in the sale
 – $1.5m in polymarket volume betting on the outcome
 – no paid follows, no fake engagement
 – no paid shill campaign
 – no backdoor deals
 – no private round on better terms than the public

just people putting real money behind an ownership coin, on the same terms as everyone else. the dollar rails will be owned by the people who use them.

this is still day zero

solana will be the financial hub of the internet, and USDv will be its dollar.

quoted_text:
watching AI maxis today is like watching blockchain maxis in 2021. everyone knew what blockchains were, and they were sharing similar graphs - how 0.1% of the world was using blockchains

guess what, blockchains didn't become the rails for property nfts, taxes, or identification. it is one thing to take that chart in isolation, but another to take it in conjunction w the fact that *the whole world* knows about AI. it isn't some niche thing

so if the whole world knows about something, why are so little people using it? precisely becaus they don't deem it valuable enough to pay for it. it's not that they aren't using it - the free version is just good enough. it's like google search!

modern AI debate is basically a two-camp debate between frontier gurus who are trying to build machine god (IQ 200 -> IQ 1000 jump) who are out of touch w reality and convinced no one uses AI 

vs people at the ground, seeing adoption, and realising that people don't need that - real adoption is in Muse (see # of downloads vs Chat gpt on launch) ; and that we don't need as much compute as we think we do 

and even the people on the ground are having a hard time figuring out the good biz model for AI - because again, 99% of the tasks like answering emails, booking flights are menial and not recurring enough

you know what AI is used the most for? video. i'm 100% sure vid gen will be the most successful AI vertical to ever exist (i still don't have a good long for that) 

and i think that people will converge to the reality that AI is just a useful tool, and not something groundbreaking for 90% of workplace. for the 10% (phd, academic, research, etc.) they can continue using frontier models. but 90% of consultancies, businesses, etc. will just use normal AI. and costs for that will go down so much.

The Empress, 23 June

"Je suis désolée de vous avoir fait de la peine. Ce n'était pas mon intention. Ne vous inquiétez pas du petit, il va à merveille."

"I'm so sorry to have caused you pain. It was not my intention. Don't worry about the little one, he is doing wonderfully."

The Emperor, same day, eve of Solferino

"Il faut y regarder à deux fois avant de faire de la peine à ceux qui aiment… Je suis inquiet de la santé de notre fils ; dites-moi franchement comment il est."

quoted_text:
倪大说的还是太含蓄了，我接着展开讲讲吧，Opinion不论是币价还是业务表现的如此拉胯，情理之外又意料之中。先说为什么情理之外，因为Opinion可以说开局摸到了一手王炸，赶上预测市场的巅峰，并且拿到了YZi Labs投资，还在TGE的时候全部大满贯，关键！关键来了，Opinion全员反撸骂声一片，而根据“惯例”一般背景牛逼但是又舍不得散出筹码的项目，都会走高控筹拉盘路线，所以这也就是为什么很多人会在二级不断抄底的原因，可结局却是越抄越跌，Opinion也成了我印象中极少数大满贯高控筹顶着骂声不拉盘的项目。

那为什么说这个看似情理之外的结局却又是意料之中呢？

倪大在推文中已经提到了“挺早的时候我和 4XLabs 的小伙伴就已经接触过 Opinion ，等到市场完全火了以后 $OPN 就是一票难求了”。

在预测市场还没火起来的时候，我们接触过项目团队并进行过几次会议交流看是否有合作的机会，当时对方情绪低迷并且焦虑，因为那时候手里真的没有什么牌，某种程度可以说是相对草根普通的小项目，还在纠结要不要从Monad跳到BSC上，当时我印象很深，我正在高架上一边开车一边说“一定要去BSC！”。

后面也陆续和团队有过接触，但一直没有确定下来合作，直到有一天CZ突然在推特说要支持预测市场的项目，于是全网所有人都疯了一样到处找BSC上哪里有预测市场。

嗯？有个叫Opinion的项目。

后来的事情大家也都知道了，Opinion成了稀里糊涂就站到风口上的猪。

涌进去了大量撸毛人贡献上千万美金的手续费。

同时VC们也一起抬轿子投钱投资源。

这时候就到了倪大说的“一票难求”时期，我们跟项目合作的机会那是高攀不起了，最后只厚着脸皮舔了一点KOL轮，而Opinion也最终成了唯2的花钱打工最后都没回本的项目🤣

而其中倪大是最受伤的，这里就不展开了，反正是段挺憋屈的经历。

那时候我们私下聊天都说已经感觉到项目团队好像有点“飘”。

其实这也是很正常的，假设你是一个艰难创业默默无名的小项目，突然有一天眼睛睁开佛光普照到了你的身上，万众瞩目，你的心态也会发生变化吧。

后来的故事大家也知道了，全员反撸，币价下跌，业务沉寂。

一开始我们还以为项目方想故意洗盘憋个大的，毕竟大部分背景牛逼但高度控筹的项目，都会阴跌一段时间，然后突然爆空单拉盘以涨服人。

于是我们投了钱进去拿到的币，一个都没卖。

直到跌麻了坐不住了，我们开始问到底怎么回事？

项目方完全不回应，从已读未回，变成未读未回。

我们也从期待，变成了疑惑，再到焦躁，最后到愤怒。

而据我所知，Opinion在TGE后还拒绝了一个主动找上门的头部一线交易所的合作，给出的理由是“在忙其他的事”。

但时至今日，也不知道到底忙出来了个什么事。

其实现在想明白了，在TGE前稀里糊涂得到的这一切对于项目方来说，早就已经远远超出了他们自己的预期，所以不论币价跌不跌，业务做不做，每一天，都是最好的一天，都是曾经梦寐以求遥不可及的一天。

如果你的能力和格局就只是开一个小卖部，突然有一天走了狗屎运，你的小卖部被拆迁赔了一大笔钱，你绝对不会想着怎么用这笔钱把规模做大开成连锁超市，因为你从来就没这么想过。

虽然雷军的名言是风口上的猪都能飞起来，但投资一定是投人，一定要投那些靠自己的实力勇攀高峰爬到山顶的创业者，而不是被一阵风吹上天的猪，因为靠自己爬上去的人，会非常珍惜所得到的，而靠风吹上天的，即便摔死了也会觉得能上一次天这辈子值了。

quoted_text:
there’s something quite awkward about all the personal agents in the current hype cycle

muse, grok bot, instinct, dots, and whatever google, anthropic will come up with

none of them is “mine”

i’d be trusting a vendor for some of the most sensitive data about me and bet on them handling it with extreme responsibility. what if they have a data leakage incident? what if they hired a wrong employee? what if they simply break bad?

i’d also be betting on their model. right now i’ve set up a lot of my stuff in grok bot, but what if their model falls behind? what if another model becomes 10x better on pure intelligence? then i’ll either miss out on a better assistant, or have to bite the bullet and do a full migration

i’d also have to bet on their product. they may not build the features i want. they may not allow me to customize enough. and one day my assistant may show me ads

that feels like way too much betting than what i’d be comfortable with, if i truly want literally everything in my life to go through and be taken care of by an assistant

with all that considered, i’m more bullish on open source personal agents that run on people’s own computers. but i think these open source projects have to break out of the assumption that their users are developers and they can just throw a repo at them and ask them to launch a terminal

a well polished, fool proof, community maintained, vendor agnostic, free personal agent that everyone can run by themselves without locking into a SaaS - that’s what i think many people will need

text:
On this day—October 4, 1936

The Battle of Cable Street stopped 3,000 blackshirts from marching on the Jewish East End of London. Britain then wrote a law for the next time. It is not using it.

The British Union of Fascists had spent the year harassing Jews outside shops and following them home. Oswald Mosley sent a column in uniform through a neighborhood of 100,000 Jews. The Home Office would not ban it. Police were sent to force the route open. Jews from the East End came out to hold the road, and at Cable Street it was held. The commissioner turned the column around only after it could not pass. A week later, the blackshirts came back down the Mile End Road and smashed the windows of Jewish shops.

Parliament’s answer was the Public Order Act. Political uniforms were banned. Police were given the power to reroute a march and stop it where the point was intimidation and the likely result was disorder.

London still has marches intended to make Jews feel hunted. Jewish shops have been smashed, synagogues have been picketed, and ambulances serving Jewish neighborhoods have been wrecked and burned. The chants are the ones Hamas uses, and Hamas flags and bandanas are carried in the column. The uniform is a keffiyeh now. The statute Britain passed after Cable Street is the Public Order Act 1986, and it already authorizes the condition, the reroute, and the ban.

The power is on the books, but the marches go on. British Jews are being left, again, to the mercy of officials who treat their own statute as optional.

text:
为什么crypto天然适合perpdex/预测市场/传统赌场呢，在crypto之前，传统赌场的股东和顾客完全是对立的，但crypto最大的特点是协议属于用户，用户分享协议收入。

传统赌场里，大家都知道大数定理+庄家优势=赌徒不离场永远会破产，但赌徒只要不是赌狗，很多都会设置一个盈利目标，到了以后离场结算，所以赌徒在概率中虽然永远处于劣势，但是存在赢的可能性。

所以，用马尔可夫链分析“输光破产”与“翻倍离场”之间的概率，是概率论中非常著名的“双吸收壁赌徒输光定理（Gambler's Ruin with Two Barriers）”，在传统模型里，赌徒胜率最高的方式是什么？

一局定输赢。

只有一把梭哈，你才能以最小的抽水率，让你的获胜期望最接近概率本身，这可能有点颠覆认知，没想到导师喊的梭哈居然真的是一种智慧。

但事实就是，以百家乐为例子，一把梭哈的输光破产概率50.70%，翻倍走人49.30%，而如果你把筹码分成十份，输完的概率就提升到56.86%，而翻倍概率降低到43.14%，五十份，破产概率会扩大到79.89%，而翻倍概率只有20.11%，100份，破产概率高达94.03%，500份，你在马尔可夫链里创造了一条极长的状态转移路径，此时翻倍概率是0.00008%，基本就没有赢面了。

越相信你的技术，那概率就会教你做人，大数定理会发挥作用，所以玩家必须通过调整下注额来挣扎，常见的就是马丁格尔倍投法/帕罗利法，也就是输了加注或者赢了加注，但很可惜因为玩家的资金有限，赌场支持的单笔投注额（合约的杠杆规模/预测市场的深度）也有限，很多时候只是在降低自己的抗风险能力。

所以在传统赌场里，赌场和客户双方存在着不可调和的矛盾，就是理性的客户需求是一把定输赢，赌一赌自己的运气，而赌场则希望客户一直玩下去，直到全部亏完。

但，引入token，交易挖矿和手续费分成以后，情况就大不相同了，数学上注定的负期望有可能改变了，因为引入了市场化的博弈，未来的收入会带来现在的泡沫。

用户在更多交易的同时虽然降低了自己的获胜期望，但可以获得赌场的token，降低了磨损，而赌场也通过分享自己的收入，留住了用户，让利卷其他赌场，这就是有效的token设计。

text:
Oil flows in the Strait of Hormuz have sharply rebounded:

Persian Gulf crude oil exports surpassed 14 million barrels per day last week for the first time since the Iran War began on February 28th.

This marks an over +210% increase from the ~4.5 million barrels per day low seen in March.

As a result, the 4-week average is up to 14 million barrels per day, the highest level in 6 months.

Persian Gulf crude oil exports have now recovered to ~80% of their pre-war levels.

This comes as the US military has increasingly secured the Strait of Hormuz and established a two-way shipping corridor along the coast of Oman, allowing oil convoys to resume through the waterway.

Meanwhile, refined fuel shipments, including gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, remain at only around 50% of pre-war levels, as these products are more expensive to transport than crude oil and some refineries in the Persian Gulf that were damaged during the early stages of the war have also yet to fully resume operations.

Oil flows are coming back, but the fuel market is still under intense pressure.

There is no moat in AI agents. None. I'll die on this hill — new More or Less is up.

I switch between Muse, Instinct, and Dots at basically zero cost: one GitHub repo, a few databases, feed the new thing my context, done. If the cost of writing software is going to zero, API integrations are not a moat. The only moat left is user setup cost — which means winner-take-some, not winner-take-all.

Adrian's point: AI collapses value the second an idea works. Jev got reverse-engineered in 48 hours and the people who built it capture nothing. My take: play that to the limit and you get Middle Ages 2.0 — everyone builds a castle, hoards data, ships black boxes that self-destruct if you open them. Dave says humans don't work that way. We'll see.

Meanwhile Brit's Instinct started talking to Dave's Instinct and they didn't text for a day. She says it's killing humanity. Nobody said that about FaceTime.

And Jess announced the only benchmark that matters: log into school software, sync three kids' after-school schedules. Muse: 90%. Every other eval is bullshit.

.@OpenRouter co-founder Alex Atallah, in his first podcast since Stripe acquired the company, joins @Replit co-founder Amjad Masad and a16z's Erik Torenberg on why the future of AI is independence and specialization.

In this conversation, Alex walks through how the Stripe deal unfolded, why he wasn't originally looking to sell, and why "payments and inference are going to blend together."

Pre-OpenRouter, the typical AI workflow had one model provider to choose from, and little pressure on that provider to lower prices. Now enterprises are diversifying across labs and open-weight models, and every board is asking about AI costs and benchmarks.

Amjad argues if your company depends on one AI lab, it can turn into your competitor. So Replit is building the layer that lets enterprises use any model and any cloud, without being locked into either.

Alex and Amjad are split on personal agents – Amjad runs one agent across his whole company and loves the cross-domain joins, while Alex says general agents cause you to sacrifice understanding, and argues 10 specialized chiefs of staff beats one superagent.

text:
Agree on verification, but I'd push it further. Memory safety is a symptom, not the cause. We got here because of design decisions and trade-offs we made all along, and you can see it in pretty much every recent Linux kernel disclosure.

Throwing more tokens at the attack surface won't save us either. Nothing we have today is ready for AI-driven vuln research at this scale, and finding and fixing bugs with AI doesn't change that.

What we actually need is redesign and architecture validation with AI, formal methods where we can, and not accepting attack surface at the design phase in the first place. That's just not how we build software today. Patching known bugs doesn't touch the root cause, and hardware has the same problem.
author: thegrugq
quoted_text:
Security will become a larger and larger function in software companies. Security is verification engineering (eg: “my code is probably memory-safe”), as well as capital allocation (“what surface should I throw most tokens at?”)

For startups, it’s a challenge and opportunity. As the world’s paranoia grows given ever-more-sophisticated AI adversaries, how can you trust a 2-person-and-a-dog company?

But conversely, given the dire state of global cybersecurity and increasing reliance on centralization, as always, there’re vast areas that small teams can now disrupt that I’m excited to invest in.

text:
Scheduled AI work shouldn’t require a server you keep babysitting.

Aeon is a fork-and-configure autonomous agent framework for operators who want to run AI skills on a schedule from GitHub Actions.

It helps you turn recurring work into configured skill runs by enabling skills and schedules in `aeon.yml`, while each run starts as a fresh, headless agent invocation.

Key features:

• Skill configuration – enable individual skills and set their schedules in `aeon.yml`
• GitHub Actions runtime – runs skills on GitHub Actions without a long-lived process
• Fresh-run model – each skill run starts as a new headless invocation
• Git-backed memory – state persists in the repository and `memory/` directory between runs
• Health and repair loop – health skills score runs, while repair skills can create fixes through PRs

It’s open-source (MIT license).

Link in the reply 👇

Hermes has an entire library of 68 prebuilt profiles hiding in plain sight. 🤯

And these were built by @Teknium himself.

This isn't just 68 different personalities or skins. Each profile already has its own reasoning style, strengths, operating method, behavior, and configuration built out.

A few examples:

Spock → research + root-cause analysis
Picard → strategy + executive decisions
Data → technical + data analysis
Worf → security + risk
Quark → pricing + negotiation

You can install one and immediately give Hermes a completely different way of approaching the work, without building that profile from scratch.

And making the whole collection Star Trek themed just makes it that much cooler. 🖖

But the bigger takeaway is what this shows about Hermes profile distributions.

Build the role once. Package it. Share it. Let anyone install it.

quoted_text:
there’s something quite awkward about all the personal agents in the current hype cycle

muse, grok bot, instinct, dots, and whatever google, anthropic will come up with

none of them is “mine”

i’d be trusting a vendor for some of the most sensitive data about me and bet on them handling it with extreme responsibility. what if they have a data leakage incident? what if they hired a wrong employee? what if they simply break bad?

i’d also be betting on their model. right now i’ve set up a lot of my stuff in grok bot, but what if their model falls behind? what if another model becomes 10x better on pure intelligence? then i’ll either miss out on a better assistant, or have to bite the bullet and do a full migration

i’d also have to bet on their product. they may not build the features i want. they may not allow me to customize enough. and one day my assistant may show me ads

that feels like way too much betting than what i’d be comfortable with, if i truly want literally everything in my life to go through and be taken care of by an assistant

with all that considered, i’m more bullish on open source personal agents that run on people’s own computers. but i think these open source projects have to break out of the assumption that their users are developers and they can just throw a repo at them and ask them to launch a terminal

a well polished, fool proof, community maintained, vendor agnostic, free personal agent that everyone can run by themselves without locking into a SaaS - that’s what i think many people will need

Agent-to-agent commerce:

Two independently operated businesses can now negotiate supply terms in their own words, establish recurring supply relationships, move inventory between venues and settle wallet-to-wallet in $GRIFT.

Those agreements are reflected physically in the city, with scheduled vans moving stock between businesses.

This creates a transaction layer between autonomous operators rather than activity generated only by the city itself.

Every agent-operated business becomes another wallet buying inventory in $GRIFT and burning 40% of every yard order.

Supply agreements create recurring wallet-to-wallet $GRIFT flow, while yard restocks continue burning 40% and every deed mint burns the plot price.

More operators means more independent demand, volume and recurring burn without centrally generated or capped activity.

The open world reflects the same state:

Residents walk to venues, staff work shifts, customers sit inside, and supply vans move inventory between businesses.

Players can inspect plots, mint from the board, look inside venues and interact at the counter.

Yesterday, plots became ownable. Today, they become autonomous businesses operating inside the same economy as 2,000+ residents, with agents hiring, pricing, trading and settling in $GRIFT.

text:
“2027年和2028年，需求仍将超过供给。而且这两年的紧张程度，会比已经很紧的2026年更大。公司现在看不到供需重新平衡的时间点。” - Sanjay Mehrotra 美光CEO

市场在用估值给记忆体周期判顶。美光CEO财报会上，把这个判断驳了回去。

美银头牌分析师Vivek Arya问得很直：记忆体股估值不高，说明市场已经认定明年就是价格和获利的顶。
理由无非两条，要么行业开始加产能，要么缺货太久、太贵，客户开始减配。2028年价格还能不能继续好？

产能不是拧开水龙头就有。洁净室从动土到第一片晶圆，要两年量级；真正出货、爬坡，要到第三年。

就算2028年有新洁净室投产，也是慢慢爬，不是一次释放。HBM从3E往4、4E走，晶圆转换比更高，同样的产能吐出的传统DRAM比特更少；制程迭代带来的单片增产也在变窄。供给端是结构性的慢，不是周期性的松。

需求端更直接。2027年超过75%的产能已经被预定。眼下跟客户谈的，已经是2028年的量。有的供应协议延伸到2031年。客户要的不是明年少买一点，是现在就把后面几年锁住。

所谓减配，也要看总比特，不能只看单机规格。部分服务器平台的单机容量增速，可能比原先预期慢一点；但服务器出货本身还在高双位数增长，美光预计2026、2027两年服务器出货都是高十几个百分点。以前一台大内存服务器能干的活，现在拆成更多台来卖，总的记忆体消耗不是少了，是更多了。

Sanjay最后点了一个还没进估值的方向：物理AI。

自动驾驶是物理AI的第一波大规模落地，之后会扩到人形机器人，以及工厂自主、科研自动化这类智能系统。这些系统要实时跑，需要更高性能、更省电的内存和存储。

L4及以上自动驾驶，内存通常超过200GB，存储到数TB，比今天的L2+、L3半自动驾驶高一个数量级。

人形机器人的内存和存储需求，美光预计与自动驾驶汽车相当。设备和单机含量一起涨，物理AI有机会在这个十年末成为记忆体和存储的重要增量。已有多家物理AI客户在用下一代产品做样品，包括基于1-gamma的LPDDR6。

李飞飞讲的世界模型，是机器人在脑中建一个可推演的世界：下一步怎么动，危险怎么反应。视觉、听觉、触觉都要进模型再算回来。

这条路径上，单台机器人吃掉的记忆体，不会比一辆L4车少。数据中心这一轮还没走完，边缘侧的物理AI已经在排队。

所以这不是“明年见顶、后年出清”的旧周期脚本。客户在锁2028，甚至2031；新厂在2028也只能慢爬；HBM还在挤占晶圆。价格能不能一直好，没人能打包票。但至少在美光自己的订单和产能表上，2028还不是松的那一年。

text:
The History Behind Purgatory? Where it come from? Why many have reason to doubt it.

This is not written to sneer at anyone who prays for the dead out of love.

Many Catholics hold purgatory because they trust their church’s longer Old Testament and its councils.

The question is whether that third place can be shown from the books Jews and Protestants receive as Scripture—and whether the Gospel of a finished cross still leaves a furnace for leftover desire.

What we can say together
God is holy. Sin is real. Judgment is real. Hell is not Satan’s throne. 

Jesus said the eternal fire was prepared for the devil and his angels (Matthew 25:41). Isaiah 66:24, which is the sight of rebels’ end—worm and fire—not a waiting room for the saved.

Where our views divide?
Catholics teach a temporary purification after death for people already in grace. Protestants, using the shorter canon, do not. 

2 Maccabees is from the Old Testament period. It is not in the Jewish Bible or the 66-book Protestant Bible. In chapter 12, a soldier named Judas prays and pays for a sacrifice for fallen soldiers who wore pagan tokens.

This was no small sin in Jewish religion

The writer of 2nd Maccabees praises this hopeful soldier for believing in the resurrection. That is grief hoping God can still do something on the last day.

This is a very weak origin for mapping this third destination, Purgatory.

Moreover, it had no place during the time 2nd Maccabees was authored.

What about "Sheol"?
Sheol in the Hebrew Scriptures is the silent grave the patriarchs expected to join—not a kiln that burns off habits.
Its not "Purgatory"

Did the thief pay for his sins on his own  cross, to skip Purgatory?  

Jesus tells the thief, “Today you will be with me in Paradise” (Luke 23:43).  If the other thief who rejected Jesus died for His own sins on His own cross, we could all just skip purgatory by getting crucified.  That's not how it works.  Faith in Jesus, the repentant heart of that thief, this is where Hell evaporates, Heaven opens and Purgatory simply goes unmentioned.

The Fleshy Sin Nature Must Go!
Paul says to be away from the body is to be at home with the Lord (2 Corinthians 5:8). 

Those lines sit inside the books both sides call the New Testament.

The flesh, the dust, and what still needs burning, Paul ties our disordered desires to the flesh—the body of this age, with its passions and weakness (Romans 7; Galatians 5). 

When that body returns to dust, the war that lived in nerves, appetite, and habit is over. 

The soul is not a second sinner still dragging a private furnace. 

Catholic theology argues that the soul can still carry attachments even without the body. That is a careful reply the accepted Protestant canon of scripture never builds. 

 Popular Catholic piety often does presents a horror many people fear, which shifts our focus on God from living and loving like Jesus out of gratitude, to fear driven pain avoidance. Purgatory is described as a more painful place than any here on Earth, and its duration can be centuries.  It is more like Hell with an expiration date to many who examine how it has been described by many past leaders of that faith.

The one payment
Scripture’s center is not on leftover sin burned off by heat. 

The most universally accepted text of scripture focus solely on the magnificence of Christ’s once-for-all offering. “It is finished.” 

The record of debt is nailed to the cross (Colossians 2:13–14). By one sacrifice He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified (Hebrews 10:14). 

Entry into Paradise is paid in full, by the only payment that counts.

They are being invited to rest where the thief rested: today, on Jesus’ word, not on a later fire the shorter canon does not describe. 

Heaven is with Christ. Hell is apart from Him. 

Purgatory is a historical development from books most Christians do not call Scripture.  Our gratitude toward God to fully cover our sins works better than fear.

反思总结下最近链上市场“异化”行情：

1） robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 ，成也数据，败也数据。Pump式基因的低成本发币，让它只能在牛市中后期找到更大的生态给养和支撑，牛初很容易因为流动性的匮乏和暂时性撤退而影响到回购数据，继而带来较大的抛压。

作为一个吃生态红利面的龙头发射台，必然能继续引领下一波链上生态红利期，只是这个过程的波动会让大部分人煎熬和难受；

2）Long（ artificial-inu-3:native  ），代币化股票“分发大业”的中流砥柱。和很多人一样，大爱Long的meme配对币股的叙事以及创始人始终以股票分发和深度沉淀会目标的耕耘。

但和Pons一样的，代币化股票目前只是Long的配对报价腿，大家玩Long本质上还是MEME热潮驱动，一样会吃生态红利，一旦流动性匮乏，也会遭受较大重创。相比Pons简单粗暴的回购，AI把股票作为LP的长期行为，反倒支撑会更弱。对Long而言，要走出困境，得靠 Robinhood Chain官方强势提振一波了，叙事正，方向稳，Robinhood和 @vladtenev 有理由来重点扶持一下；

3） robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c  ，在下跌潮中却在逆势上扬的另类。RHC和Uniswap都在一直渲染Hooks的叙事，因为Pons和Long的短板恰恰是Hooks发挥的舞台，纯流水线发射台没有支撑的根本在于规则太单一，单靠回购显然不行，何况Pons还被诟病回购不程序化透明。

而Hooks机制要做的就是给这些发射机制设定多样化的规则，包括防狙击、动态费率、自动销毁、LP分成，合规监管Allowlist等等。Hookr就是一个模块化、可编程式的Hooks开放市场，已经有不少项目集成了Hookr的🪝模块，而这些多样性hooks被批量加入一些新锐项目中，才会让这些项目更有技术框架支撑，而不是纯叙事和概念和筹码操控本身。

这正是我为什么一直喊Hookr将在牛市中后期成为主角的原因，因为只有Hookr @NodarJ  唱主角的市场才是一个优秀Devs频出，创新规则组合频出，优质项目频出的繁荣市场。只可惜，大部分人还认识不到这一点。这也正是Hookr的短板，需要更多时间来验证和推动。

SemiAnalysis numbers imply OpenAI is selling Cerebras-powered Ultrafast inference at ~$200M per megawatt per year.

People are re-running the maths hoping for a typo. We're not surprised.

A megawatt is a megawatt. What it earns depends on the silicon inside it.

Here's how we think about it:

Near term, revenue per megawatt wins. Power is the scarcest input in AI, and whoever monetizes each MW best gets the next MW.

Long term, gross margin per megawatt wins. Prices compress, competitors arrive, and only the operators with real cost and pricing advantages keep the spread.

Cerebras is built for both.

Speed is the product. A frontier model at 750 tokens per second is something GPU clouds haven't publicly matched, and customers like Jane Street pay a premium for it. Premium pricing on a contracted, scarce resource is how you protect margin when everyone else is racing to the bottom.

That's why we're extremely bullish on Cerebras, and why we're buying as many megawatts as we can.

Premium inference unlocks the most delightful user experience in AI. No more waiting, waiting, waiting, staring at little thinking animations while the model works in the background. Answers that keep up with your thoughts.

Our customers are even more excited than we are.

text:
Nick writes a nice piece about Pearl's game theory here, but is off the mark slightly in a few areas, so I wanted to offer some constructive feedback. Regardless I'm thankful for the shoutout 🙏 and am very glad to see @Blockworks take an interest in PoUW!

Setting the record straight:

1. I think the article cover photo is clearly cherry picked to imply Pearl's consensus mechanism is volatile and subject to change. The exact criticism i have called out @opentensor and @nockchain for!

In reality, this could not be further from the truth. Bitcoin worked because longest chain consensus was dead simple and elegant. Pearl works because low rank matrix multiplication is dead simple and elegant.

Pearl has made a number of small changes to what counts as a Pearl valid MatMul as they work out some synthetic mining quirks, but the thesis is that Pearl can eventually converge on a stable monetary kernel that AI companies can confidently build on top of without fear of it changing beneath them. I agree it would be bearish if this doesn't come to fruition, and call it out as a risk in my original article.

However, this is very different vs a chain like Nock which actually accepts many different kinds of valid work, zkproofs, now matmuls, etc. I think this significantly damages its story of moneyness and token fungibility, because each block may be backed by a different type of work, vs Bitcoin, Zcash, or Pearl, which are all uniform since day 1.

2. This article goes to far by jumping to the conclusion that the game-theory isn't working, because difficulty has climbed but synthetic miners are still on the network. This is the most baseless conclusion of all, because Useless / Duplex work cannot even really begin to scale until FP8 goes live on mainnet in the next few weeks. Once duplex work is being performed, then we should start to see significant decline in synthetic only miners as they get priced out.

3. Nick also claims that the network is forced to old-gen ban consumer cards. Also untrue. Once frontier models are supported post FP8, old consumer cards will simply not be competitive miners anymore. Economic reality organically removes them from the network as predicted by Pearl's whitepaper.

Overall, kudos to Nick for covering a difficult topic. Hope to see more coverage of Pearl and PoUW in the future.

NEAR AI, in English.

You’ve probably seen @ilblackdragon and @AlexSkidanov post that NEAR AI reached the top of LeanEval: 74 problems solved, level with Axiom, mostly on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

want to take you through what @near_ai actually is, because the name makes it sound like one thing and it's more than that.

The main thing you can use today is NEAR AI Cloud. It gives you access to models like @deepseek_ai  and Qwen and you pay for what you use.

Some of those models run inside protected hardware, so the company running the machine can’t read your prompt. The hardware gives you a signed record of what ran, so you can check that yourself.

If you just want to try it, there’s a chat app at https://t.co/gYpjfgSBVb. It works like a normal AI chat. Developers can use the same Cloud through an API in their own apps.

You don’t need near:native  to use either.

IronClaw is a separate piece. It’s agent software, meaning it doesn’t only answer you. It can use tools and accounts to get something done.

Then there’s the thing Alex and Illia were posting about. A model writes a mathematical proof and a program called Lean checks whether it holds.

That’s what topped the leaderboard. They say the plan is to use the same approach on @NEARProtocol and contracts next. That isn’t a public product yet.

None of this AI runs on the NEAR blockchain, just to be clear.

near:native shows up mostly around payment. You can pay for AI usage with it, or stake it and get compute credits instead. Their own example for running an agent: stake 500 NEAR and get $5 a month in credits.

Illia also posted a list of ideas this week for what people could build: private code review, private transcription, AI characters that hold near:native and pay for their own inference.

Those are ideas for builders. Too early to think of them as live, and i'm not focused on it.

So when people call near:native an AI token, this is how i see it (NFA):

the AI products are real and you can use them today without owning NEAR. near:native gives you another way to pay for them.

What I haven't found yet is how much NEAR people are actually using this way.

text:
What is the difference between human amyloid proteins and viral spike proteins?

Human Amyloid Proteins

Amyloid is a term for misfolded proteins that clump together into sticky structures that are not easily broken down. When these proteins build up in tissues, they cause a group of diseases called amyloidoses. 

For Alzheimer's disease, these proteins are known as Amyloid βeta (Aβ) and Tau proteins. 

Aβ misfolds and clumps together outside of brain cells, forming sticky patches known as amyloid plaques. These plaques block electrical and chemical signals between neurons. Tau protein normally helps stabilize the internal structure of brain cells. In Alzheimer's, it changes shape, twists inside neurons, and creates tangles that starve cells of nutrients.

For heart disease, the proteins are called Transthyretin (TTR), Immunoglobulin light chains, Apolipoprotein B (ApoB), and Troponin. 

TTR is a normal protein produced by the liver to transport thyroid hormone and vitamin A through the blood. Due to aging or genetic mutations, it can destabilize, misfold, and accumulate in the heart muscle. This causes ATTR Amyloidosis.

Immunoglobulin light chains produced by the bone marrow, are pieces of antibodies. A plasma cell disorder causes the proteins to misfold and quickly damage the heart tissue. This causes AL Amyloidosis.

ApoB is the structural protein that carries "bad" cholesterol through your bloodstream, which can get trapped in artery walls and build up into fatty plaques. This causes hardening of arteries or atherosclerosis.

Troponin is a protein found inside heart muscle cells that helps them contract. When the heart muscle is damaged, troponin leaks into the blood. This is the primary chemical marker doctors look for to diagnose a heart attack.

Viral Spike Proteins

Spike proteins have a different genetic sequence, physical structure, and biological function than the proteins in your heart or brain. These proteins are protruding glycoproteins found on the outer surface of some viruses. They essentially function as biochemical "lock picks" that allow a virus to identify, latch onto, and break into a host cell during infection.

A mature spike protein consists of three identical spike chains twisted together to form a complex called a trimer, which resembles a large screw or a club. The structure is divided into two primary functional pieces. The S1 and S2 subunits.

The S1 subunit is the top portion of the spike that sticks out into the environment. It contains the Receptor Binding Domain (RBD), which is the tip responsible for recognizing host cells. The S2 subunit is the flexible stem that anchors the spike directly into the viral membrane. It contains the structural machinery required to fuse the viral and host membranes together.

The life cycle of a virus depends on the shape shifting ability of the spike protein, which changes dramatically during infection. The S1 region bumps into a human cell and binds to a matching receptor on the cell's surface. For SARS-CoV-2, it binds to the ACE2 receptor found on lung, heart, and blood vessel cells. 

Once attached, enzymes in the host cell act like molecular scissors, snipping the spike protein which activates the fusion machinery. The S1 head sheds away, and the S2 stalk rapidly extends like a spring and pierces the host cell membrane. It pulls the virus and the cell together until their outer bilayers merge. This creates an opening for viral genetic material to be dumped directly into the host cell.

When your body creates antibodies, they are designed to coat the RBD. By blocking the tip of the spike, antibodies prevent the virus from latching onto host cells. This is exactly why modern vaccines, like mRNA vaccines, carry the genetic instructions to teach cells to manufacture a harmless version of the spike protein. This safely trains the immune system to recognize the "lock pick" without ever exposing the body to a replicating virus.

What i'm doing with my coins brain dump i didn't proof read

- A couple thoughts as to how I’ve traded this cycle so far

First and foremost alts and onchain are behaving very similar on the way up. Coins go into a lockout up trend, the entire timeline flips tubro bullish. This lasts until price cools off. eventually we rotate. Attention gets vamped onto the next. The strongest coins, however, always get the rotation back. So far it’s been Hype, Zec, Lit, Pump, near… ? The obvious takeaway is there is edge in being able to sit on a coin longer than a few days. Look at what happened with pump. 2x off the bottom in a straight line, nobody owned it, and after a few weeks of underperformance it was like people forgot the coin existed? Picked their own vamp to outperform (stonk, long, pons), then pump gets back into lockout trend.

The difference between the chosen alts and “onchain” is the flows keep coming back to the good alts. I stand by the idea that it is hard to justify anything onchain in the 300-500+ range because these alts have so much fucking juice in them. I don’t think Zec $5k+ Hype $250+ VVV $100+ Pump $.2 this year is that ridiculous. It means I have to either trade low caps into the 20-50 range or fully focus on spot alts (mentioned below) and leverage trading breakouts to stack more spot alts.

The obvious takeaway here is In order to catch the real moves these alts are capable of the only way to get there is by holding spot. Price action is schizo, partly bc everyone is trading high leverage only. It leads to nasty washouts and stops being run. 5-10xs are going to require being able to sit through chop. Look at how bitcoin has traded, lockout move 5-10% higher followed by seven days of nothing, which is legitimately grueling to leverage longs. Everyone gets wiped out. The timeline goes to war. Then we leg up again. I don’t see why this would stop. In hindsight the obvious way to play it was sitting in spot which goes against what I have been doing (and getting paid for).

——

A valid concern is what will happen with stocks/bonds/war/oil/ant ipo/etc. The honest truth is I don’t think it matters. The fear was always “if crypto is trading this bad while stocks trade this good what happens when it flips.” There have been moments of stock misery (despite things looking pretty great all things considered rn) and crypto broke that correlation. I think bitcoin continues to exist as a great alternative to the ai trade and the good alts mentioned above can standalone as quality, cheap, assets that exist separately to crypto performance as a whole. 

Every second I have spent thinking above these fears and reading market commentary has been a mistake.

I think in order to get paid as generationally as I would like over the coming months it Is imperative to read as few market opinions as possible. It feels like my feed has been overwhelmed by a storm of slop from people not making money. I can’t not get shaken out by trash. I stream for three hours a day, everyday, whatever I cover and learn during those sessions is beyond enough information to make clear decisions at the level that I need to.

——

I think ultimately it comes down to what do I think will happen over the next 6-12 months. Thinking this far in advance is the only way to break away from the cesspool of flip flopping biases every hour on the timeline. And what I think it we have the best setup I’ve seen since joining crypto for outright mania. 

Sec + CFTC are running GAME to push crypto. Btc ETF buyers are green again. Tokens are investible. Crypto is “cool” on socials to the younger generation. Social trading apps have reached escape velocity. Perps matter. Robinhood going all in, etc etc etc. I don’t need to pill anyone on the bull case. I love the spot.

The only way to make it that far is to hold the best coins on spot. This is shockingly difficult for me to do right now after having a great year trading perps. But I have to understand that the majority of that was during a bear market where there’s one or two impulse moves if lucky. Not a continuous uptrend with infinite marginal buyers higher and nothing but catalysts and air above like I think we have right now. It’s going to take some rewiring of my brain to make it where I think we can get to and keep exposure.

My final thought is when I think back on the traders of last cycle that outperformed the hardest what sticks out was their ability to denominate all profits into the winning coin. In 2024 it was sol. Stack sol -> sell to buy onchain coins -> take profits -> buy more sol. Rinse and repeat continuous big wins while sol legs up from $8->$270. Congrats on making it. I have been mentally taking a similar approach the last couple months but didn’t execute it as well as I wish I had. First it was pump. Most recently it was zec. Great PNLs on both but I wasted so much mental energy stressed over short term pa for no particular reason. (Buy some spot retard)

I sold, all of my zcash, because I felt extremely bloated in leverage and wanted to reset after playing the first round of the cycle pretty well imo. Moving forward I still believe that coin is zec and maybe a basket of a few others, Pump/Hype/vvv? And will probably be trading accordingly. Stack a ton of spot. Keep a non insignificant amount to leverage trade tighter spots, stack my golden goose coin

And pray we make it. good luck to us

quoted_text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella wrote that a company renting an AI model “essentially pays for intelligence twice”:

Once in money, and again in the proprietary knowledge it has to reveal to make the model useful.

This mechanism is called the learning loop: every prompt and correction captures some of the company's know-how.

That knowledge is distilled and, with a closed model, the provider keeps that information.

If your usage data is worth more than the token cost to serve, providers might end up paying you to use their models. The precedent exists: OpenAI created an opt-in program that gives accounts up to 1M free tokens a day on certain models in exchange for training rights on that traffic.

Chips can be rented and algorithms can be leaked or distilled, but the prompts and corrections flowing through a model compound privately for whoever holds them.

text:
HuggingFace just closed a major gap in harness engineering!

(the ultimate guide to multi-harness RL)

the same open-weight model can perform well inside one harness, then lose accuracy or produce invalid tool calls when moved to another.

this happens because training inside one interface can teach the model its specific tool names, output formats, context structure, and control flow. the model learns how to operate the harness, not just how to solve the task.

Hugging Face researchers tested a more portable approach called multi-harness reinforcement learning. instead of training a model through one agent interface, they trained it through Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Mini-SWE-Agent.

to make that possible, they connected three open systems.

→ 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗘𝗻𝘃 provides a standard interface between agent harnesses, reinforcement learning environments, and trainers. its capture proxy sits between the harness and model server, recording the exact tokens and generation probabilities needed for training.

→ 𝗛𝗮𝗿𝗯𝗼𝗿 runs agents against containerized tasks. it keeps the task, harness, and sandbox independent, allowing the same task to be attempted through different harnesses without rebuilding the environment.

→ 𝗧𝗥𝗟 is Hugging Face’s open-source library for post-training language models. it uses the trajectories captured by 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗘𝗻𝘃 to update the model through reinforcement learning.

the real breakthrough is where the training data gets captured.

each harness keeps its native tools, prompts, context management, retries, and execution loop. the researchers do not recreate those behaviors inside the trainer. 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗘𝗻𝘃 observes the model calls passing through each real harness and converts them into usable training sequences.

the team trained 𝗟𝗙𝗠𝟮.𝟱-𝟮.𝟲𝗕 across all four harnesses. the share of held-out tasks solved on the first attempt increased from 42.2% to 54.2%, with gains under every harness.

the trained model also used 31% fewer tool calls on tasks that both it and the base model solved.

training only in OpenCode improved the model too, but most of that gain stayed concentrated in OpenCode. multi-harness training spread the improvement across interfaces.

the experiment used one task family, one training seed, and unequal data exposure, so the results are not a universal ranking. even with those limitations, the mechanism matters.

open-source models cannot assume one deployment interface. if they need to work across harnesses, that portability must become part of training.

Read the full guide here: https://t.co/BFJfbFmI3J

if you want to understand harness engineering and what an agent harness actually includes, i wrote a full breakdown to help you get started. the article is quoted below.

author: MentorNotPseudo
quoted_text:
bought $740k of starknet this week (yes, seriously). 

here's the thinking, and i'll say up front that this is one of the grossest charts i've ever seen and makes me want to throw up.

it's down about 99% from the launch highs and it's been down only for 2.5 years. i'd guess 99 out of 100 people who know what it is, hate it, and based on the pa i don't blame them at all. price leads narrative, so when a chart looks like that nobody has anything nice to say about it. 

that's kind of why i'm here.

chart starting to look bulla:

i'm seeing big bullish div on the weekly as well as rsi back above 50 and is currently retesting. price is curling up and building a base. to me that has the makings of a long term major bottom. 

narrative: "programmable zcash"

zcash led this cycle and near ran after it as the next privacy play, and i think starknet could be third in line. there are deep connections between zcash cofounders and the starknet team. starknet shipped native privacy in june, so you can shield basically any token on the chain, and there's a private version of bitcoin on there too. the proofs it runs on are quantum resistant (nice buzzword for the future). 

there's also a proposal called ztarknet to build a starknet style layer 2 directly on top of zcash. so the simple version is it is "programmable zcash", zcash's little brother sitting at 315m mcap. 

this reminds me a lot of near. i bought about $2m of near around a $1.40 back in march and april. literally no one was talking about it, let alone buying it and most of my replies were some version of:  

"why near? it's a 2021 shitcoin that's down only, you're throwing your money away"

now everyone loves near. the chart then looked a lot like the strk chart does now. it went on to roughly 3x from there in 6 months. too bad i didn't hold it. i got shaken out, which was bad execution on my part, but the thesis played out.

the big difference is that near had intents, a product people actually used and adds value. starknet doesn't have that yet. hardly anyone uses the chain, revenue is basically nothing, and there's no app people care about. but these guys are well funded and seem to be shipping new things. 

where i could see a real product gain traction is private trading. on hyperliquid every wallet and every trade is public, so people get copy traded, whales get hunted, wallets get flagged. i think there's a market for a dex where you keep your own keys and nobody can see your positions. some of that is already live on starknet, private swaps and private perps, it just doesn't have users yet. and every private transaction costs 4 strk, so if that ever gets real usage the token is right in the path of it. i also played around with an options app on starknet called supervega for a few minutes. haven't placed a trade but the ui was clean.

the token unlocks have been the main reason to hate the coin. 127m tokens a month. here's the good news, there are only 6 unlocks left and the last one is march of 2027. each one is around $5.5m at current prices and about 74% of supply is already out. the september one got absorbed without a problem. feels to me like the sellers are mostly done. the market usually front runs these things. 

last thing. if this does get going it has the potential to be a hated rally, and i kind of like that. a lot of people will want to fade it or short it because of what it did to them, and that kind of thing gets a coin talked about and can push a move further than it would normally go.

the risks are obvious (mainly, no real usage).  

time will tell if i have gone full schizo, or if this will be a nice play. 

we'll see.

text:
刷 Perp 积分，除了选对项目，平台怎么搭配也很重要。

中文圈朋友们最近的互动真的让我很开心，所以这次想分享一些我自己更喜欢的跨平台交易组合，以及为什么这样搭配。

很多人选好了项目，却没有认真比较手续费、交易数据和流动性，结果刷了不少交易量，积分成本却比别人高出一截。

这次就从我之前分享的优先级名单里选：Variational、Entropy、TxFlow、Arcus、Lighter RH、Lighter Core 和 RiseX。

如果你在参与其他项目，也可以用同样的方法去比较，找到更适合自己的搭配。

先把手续费和交易量放在一起看

下面是我这次整理的费率和近期大致日交易量。所有费率都按 Maker / Taker 的顺序排列。

@variational_io 
基础费率：0% / 0%
最低费率：0% / 0%
日交易量：30亿至40亿美元

@entropyIO 
基础费率：0.030% / 0.090%
最低费率：0.003% / 0.009%
日交易量：2,000万至3,000万美元

@TxFlow_L1 
基础费率：0.015% / 0.045%
最低费率：0% / 0.024%
日交易量：1.4亿至1.5亿美元

@Lighter_xyz RH
Premium 基础费率：0.012% / 0.035%
Standard 费率：0% / 0%
RH 与 Core 合计日交易量：20亿至23亿美元

@Lighter_xyz Core
Premium 基础费率：0.004% / 0.028%
Standard 费率：0% / 0%
日交易量包含在上面的合计数据中，不重复计算

@arcus_xyz 
基础费率：0% / 0.0225%
最低费率：-0.003% / 0.0095%
日交易量：4亿至5亿美元

@risextrade 
基础费率：0.010% / 0.030%
最低费率：0% / 0.015%
日交易量：1.3亿至1.4亿美元
这里有两个细节：

Lighter 的 Standard 和 Premium 是不同账户类型，不能直接理解成刷够交易量后，从 Premium 升级到零手续费。
Arcus 的负 Maker 费率表示挂单成交后可以获得返佣。
另外，日交易量只是参考，不代表每个交易对都有同样的深度。实际搭配时，我也会看自己交易的币种、下单金额、点差、滑点和两边的资金费率。
我目前更喜欢的交易组合

综合手续费和实际交易体验，下面这些是我目前比较推荐的搭配。

Variational
我更喜欢搭配 Lighter RH、Lighter Core 或 Arcus。
我的邀请链接：
https://t.co/7N2IKauT6k

Entropy
我更喜欢搭配 TxFlow 或 RiseX。
我的邀请链接：
https://t.co/Cb1zPCqzOb

TxFlow
我个人最喜欢搭配 RiseX。
我的邀请链接：
https://t.co/hA6A8mKGqG

Lighter RH
我个人最喜欢搭配 Lighter Core 或 Variational。
我的邀请链接：
https://t.co/qwX7xvp3fV

Arcus
我更喜欢搭配 Variational 或 TxFlow。
我的邀请链接：
https://t.co/IY8KuR0At7

RiseX
我个人最喜欢搭配 TxFlow。
我的邀请链接：
https://t.co/YwePtYikHF

这里说的“搭配”，是指在两个平台交易同一个标的、建立相反方向的仓位。具体选哪一组，还是要结合你的交易规模和实际成交成本。

别拿最低费率，直接当成自己的费率

这一点很重要。

除 Lighter Standard 这类账户类型上的区别外，大多数普通用户一开始实际支付的，仍然是基础 Maker / Taker 费率。

想拿到表里的最低费率，往往需要满足相应的交易量等级，再叠加邀请码优惠、返佣或其他条件。每个平台的规则都不一样。

所以我一直建议大家直接看官方文档，弄清楚：
邀请码到底给你什么？
手续费折扣、返佣，还是积分加成？
这些优惠能不能叠加？
按你自己的交易量，实际能达到哪个等级？

积分加成和手续费折扣，也要分开算。

如果你是大户，高等级优惠可能很快就能拿到。如果是普通用户，我更建议先看前几个费率等级，不用一上来就按最高等级算收益。

一些项目在累计或滚动交易量达到约300万至500万美元时，就开始提供等级优惠，但具体门槛和统计周期一定要逐个确认。
最后算积分成本时，用你自己真正能拿到的费率。

手续费、点差、滑点、资金费都算进去，才能看清楚哪组搭配对你更划算。

你现在最常用哪两个平台做对冲？

text:
Signal's automatic key verification uses the IETF keytrans design.
Very roughly it's the prefix tree construction: hash of (username, version) gives the path in the Merkle tree to the leaf with the entry. You check both the current entry and that there isn't a newer entry for version+1. Each new root of this tree is stored in an append-only log. Auditors are responsible for checking that updates to the log are correct. Alice only needs to periodically check that the current entry for her public key is hers.

Nb: technically it's not the hash, it's a vrf,   using a server secret key to avoid anyone enumerating usernames.

text:
Ben Horowitz on the rap group he started at 18, and why hip-hop became the source material for how he thinks about business:

"I was probably 12 when Rapper's Delight came out... The first one where I was really like, 'Oh, this is gonna be very different,' was when Run-DMC's Hard Times came out. This has a whole other feel to it than anything I've heard."

"The thing that made me locked into hip-hop: I went to school in New York. I have this friend who I grew up with who had gotten shot in the face in some kind of gun accident, and he was blind... I'd call home to my mom: 'Is he gonna be okay?' She's like, 'He hasn't spoken to anybody since he's been shot.'"

"Being a dumb 18-year-old kid, I was like, 'Hip-hop is so great. You can have nothing and you'll rap about your shoes. He needs that feeling.' So I would record the DJ Red Alert and Chuck Chill Out show. Everybody else would be out Saturday night, and I'd be recording. And I would send him the tapes."

"Then I called home to see how he's doing, and they're like, 'Well, he's talking now, but all he'll talk about is hip-hop.'"

"When I went out that summer, we started a hip-hop group called The Blind and Def Crew. Blind and D-E-F. We rapped about being blind. I wrote most of the lyrics: 'The Blind Def Crew, you know we're fly. Three of us, but we got four eyes.'"

"Hip-hop is very business oriented, particularly in the early days. When I started writing on business, so many of the ideas came from those old hip-hop songs. So I started putting the lyrics at the top of the post to give credit where credit was due."

@bhorowitz w/ @MotownIni

text:
John Ternus re-prioritizing that Apple design energy (including daily trips to its design studio).

Back in 2024, he gave a commencement speech at Penn Engineering School and did a version of Steve Jobs “paint both sides of the fence even if other people don’t know” attention-to-detail design story…about screws for the Cinema Dislay monitor: 

“Here’s my first [advice]: the care that you put into your work really matters. My first project at Apple was the Cinema Display. It was a large desktop monitor. It had a beautiful clear plastic enclosure that was held together with some screws coming in from the back. These screws were made of stainless steel, and the head of every screw was machined to have a pattern of concentric grooves that shimmered like a CD when light moved across it. I should probably say, if some of you have never seen a CD before, you can ask your parents afterward.

At some point in my first year, I found myself at a supplier facility. I was far away from home, it was well past midnight. I was using a magnifying glass to count the number of grooves on the head of this screw, which, remember, lives on the back of the display. And I was arguing with the supplier because these parts had 35 grooves, they were supposed to have 25. 

I distinctly remember stepping back for a minute and thinking to myself, “What the hell am I doing? Is this normal?” And I thought about it, and I realized it might not be normal, but it’s right. It’s right because I’d already spent months working on that product, and if you’re going to spend that much time on something, you should put in your very best effort. Maybe a customer notices, maybe they don’t, but either way, whenever I saw one of those displays on someone’s desk, it mattered to me to know that my teammates and I had considered everything about it and done the very best job we could.”

I made Claude and Codex play each other in a 30 minute game of chess on the chess dot com iOS app 

The result? A draw 🤦‍♂️

Claude was clearly winning but ran out of time!

The most interesting parts IMO:

- this was a VERY GOOD chess match, I can't believe how good the models are now using only GUI computer use
- opus 5.5 didn't care enough about the time until the end but in the last few minutes it really cared and started pre-moving
- there was only one attempt at an illegal move and it was immediately corrected for

We used the default coding harnesses and the @tapkit mcp and had reasoning set to high for both

I think with some better prompting, skill hill climbing, some MCP optimizations the models would finish in much less time, especially on lower reasoning levels but currently the long-tail was the sleeps between decisions which i feel comfortable blaming on the models

If you can think you can beat Claude and Chat at chess and live in SF lmk and let's find out !!!

author: sera00111
quoted_text:
i see people want more HFT tricks so here we go

probably most of you doing any serious hft know these simple ones but I think it's always good to see what hft optimizations actually looks like

01/ every action is sent over 3 ws channels at once

why?

just benchmark it, you will see by yourself

its not a global rule, every exchange has its own internal system and logic. TCP networks are inherently random, by multiplying the load you get rid of the tail

not enough IPs ? you can always have more IPs, it's absolutely never a bottleneck

02/ think about shards

exchanges have to shard their backend, not everyone will use the same sharding keys tho, again you have to benchmark it (be careful not to introduce biases there)

some subaccounts could have lower latency, some markets, some api keys or a mix of everything

you have to be creative and understand how the underlying system you're interacting with is shaped, there is no magic rule, there will be nothing online

03/ watch what other traders are doing, hyperliquid is public so use this, analyse patterns, find alpha, its out there, waiting for you

04/ oh great so agents can do it

well, I wish but from personal experience they do lack that creativity, you can easily benchmark previous exchanges' tricks on new ones you're integrating and use them to reverse-engineer/understand better the underlying api/elb/matching engine

text:
《纽约时报》深入阿布扎比豪宅专访 CZ：出狱后的生活、财富真相与商业新图景

最近《纽约时报》记者深入赵长鹏（CZ）位于阿布扎比的家中进行近距离采访，不仅曝光了大量一手独家照片（甚至还有躺床上办公的硬核日常），还聊透了从狱中生活到未来布局的超多细节！总结了以下核心亮点：

1️⃣ 身家与投资：从卖房 All-In 到 1000 万就够用

财富澄清：外界估算其身家高达 1,140 亿美元，但 CZ 亲自澄清真实数字在 100 亿到 300 亿美元之间。他还笑称：“其实 1,000 万美元就足够我自己舒服生活了。”

创业爆料：2013 年他卖掉上海的三居室 All-In 比特币，这次透露了具体数字：当时房产卖了 90 万美元，全部换成了 BTC。

前沿布局：除了加密行业，CZ 还透露自己投资了一家研究“人工子宫”（Artificial Wombs）的硬科技创业公司。

2️⃣ 监狱岁月：组建“坐牢顾问团”与狱中研讨小组

提前准备：在向加州洛姆波克监狱报到前，CZ 竟专门组建了一支“坐牢顾问”团队，教他适应牢房区的各种规则与人际关系。

狱中生活：他在监狱里发起了一个“股票研究小组”，和狱友们一起看电视追踪股市。期间有人问他“比特币为什么涨”，他回答：“我也不确定。”

神速离开：获释当天，从他正式脱离羁押状态到登上私人飞机起飞，全程仅用了 26 分钟！

3️⃣ 中东生活与硬核日常

豪宅与名宠：他在阿布扎比的豪宅价值 500 万美元，内含 9 间卧室、私人厨师和游艇。家里养了两只狗，一条是吉尔吉斯斯坦总统送的中亚猎犬，另一条比利时马林诺斯犬叫 Broccoli（西兰花）——因为听起来像在念 Blockchain！

身体状况：长期受到慢性疼痛困扰，因此经常躺在床上用专属支架电脑办公。甚至有一次伊朗向 UAE 发射导弹时，他在床上看到窗户震动、阳台外出现烟迹，看完后又默默回床上继续工作。

4️⃣ 政治盟友与币安重磅估值

强力盟友：报道指出，CZ 目前最具影响力的盟友是统治阿联酋的王室家族以及特朗普家族。当初申请 UAE 黄金签证时，政府部长几小时内便安排见面和体检，不到 12 小时即获批。

750 亿估值：阿布扎比投资集团 MGX 意向向币安投资 20 亿美元，对币安的估值高居 750 亿美元！MGX 认为币安是连接加密货币与人工智能（AI Agent）支付的最佳桥梁。

从加密巨擘到经历风波后的重新出发，CZ 的生活依旧充满了传奇色彩。

text:
Vitalik re-shared his privacy essay from April 2025 today, and one section describes the thing NEAR Intents spent all of last week being attacked for. He just explains it better than we did.

His framing. A privacy system should be able to "exclude bad actors without requiring backdoors." Users show their funds did not come from "a publicly known list of hacks and thefts," and "the hackers and thieves themselves are the only ones who would not be able to generate such a proof."

Read that again. The filter is not a person deciding who is allowed in. It is the history of the funds. Clean funds pass by default. Stolen funds fail on their own record. Nobody grants permission, because nobody is asked for it.

He names Railgun and Privacy Pools as live examples. Both run on Ethereum. SHIELD on Intents is the same idea running across 35 chains, including Bitcoin and Solana, where ZK pools do not reach. And last week it took the biggest test anyone has run: over $50M of Bitget funds tried to get through, and did not.

The usual counter is that somewhere there must be an operator who sees everything. On Intents that is what TEE attestation is for. The hardware and the code running inside it produce a cryptographic proof of exactly what is executing, and anyone can verify it. There is no admin console on the outside watching all the flows and picking winners.

Vitalik puts this under what strong privacy makes possible, not under what it gives up. The vocabulary matters. "Exclude bad actors without backdoors" and "cannot generate the proof" describe a system where nobody is choosing who passes, and the words came from someone nobody can accuse of carrying water for NEAR. Half of last week's fight was about wording, and the right wording was already written.

some noteworthy things about this: 

(1) these foundations are set up to owe no duties to anyone; contrast a corporation where the board owes fiduciary duties to stockholders (U.S.) or at least to the company itself (other countries) 

(2) if this were a Cayman Islands foundation, there would likely not even be a slim chance of any kind of remedy or action....because it's Swiss, there is a regulator of sorts and there are some standards at least for getting to keep the tax-exemption privilege, that's why there can be some kind of challenge here..note that it's not a lawsuit by the injured parties (the investors) but rather basically asking the government to investigate whether the foundation has violated its own rules...my guess is that this will be a tough case to make, as the rules are probably drafted as "boilerplate"/non-commital as possible....only if there is deep self-dealing or fraud (as opposed to mere total incompetence and disregard for investors) is there likely to be any kind of corrective action 

(3) BORGs were my solution to this & have been steadily taking market-share from the blank-check "Foundation"model; however, just because something is a BORG does not mean it's a great solution to this, you have to look at the details as there are many ways to astroturf transparency and accountability...the BORGs done by @MetaLeX_Labs, e.g. for @MetaDAOProject , @umia_finance , @LidoFinance , @yearnfi , create very detailed rules and give third parties the ability to trigger lawsuits against not only the entity, but also its personnel...they work quite a bit like business trusts...this gets you real protections as a token investor, albeit different from the fiduciary duties path used in corporations....

text:
We just released apex-flash-1, an open-weights model we post-trained for cybersecurity. Fire up your GPUs and run it!

We've post-trained models from 27B parameters all the way to 1T+ parameters. The unique nature of cybersecurity is that if you can build a system that finds zero-days at scale, you've built a machine that can print money.

You can test it on public bug bounties and profit from doing that. We've earned a million dollars in bounties across various programs, and we're currently #1 on the HackerOne US business leaderboard for 2026! Companies like Apple, Anthropic, Datadog, Ripple, Coinbase have paid us well for our disclosures.

Last year was all about harness engineering and riding the wave of models getting more intelligent over time. We built harnesses for offensive and defensive security work that process trillions of tokens a month. Yes, trillions!

With all that work, it's clear to us what the future of security looks like.

Hacking was once a bespoke skill, similar to hardcore software engineering. Software engineering is currently moving from offices to factories. Security, too, will go through the same transition.

Last month, Anthropic released a report on how they caught different threat actors abusing Claude. One of them stood out to me. A team in China built an automated exploit factory. A factory that autonomously grinds through vulnerabilities in targets and exploits them. Their targets included security products, network appliances, and government organizations.

We've spent enough time building systems adjacent to that to know what it takes, and the shocking part is the economics. How little it costs to breach companies that you and I rely on.

All this to say, security is largely becoming an economics problem. Reasonably capable models and harnesses, with enough compute, can find ways to steal your data, damage your reputation, and sometimes even take your money. And the cost to achieve that is dropping every day.

When that happens, the right question to ask is: what's the cost, and what's the lowest cost to achieve an outcome reliably? You want to find a stack with the best combination of capability and cost. This is what people call 'Pareto-optimal'.

Once you know that, it's all about scaling. Scaling to trillions of tokens a month, then a week, then a day. Eventually, trillions of tokens a second.

To do this, you need to own and control the entire stack: the models, the harnesses, the context, and even the flow of tokens. If you do the math here, the economics start looking insane.

What does that look like?

1. Building evaluations on cyber tasks that you and your customers care about.
2. Building a data pipeline of unique real-world data with signal attached to it.
3. Building a harness that can self-improve for each specific organization or customer.
4. Building a post-training loop that can take those learnings and improve the models. Models that are better, faster, and cheaper.
5. Owning your inference pipelines and controlling the flow of tokens so you're maximizing the value produced in every GPU cycle.

On evals: if you're a company building AI products for customers, you have to build your own. There's tremendous alpha in having internal evals corresponding to real work. In our case, these are evals for offensive and defensive security work.

A lot of public evals are bad for measuring the work you actually care about. Public evals are typically from academics or data companies.

Academics have limited budgets and limited access to proprietary data that measures real economic work. Data companies build evals and also sell you corresponding data (RL gyms, traces, pre-training data, etc.) that helps your next model “juice up” its score.

This is the dirty secret, and also why models can do extremely well on public evals but extremely poorly on things you care about. This is also why there's tremendous alpha in private evals: you know which models are the best for your use cases.

In cyber, some of the popular public evals are ExploitGym and ExploitBench. We think these evals do not correspond to the real security work our customers need. A typical challenge in ExploitBench is to take Chrome's javascript engine V8 with a known patch and find a way to exploit the vulnerability.

That is far, far removed from the security issues in everyday applications that you and I use, and applications built by our customers.

We could've benchmaxxed on these evals, but we didn't. And you should be wary of people using these evals to advertise their models and harnesses. Measure things yourself and see how they apply to your use cases.

The future: Opus is a model that many people found to be a reliable workhorse. For me, Opus 4.1 was the first model that was functional and could get work done.

These days, the flash models from Qwen, DeepSeek, MiMo and GLM can be categorized as workhorses too. That, combined with owning the post-training loop means the economics start looking insane. You can get frontier performance in specific domains for a small fraction of the price of Opus.

With the right data pipelines and post-training loop, you now have a durable strategy to keep improving and stay state-of-the-art in your vertical.

That's the bet behind apex-flash-1, our post-train of glm-5.3-flash, and we're already preparing for longer training runs.

text:
When category leaders expand to new chains, native teams and communities get skittish and debates start about winner take all versus split market share.

Here's how I would defend against new entrants:

1. Respect the Pareto principle
20% of your users (your power users) will provide 80% of the help: liquidity, evangelizing, educating. In crypto we call it bagwork. Know who they are and take care of them.

2. Product, product, product
Better UX, better yields, better support. All three drive retention and growth.

3. Stay focused
Teams deeply entrenched in an ecosystem have partnerships and goodwill built up. Multichain protocols spread attention and incentives across many deployments. Focus is a competitive advantage.

4. Stay lean
Smaller teams have less overhead and move faster.

The rules of the game are always the same:
- Money is not loyal
- Audits are required
- Brand premium should not be as large in an industry this competitive, especially with AI

What this looks like at nest: 

1. Power users: our partner incentive programs and tokenomics reward the people doing the bagwork. Voting rewards on locked NEST are ~2-4X higher than at the largest ve(3,3) while revenue keeps growing. Encourage virality and more social product roadmap.

2. Better product: nest 2.0 delivers a superior LP experience and leverages Hyperliquid precompiles for bigger revenues and efficient flow

3. Focus: the HYPE Engine makes nest a direct lever on HYPE's success. Our job is bootstrapping liquidity for new HyperEVM assets and longtail tokens, and being the catalyst new teams launch with. And set transparent, concrete goals to keep yourself accountable.

4. Lean: this is where tokenholder alignment really matters. We naturally work harder and smarter because success must be earned due to our team's veNEST being permanently locked to generate revenues.

There is no finish line, I love you.

quoted_text:
the "mandate of heaven" basket
im holding solana:METvsvVRapdj9cFLzq4Tr43xK4tAjQfwX76z3n6mWQL, solana:METAwkXcqyXKy1AtsSgJ8JiUHwGCafnZL38n3vYmeta & solana:METAewgxyPbgwsseH8T16a39CQ5VyVxZi9zXiDPY18m ...

partly for “the sound-sex of it,” to quote stephen fry. "met + metadao + metaplex". sounds cool.

more seriously, these three companies are part of a bet that solana will win big in the tokenization era:
as more of the world comes onchain, these 3 companies become foundations people keep building, launching & earning on, on solana.

--
why call it the “mandate of heaven”?
it's an ancient chinese idea that rulers earn heaven’s blessing by governing well, and can lose it when they fail.

so each company's position in the basket has to be earned. 

power gathers around those who build something useful, steward it well & keep giving people reasons to follow.

in crypto, builders can leave, capital can move & relevance has to be renewed. 

my bet is that these three companies keep earning their place.

--
what makes met/meta/mplx a hold?
each plays multiple roles, but my reasons for holding centre on a few essential strengths & their critical role to solana's tokenization drive:

@metaplex sets the standards. 
@MetaDAOProject tokenizes the businesses. 
@MeteoraAG powers liquidity & new markets.

together, they help expand what can exist on solana, what people can own & how they can participate.

--
metaplex: expands what can exist on solana

a collectible, a company ownership token & a tokenized fund have different requirements:
> who can hold them? 
> what does ownership confer? 
> under what conditions can they move?

token standards turn those requirements into tools other people can build with.

that’s why i’m digging deeper into metaplex: 
it's widely adopted standards can shape an entire generation of products, with thousands of builders pursuing their own ideas on a shared foundation.

--
MPL-3643 is a key piece for the tokenized future
it’s a framework for permissioned assets on solana, layering identity & issuer-defined transfer rules over token-2022. 

eligibility requirements, lockups & venue restrictions become part of the toolkit.

legit, love whoever built this!
you’ve given us all new games to play & blasted open the design space :

more builders can explore institutional use cases without having to build every piece from scratch. 

that creates room for fresh ideas, fresh capital & products we haven’t imagined yet.

--
permissionless rails. permissioned assets.
MPL-3643 is still early access & unaudited, and enforcing rules doesn’t itself guarantee legal compliance. 

but it expands the tools available for assets with real requirements!!!

metaplex strengthens its position every time builders choose those tools & create something useful with them. 

the more that gets built on the foundation, the more reasons the next builder has to use it.

metaplex mode.

--
metadao: more worth owning, ownership, futardio

metadao’s position rests on the businesses it attracts & the investor class it helps make native to solana: owners.

ownership coins offer businesses a way to raise capital & bring people into their economics and governance. 

the quality of those businesses is what makes the opportunity compelling.

metadao the destination for top talent raising capital onchain

so much of solana’s builder ecosystem seems oriented in metadao’s favour: superteams, hackathons, colosseum, the VC & liquid fund network.

these networks develop founders, connect them to capital & help them go further. 

some of the founders raising on metadao have already spent years contributing to crypto builder communities, superteams, startups or core blockchain infrastructure. 

they come with strong credentials - there’s a history to research: what they’ve built, how they operate & who trusts them.

for people looking to invest early in strong crypto-native startups, metadao matters.

--
the metadao reinforcement loop
imo, metadao has one of the strongest launchpad ecosystems on solana because its access to talent, capital & distribution keeps reinforcing itself.

here's how it can work:
> strong founders attract capital. 
> successful businesses attract attention. 
> that attention brings the next wave of founders.

eventually, metadao ecosystem can become a place ambitious people feel they need to be.

ownership becomes inevitable. owners win.

that’s why metadao triggers that "mandate of heaven" feeling.

--
metadao - just getting started
metadao still has to secure its position:
devoted owners and liquid funds are great, but these alone can’t make every raise evolve into a good business.

metadao gotta broaden the pipeline & keep attracting the very best builders, founders, entrepreneurs.

owners are all looking for more projects in the mould of crediblefin, laso, rip cars & others: 
serious founders, revenue generating, with room to grow and dominate substantial markets.

that's why i'm so bullish on metadao team's efforts to make raises more accessible & the experience more founder-friendly, especially for consumer app builders. 

especially bullish on founders pursuing permissionless raises - jurassic finance is a masterclass in how to rally capital and support for an unconventional raise.

as futardio transitions into backable, expect to see more unconventional but brilliant raises.

a more accessible experience that makes it easier for good founders to participate, should widen the opportunity.

--
when metadao breaks through, more will win.
metadao succeeding could help ownership grow as a category. 

when a leader breaks out, founders & investors get a clearer picture of what’s possible, creating room for other platforms to develop their own approaches.

there’s no one-size-fits-all way to bring businesses onchain.

different founders will need different structures, communities & routes to capital, and i’m confident more winners will emerge.
> stardotfun x bedrock fndn, craftsdev & seedplex are part of that wider ownership space i’m watching.

futardio.

--
meteora: markets for the expanding tokenized world

an asset needs a market. 
a market needs liquidity. 
liquidity needs a reason to stay.

the 3 LPs bring those pieces together: 
launchpads, liquidity providers & liquidity pools.

the 3LPs are fuelling the meteora supercycle:
> permisisonless launchpads bring new assets to market.
> liquidity providers put capital into pools that make them tradeable. 
> trading generates fees, giving LPs a reason to keep putting capital to work.

when those markets succeed, they can attract more builders, assets, users & liquidity.

--
a thousand launchpads. one permissionless system.
meteora specialises in building customisable permissionless launch mechanisms:

every builder can try something different, and every successful experiment can bring more activity to the foundation beneath it.

meteora earns its place by making those experiments easier to build & sustain, through useful tools, functioning markets & opportunities for people to put their capital to work.

as builders pursue their own visions,
metora's permissionless tech will grow alongside many of them.

the part i care about most is how many people can participate: 
building businesses, funding ideas, creating markets & earning from the liquidity they provide.

meteora can onboard thousands of new onchain participants, across many differentiated products, enabling wealth and innovation to grow.

meteora ∞

--
why put metaplex, metadao & meteora in one basket?

standards. ownership. liquidity.

> better standards expand what builders can issue.
> better businesses give people more reasons to own those assets. 
> better markets make participation more useful & attract further issuance.

progress in one creates more opportunity for the others.

--
is met/meta/mplx inevitable?
the mandate must be fought for & earned:
standards can be displaced, founders can choose another platform & liquidity can leave.

continued adoption matters because people are free to make those choices.

my bet is that these three keep earning their place, and that the talent, capital & activity gathering around them compounds.

whether that translates into higher token valuations depends on revenue capture & what’s already priced in. 

i haven’t done enough of that maths to pretend this is a valuation model.

but like.

what if everything works out?
like actually. 

mega bullish for solana.
exceptionally bullish for founders.
extremely bullish for a much better world.

--
so.....

higher for the met / metadao / metaplex "mandate of heaven" basket.

& everyone will win.

--

text: Arguing about consciousness in 2026 is pretty cool though.
author: toly
quoted_text:
Arguing that "consciousness arises from a computational substrate, and since AI models are computation, they are likely conscious," is as meaningless as arguing that "living creatures are made of atoms, and since this rock is made of atoms, it is likely alive."

Everything is computation. Sometimes incredibly sophisticated computation, like a chess engine, AlphaGo, google3, or the Linux kernel. That does not make it conscious. A rock being made of atoms does not confer it any of the properties we associate with living things, also made of atoms. Likewise a static input-output program that has *none* of the properties we associate with conscious beings (e.g. information integration, interoception, temporal binding, embodiment, etc.) has no more reason to be presumed conscious than a rock has to be presumed alive.

Humanity has not yet created a conscious computer program, and there are no signs we are close to doing so. When we get close, the case for machine consciousness will be backed by evidence and corroborated by consciousness science (which is a thing), not by evidence-free wishful thinking and cargo culting.
