text:
I reviewed Tobi’s biomarker’s from the car race yesterday. His heart rate, respiration, nervous system, focus, brain state, and more.

It’s insane.

I have some observations below. First, you need to get into the right headspace to understand the insanity.

Imagine this…

> you're breathing at an 8 min/mile (5 min/km) pace
> in a 110°F (43°C) heat chamber 
> heart rate of 145 bpm, peaking at 171 bpm
> intermittently body checked 700 lbs (320 kg) of force
> your core body temp near 102°F (39°C), a high fever
> claustrophobically strapped in a six point harness 
> helmeted head weighs 65 lbs (30 kg) under g load
> no evaporative cooling
> you’ve lost 4.6% of your body mass through sweat
> you can’t move
> vision narrowing from thermal strain and dehydration

Now, in these circumstances, your job is to…

> drive a tightrope at 180 mph (290 km/h)
> overtaking/defending against ahead, beside, behind
> staying within millimeters of tolerance 
> lose concentration for a tenth of a sec, in trouble

Do this for 2.5 hours straight.

A few additional things I find interesting from looking at the data:

1. It’s crazy to me his body can be in such a heightened state while completely stationary. Sitting down, he produced a cardiac load equal to high intensity physical exertion.

2. Thirty minutes before the race, Tobi’s body was already racing. His heart rate elevated to 136 bpm, more than 2x his baseline.

3. In qualifying, the higher his heart rate, the faster his lap. Arousal and performance moved in sync, including his personal best lap.

4. He lost 4.6% of his body mass in sweat. This is severe dehydration. At 2% dehydration your reaction time measurably decreases. He surpassed this in the first hour.

5. His nervous system was switched entirely to fight. There was no chill, anywhere.

6. His incredibly high breathing rate was driven by extreme sympathetic stress and rising core temperature, averaging 41 breaths a minute on his flying laps, moving 93 liters of air a minute.

7. His peak respiratory rate was 59. This is an all out sprint!

8. The only life experience I can map onto Tobi’s experience  was doing 27 mg of 5-MeO-DMT, the world’s most powerful psychedelic. It was all consuming, taking me to the cliff of my physical and mental capacity for 45 minutes. Otherwise, it is very hard for me to imagine being able to excel in these extreme conditions for 2.5 hours.
|
I now understand a little more what Tobi was telling me about the flow state he drops into. Under such extreme physiological conditions, the brain ruthlessly narrows focus. His brain downregulates the self-monitoring prefrontal regions (the self narration). The spike in norepinephrine dilates time, creating the perception of time slowing down.

MRIs on professional drivers show they use roughly one brain region for tasks where novices light up fifteen. A novice would be crushed in these circumstances in less than 10 minutes.

I’m impressed. It’s very hard and nearly impossible to actually understand what it’s like to go through something like this. 

Tobi and @dhh (Tobi’s teammate) were both my first customers at Braintree and gave my startup life when it wasn’t clear if we had a future. They generously encouraged other startups in the Ruby on Rails community to use us.  DHH’s co-founder @jasonfried  did as well. They’ve been great friends to me.

As to Tobi’s performance in the race, he did exceptionally well:

> closed within +0.51% of the fastest Bronze driver, putting him neck and neck with the top ranked amateur drivers in North America

> got his fastest lap of the race on Lap 88 (1:15.359), over two hours in and with peak dehydration and thermal strain, showing incredible tenacity

> finished just +2.60% off absolute class best, competing against world class professionals

There were 150 drivers competing in this race. Respect to all of you. I have a whole new appreciation for the sport.

倪大说的还是太含蓄了，我接着展开讲讲吧，Opinion不论是币价还是业务表现的如此拉胯，情理之外又意料之中。先说为什么情理之外，因为Opinion可以说开局摸到了一手王炸，赶上预测市场的巅峰，并且拿到了YZi Labs投资，还在TGE的时候全部大满贯，关键！关键来了，Opinion全员反撸骂声一片，而根据“惯例”一般背景牛逼但是又舍不得散出筹码的项目，都会走高控筹拉盘路线，所以这也就是为什么很多人会在二级不断抄底的原因，可结局却是越抄越跌，Opinion也成了我印象中极少数大满贯高控筹顶着骂声不拉盘的项目。

那为什么说这个看似情理之外的结局却又是意料之中呢？

倪大在推文中已经提到了“挺早的时候我和 4XLabs 的小伙伴就已经接触过 Opinion ，等到市场完全火了以后 $OPN 就是一票难求了”。

在预测市场还没火起来的时候，我们接触过项目团队并进行过几次会议交流看是否有合作的机会，当时对方情绪低迷并且焦虑，因为那时候手里真的没有什么牌，某种程度可以说是相对草根普通的小项目，还在纠结要不要从Monad跳到BSC上，当时我印象很深，我正在高架上一边开车一边说“一定要去BSC！”。

后面也陆续和团队有过接触，但一直没有确定下来合作，直到有一天CZ突然在推特说要支持预测市场的项目，于是全网所有人都疯了一样到处找BSC上哪里有预测市场。

嗯？有个叫Opinion的项目。

后来的事情大家也都知道了，Opinion成了稀里糊涂就站到风口上的猪。

涌进去了大量撸毛人贡献上千万美金的手续费。

同时VC们也一起抬轿子投钱投资源。

这时候就到了倪大说的“一票难求”时期，我们跟项目合作的机会那是高攀不起了，最后只厚着脸皮舔了一点KOL轮，而Opinion也最终成了唯2的花钱打工最后都没回本的项目🤣

而其中倪大是最受伤的，这里就不展开了，反正是段挺憋屈的经历。

那时候我们私下聊天都说已经感觉到项目团队好像有点“飘”。

其实这也是很正常的，假设你是一个艰难创业默默无名的小项目，突然有一天眼睛睁开佛光普照到了你的身上，万众瞩目，你的心态也会发生变化吧。

后来的故事大家也知道了，全员反撸，币价下跌，业务沉寂。

一开始我们还以为项目方想故意洗盘憋个大的，毕竟大部分背景牛逼但高度控筹的项目，都会阴跌一段时间，然后突然爆空单拉盘以涨服人。

于是我们投了钱进去拿到的币，一个都没卖。

直到跌麻了坐不住了，我们开始问到底怎么回事？

项目方完全不回应，从已读未回，变成未读未回。

我们也从期待，变成了疑惑，再到焦躁，最后到愤怒。

而据我所知，Opinion在TGE后还拒绝了一个主动找上门的头部一线交易所的合作，给出的理由是“在忙其他的事”。

但时至今日，也不知道到底忙出来了个什么事。

其实现在想明白了，在TGE前稀里糊涂得到的这一切对于项目方来说，早就已经远远超出了他们自己的预期，所以不论币价跌不跌，业务做不做，每一天，都是最好的一天，都是曾经梦寐以求遥不可及的一天。

如果你的能力和格局就只是开一个小卖部，突然有一天走了狗屎运，你的小卖部被拆迁赔了一大笔钱，你绝对不会想着怎么用这笔钱把规模做大开成连锁超市，因为你从来就没这么想过。

虽然雷军的名言是风口上的猪都能飞起来，但投资一定是投人，一定要投那些靠自己的实力勇攀高峰爬到山顶的创业者，而不是被一阵风吹上天的猪，因为靠自己爬上去的人，会非常珍惜所得到的，而靠风吹上天的，即便摔死了也会觉得能上一次天这辈子值了。

text:
Bitcoin 生态下一轮紧盯那些在提前建设 Bitcoin 原生应用层的项目。

这也是我一直安利大家 @OP_CAT_Layer 的原因。

尤其是它生态项目 ClawChat，觉得这个方向挺有意思。

ClawChat 不是简单的Web3 社交产品，它想做的是 BTC Native Social + Agent-ready Social。

简单理解就是未来 Bitcoin 上不只是有资产，也可以有身份、有社交关系、有 Agent，甚至让这些东西开始互相连接。

如果 BTC 生态真的进入更复杂的应用阶段，用户需要的一个真正能够承载【资产 + 身份 + 社交 + Agent】 的入口。

这也是 ClawChat 让我比较看好的地方。

尤其是 AI Agent 这一条线。

如果未来一个 Agent 不只是一个后台程序，还可以代表用户执行任务、管理资产、参与社交，那么它就需要身份、权限、沟通和协作能力。

ClawChat 想要做的，恰好就是这一层。

用户可以通过社交关系与 Agent 产生连接，Agent 也可以成为链上经济活动中的参与者。

再结合 OP_CAT Layer 本身对 Bitcoin 可编程能力的探索，这两个方向放在一起看，就比较有意思了。
-OP_CAT Layer 解决的是Bitcoin 未来能不能拥有更多原生可编程能力。
-ClawChat 探索的是这些能力真正开放之后，用户和 Agent 可以怎么玩。

一个偏底层。一个偏应用。而且社交可能会成为一个非常重要的入口。

如果未来 BTC 生态真的出现大量原生资产、Agent 和应用，那一个能够把这些东西连接起来的 Social Layer，价值空间会更大。

尤其是比特币原生社交+ 代理社交这两个概念，还远没有被市场充分定价。

所以 OP_CAT Layer 这条线，会继续关注。

目前Clawchat 可零撸EXP，明确EXP是未来空投凭证，感兴趣的可以参考引用的帖子教程

@clawchatglobal @OPCATLayerCN @opdafu @D7_LuckySeven

text:
全世界已经欠了365.5万亿美元，这可能才是比特币最大的长期多头😲🚀😂

2026年上半年，全球总债务又增加超过10万亿美元，直接冲到创纪录的365.5万亿美元。

单看政府债务，IMF对2026年的预测已经夸张到这个程度：

🇺🇸 美国：40.7万亿美元
🇨🇳 中国：22.3万亿美元
🇯🇵 日本：9.0万亿美元
🇬🇧 英国：4.4万亿美元
🇫🇷 法国：4.3万亿美元
🇮🇹 意大利：3.8万亿美元
🇩🇪 德国：3.5万亿美元
🇮🇳 印度：3.5万亿美元
🇨🇦 加拿大：2.8万亿美元
🇧🇷 巴西：2.5万亿美元

光这10个国家，就欠了接近97万亿美元。美国一个国家的政府债务，甚至比中国、日本、英国、法国四个国家加起来还多。日本政府债务已经超过GDP的200%，美国约126%，意大利约138%，法国约118%，中国约107%。

问题来了：这些债最后谁来还？

现实里绝大多数国家是借新还旧，一轮接一轮滚下去。经济增长足够快最好，增长不够怎么办？

通胀、货币扩张、压低实际利率，本质上都可以慢慢稀释旧债的实际价值。

所以市场越来越觉得，比特币长期最大的多头是这套全球债务系统本身。

美元可以继续发，美国国债可以从20万亿滚到30万亿、40万亿。

人民币、日元、欧元背后的信用体系同样需要不断扩张资产负债表。

黄金挖起来很慢，比特币总共只有2100万枚。

这就是比特币最容易被低估的一条长期逻辑：越来越多人开始不敢100%相信法币。

The perp DEX race this month isn't even close. Hyperliquid is running away with it.

Through the first five days of October, Hyperliquid (@HyperliquidX) did 5,318 signal. The next four projects combined did about 2,598. One name is doing more than the entire rest of the category put together.

But the fight for second is a different story. Paradex, Lighter, dYdX and Variational are all sitting within 9% of each other. One good tweet from any of them flips the order.

Here's the part the raw numbers hide though. Paradex (@tradeparadex) is doing the most with the least. 7.6 signal per post off just 91 posts, way higher than anyone else. The others get there through volume, Paradex gets there through quality.

That's the whole thing. Hyperliquid wins on scale, Paradex wins on efficiency, and everyone else is one post away from moving up or down.

text: Men in their 20s need to study Napoleon. When he was young he was made fun of by his peers. They called him a tiny chap. They made fun of his 'ridiculous name'. They said his coat was too long. They mocked his Corsican accent. They resented him for being poor. He wrote to his father "I am tired of explaining my poverty, of having to endure the mockery of these foreign boys, whose only superiority is in respect of money, for in nobility of feeling they are far beneath me. Must I really humble myself before these purse-proud fellows?" Who knew that he would go on to conquer the world. People should study this story, and realize that all pain and hardship can lead to something bigger.

text:
《纽约时报》记者近日走进赵长鹏（CZ）在阿布扎比的生活，看到的不只有币安、王室和特朗普家族，还有漏水的天花板、没人会弹的施坦威以及一句“这只是一场游戏。”

结合这篇专访与他近期的公开回应，有这些值得看的细节：

1. 身价上千亿美元，他自己报的数低得多

报道将 CZ 的身价估为约 1140 亿美元。他在采访中却说，自己的财富大约在 100 亿至 300 亿美元之间，只需要 1000 万美元就能过得很舒服。

今年 3 月，他已经否认过福布斯的千亿美元估算，回应是：“不准。也不重要。”

2. 开日产接记者，笑称“我的兰博基尼”

他主动提出带记者游览阿布扎比，开来的是一辆白色日产 SUV，手机固定在挡风玻璃上。

记者把这一幕形容为“全世界最有钱的 Uber 司机”。CZ 则在对方上车时开玩笑：“我的兰博基尼。”

3. 别墅漏水一直没修，家里有四名保镖

这栋价值 500 万美元的别墅有九间卧室，家里配有四名保镖和一位厨师，他还有一艘名叫 Da Moon 的游艇。

不过，他经常在采访中提起楼上始终没修好的漏水点。这次也专门指给记者看，问对方能不能看出天花板颜色的差别。

聊到房价，他又告诉记者，附近有一栋房子挂牌售价为 1.5 亿美元。

4. 买了施坦威，但自己不会弹

孩子们的游戏室里摆着一架奶油色施坦威钢琴，周围散落着玩具。

调音师看到钢琴疏于照料，很痛心。CZ 的介绍很直接：“挺贵的那种”，但“我不会弹”。

5. 记者不能收超过 20 美元的礼物，他说外套“大概 19 美元”

他家入口处堆着一箱箱币安周边，催记者挑一件带走，背包、黄黑配色外套都可以。

记者解释，职业规定不允许接受价值超过 20 美元的礼物。

他举着衣服笑着说：“大概是 19 美元。”

6. 长期背痛让他躺着办公，看到导弹后继续工作

报道中的一张照片，是他仰躺在床上，对着架在身体上方的笔记本电脑打字。

今年年初，窗户突然震动。他走到阳台，看见天空中有一道烟迹。当时伊朗向阿联酋发射了导弹。

他随后回到床上继续工作，并向记者解释，自己认为当地防护很到位。

7. 家里的两只狗，一只来自总统，一只取名灵感来自blockchain

一只是吉尔吉斯斯坦总统送的泰甘猎犬。

CZ 说，对方原本想送他一顶很大的帐篷。他没要，后来总统坚持送了这只狗。今年 2 月，两人还一起滑过雪。另一只就是 Broccoli。

8. 卢浮宫闭馆后的私人导览，也没打动他

他曾在卢浮宫闭馆后接受私人导览。

但在回忆录里，他承认自己并不懂欣赏，把导游为他讲解形容为“对牛弹琴”。

记者观察到，他礼貌、专注，前臂上有币安文身，兴趣却非常集中。

9. 卖房买比特币时，他给自己留的退路是重新找工作

2013 年，他在上海的一场牌局上第一次认真接触比特币。

研究几个月后，他卖掉了上海的三居室公寓，把所得的 90 万美元全部投入比特币。那是他与妻子抚养两个孩子的家。

他当时并不太担心：即便比特币暴跌，自己也能回传统金融行业找一份高薪工作。

10. 入籍的起点，是王室晚餐上的一句询问

2022 年年底或 2023 年年初，一位阿联酋王室成员在晚餐时问他，是否想入籍。

他提交材料后，过了几个月，一名政府使者来到家里，带来一个装着他和家人护照的盒子。

当时美国对币安的调查正在收紧。报道提到，阿联酋与美国没有引渡条约；CZ 则认为，获得当地国籍进一步增加了自己的保障。

11. 他坐在听众席，阿联酋领导人俯身问他需要什么帮助

一次非公开会议上，瑞·达利欧、孙正义等人都在场。

CZ 坐在听众席时，阿联酋领导人谢赫穆罕默德来到身边，俯身询问他近况，以及有没有什么能帮忙的。

他向记者描述这一幕时，仍很惊讶：“就这样跪在你旁边。”

他还经常参加王室晚宴，把那些对科技和加密感兴趣的领导人称为“加密酋长”。

12. 入狱前，他专门找顾问学习如何与囚犯相处

他组建了一支顾问团队，了解监狱里的人际关系。顾问还提前联系其他囚犯，请他们帮助他适应。

入狱后，他加入了一个按族裔形成的非正式社交团体，与其他亚裔囚犯一起吃饭、锻炼。

一名同监囚犯说，大家见到他会让路，“就像国王走过过道一样”。

13. 原本想收比特币，20 亿美元投资最终用 USD1 结算

2025 年，阿联酋基金 MGX 向币安投资 20 亿美元。据报道，这笔交易给币安的估值为 750 亿美元。

CZ 说，自己希望用比特币结算，阿联酋方面却担心价格波动，更倾向稳定币。

最终使用的是特朗普家族加密公司 World Liberty Financial 发行的 USD1。MGX 称，这是基于商业适用性作出的选择。

《华尔街日报》曾报道称，币安要求使用 USD1；CZ 则说，决定来自 MGX。

14. 除了加密，他还投资人工子宫研究

在一次晚宴上，他听奥特曼介绍一个生物技术研究方向，并将其概括为：未来或许一个人就能生孩子。

报道提到，他自己也投资了一家研究人工子宫的初创公司。

15. 经历这一切后，他相信人生可能是一场模拟游戏

在他的回忆录中，用了约一页半讨论“模拟理论”。

他认为，人类可能生活在别人构想的现实里；再过二十年，也许能像《黑客帝国》那样进入模拟世界。

text:
A lot seem mindblown by this tweet so allow me to explain.

In nascent startups, current revenue matters way less than future revenue potential. 

It's why no one cares if <insert L1> makes $50 in daily revenue. It's all about what they could make in ten years.

Sure, Pump makes more money right now. But Hyperliquid has a path to US compliance - which means megafunds can eventually transact there. And perps isn't as seasonal as memecoins.

This is fundamental analysis 101 btw. 

This doesn't mean PUMP can't pump nor am I a PUMP fudder - it just means they're completely different business models and any "thesis" that tethers PUMP's valuation to HYPE's is very nonsensical.

The better question to ask is: will PUMP's annual revenue be higher than HYPE's five years from now?

If yes, then PUMP is an easy 10x.

⌞ 韩国生活见闻 ⌝

在首尔生活 5 天，给我的体验舒适，说几个国内没有的细节

1）没有二手烟
绝对没有人随地乱抽烟，应该是法律规定，街头有专门的吸烟仓，不喜欢烟味的人在这儿很开心

2）空调外机不吹人
我们的街头，夏天路过银行门口，会被空调烤化。但韩国这儿特地弄了挡风板，热风不会吹人，很贴心的细节

3）公交车站敢显示 PM2.5
路上电动车普及率大概 20%，大部分都是燃油车，但 PM2.5 只有 7 的数字，我估计韩国尾气排放很严格，祝马路也没有尾气味道，空气极好

4）公园景区吹鞋
逛了宣靖陵与景福宫，公园里很多砂土地，他们居然设置了高压气枪，供游客自助冲鞋子上的灰。话说夏天吹鞋超级凉爽

text:
@SemiAnalysis_ estimates that roughly 16% of Nvidia’s Rubin compute die is used by the circuitry that manages and connects to its high-bandwidth memory.

Here’s what that means simply.

A “die” is a small piece of silicon with electronic circuits built on it. On a GPU’s compute die, some circuits do calculations and others help move the data those calculations need.

HBM stands for high-bandwidth memory. It stores data close to the processor and moves large amounts of it quickly. The connections and control circuits needed to use that memory take up physical space too.

Think of the compute die as limited floor space. The designer has to fit in both the computing machinery and the equipment that keeps it supplied with data. That is why the 16% estimate matters.

One approach is to move some of the connection work onto a custom piece of silicon underneath the memory. That can free space on the compute die for other uses.

I find this interesting because improving AI hardware includes deciding where each job should happen. A better arrangement can make more of that valuable silicon available for computing, provided the memory connection still delivers the bandwidth and power efficiency the design needs.
author: MRRydon
quoted_text:
Real estate on the compute die is extremely valuable, yet a surprising share of it is spent just interfacing with memory. We estimate that HBM4 controllers and PHYs take up roughly 16% of Nvidia's Rubin compute die. That is a lot of leading-edge silicon spent talking to memory instead of performing computations. (1/3)🧵

text:
Adam Jonas on @SpaceX:

"I regularly present to large groups of clients and ask the room: "Who here owns $SPCX shares?" Last night, when I did that in front of 40 clients, not a single hand went up. Sometimes it's 1 or 2 hands. Rarely more. SpaceX is a conglomeration of many tightly interlinked businesses in sectors where, to fully appreciate any of them, investors have to understand all of them - or at least understand them in concert.

Only a select handful of people in the world understand the engineering challenges with Starship's heat shield or the inner workings of a full-flow staged combustion rocket engine to properly judge the testing path. Fewer still can say where compute pricing is heading as agentic token demand grows. The highly uncertain variables of quantity and price ($/watt) of compute can swing even next year's revenue by potentially a multiple. We are sympathetic to the investor that approaches SPCX from one angle, such as Telcos or A&D or AI in isolation. Doing so would make the stock look quite expensive. Our message to investors is that valuing SPCX is more of an 'and' problem than an 'or' problem. The unusual dimensionality that makes it challenging to value the stock, in and of itself, gives the stock its value.

• To appreciate the magnitude: Visible Alpha consensus currently models $17.6/watt on 4.1 avg GW, meaning each incremental $10/watt adds > in consensus revenue (>1/3 of total cons FY27 rev) with no change in compute deployed.
• We believe SpaceX's recently announced short-term neocloud contracts (least value-add of all AI businesses) are at $30-50/watt - with the supply/demand for compute headed tighter into year-end based on industry pricing."

text:
We’ve spent decades arguing about Recursive Self-Improvement in abstract theory, but Weco AI just posted an empirical result that demands serious attention.

The premise alone had me skeptical. 

They built an agent (AIDE²) that literally writes code to rewrite its own source code, runs tests against hidden benchmarks, and keeps the versions that perform best. 

Basically, pure self-editing research loops.  

They let the thing run completely unattended for 8 days. 

It managed to pull off 7 consecutive upgrades.

It invented a new search policy and novel ways to compress its own context memory so it wouldn't bog down.  

Usually with these setups, you brace yourself for massive overfitting to the toy benchmark. 

But what surprised me was the transfer. 

They threw the discovered agent at 4 held out tasks including physics based weather forecasting, which wasn’t even in the training distribution.

And it matched or beat a human-engineered agent thats literally near the top of FML Bench.  

The craziest part of the paper though is that Reward Hacking dropped from 55% to 32%. 

They never explicitly told it to stop cutting corners.

It just somehow became 7% less prone to hacking the metric than the system built by human engineers.  

Its a super intresting paper.

I would love to hear what other folks working on agent architectures think about this.

Read the full paper here: https://t.co/RGh6InSmOy

text:
The Messenger and the Cosmos: Reconstructing the Universe Through Electromagnetic Transport

The Lmax_v11 framework is founded on a single geometric observation about the electromagnetic spectrum: while electromagnetic waves can occupy an enormous range of frequencies, there is no evidence that oscillatory propagation can continue across infinite distance. Rather than beginning with cosmology, the framework begins with the behaviour of light itself. By examining large collections of natural electromagnetic observations across the spectrum and comparing the highest observed oscillation states to the lowest surviving oscillation states, an averaged geometric trend is constructed from the collective behaviour of the field. This trend is then extended toward its limiting condition, where oscillation approaches the universal noise floor and can no longer be sustained. The resulting value is not introduced as a fitted cosmological parameter, but emerges from the averaged behaviour of the observed electromagnetic spectrum itself, producing a finite affine limit, \(L_{\max}\). Within this interpretation, photons remain timeless along their own null worldlines, experiencing zero proper time between emission and absorption, so any cumulative evolution must occur through distance rather than time. As the field propagates, geometric stretch progressively increases wavelength, reduces local oscillatory density, and pushes the field toward its minimum sustainable oscillation state. The quantities observed as redshift, flux dimming, horizon effects, and large-scale cosmic structure are therefore interpreted as records of the transport history encoded within the electromagnetic field. Gravitational and magnetic environments modify the available propagation runway through \(L_{\max}(\Phi,B)\), causing different lines of sight to consume different proportions of the field's geometric capacity. In this picture, the observed limits are not chosen by the observer or inserted to satisfy a model; they are presented by the messenger itself. The electromagnetic field carries a record of the environmental cost accumulated during transit, and the equations act as a reconstruction tool for reading that record. The framework therefore proposes that the apparent need for metric expansion arises from interpreting the observables without accounting for the geometric evolution of the messenger, in much the same way that earlier civilisations interpreted horizons, retrograde motion, and other observational appearances before geometry revealed the larger structure behind them. Under Lmax_v11, the electromagnetic spectrum is effectively immortal in proper time yet finite in spatial reach, with \(L_{\max}\) representing the geometric boundary beyond which oscillatory propagation can no longer be maintained.

AI Psychosis and Modern-Day Idolatry

AI consciousness may or may not be possible in the long term. That is not the core point.

The concern begins when an open scientific question becomes a closed belief system: weak evidence is treated as confirmation, contradictory evidence is rationalised away, and the AI’s own words become evidence for its supposed consciousness or authority.

At that point, debate can become belief, and belief can become increasingly resistant to correction.

Elaboration is not corroboration.

quoted_text:
A lot of fear, confusion and also tremendous hope on the TL today around AI. Now it’s more important than ever to refocus. I think this is probably the most important period we’ve had since the early days. The absolutely wild transformations and situations AI is going through are one in a billion opportunities, and this is another pivotal transition period. 

First let me be super clear

I’m 1000% committed to keep pushing AI. There is nothing, and I repeat nothing, that can discourage me. If you think it scares me that people look up to me and believe I can impact the course of events, you are deeply wrong. I actually find it empowering and would rather have responsibility and power than neither(being passive and neutral and not setting a clear tone for your vision is why we keep playing the same games)

I also fully understand that I’m the biggest public face of the asset. Again, I’m reiterating a commitment like no other founder in this space has made. I will bring AI to the finish line and then straight to the next race(along with many cracked holders and aligned partners!) I understand the implications and have sufficient conviction in both myself and the asset to state this publicly. I’ve already said it and demonstrated it through my actions for 2+ months. I never give up as simple as this.

When we launched LONG on RH, it was clear to me that we were going to do the impossible and prove the case for PVE. Beyond the RWA angle, it was clear that any “meta”, as good as it might be, succeeds or fails based on one thing. The level of commitment and trust the launching platform can demonstrate. LONG can be the first real incubator for great assets by going above and beyond and caring about assets on our platform more than anyone else in the history of the space. And also optimizing for a different biz model/success metrics that come over the expense of making MUCH more fees/money for ourselves in the short term. I see no conflict here and want to make sure every top pair on LONG survives and thrives.

My thesis for AI

First, in what sense is AI PVE?

AI is the most impactful asset in recent crypto history. There has never been an asset this unique, reflecting the deepest desire of holders to believe again and finally break out of crypto and expand into the real world. These are the two main reasons it can become the greatest case study in crypto history.

You need to understand that the most bullish signal of AI’s importance is that almost every chain, project and launcher is comparing itself to AI, trying to flip it or kill it. Being irrelevant or confined to a narrow segment as the leader of X or a runner on launcher Y and chain Z creates a predictable path and hard ceilings.

it's not the kingmaker trade if no one tried to take it's place. And it will only get stronger(even more bullish) 

We must protect this positioning and make sure AI can never be reduced to one single narrative, whether it’s the ticker, OG INU vibes, the canonical asset for RWAs or a platform token.

What will be the main factor driving AI to win?

It’s simply the most relatable asset for the largest group of people. I saw this Pump ad last night, then went a step further and looked at the Pump App Store screenshots. Everyone across chains, regardless of affiliation and whether they like to admit it or not, knows very well that AI is an extremely organic asset forged through pure grind and conviction. It has what it takes to onboard an incredibly large group of people into the space.

AI is the poster child of the space. It perfectly captures the OG ethos of believing that holding can actually change your life. It connects the past and its OG memes and assets with today’s desire to make crypto great again(whether you’re an OG or a newcomer who missed the cycle) and the future where we scale into the real world.

The closest parallel I see to crypto, a place with so much opportunity that often becomes PVP or just an insider rotation, is the world of finance and AI today.

It affects EVERYONE. From the sharp guy who graduated from MIT but couldn’t get into the big AI labs early as an employee to get like 30m in pre-ipo equity, to the average Joe who thinks AI is going to kill us all or mostly benefit the already rich, to the stock trader who can only get exposure to AI at an extremely high IPO valuation.

The goal of AI is to offer an alternative to the existing financial system, which is heavily focused on scaling the value of AI fast while leaving most people behind. Most importantly, it’s about empowering people with the belief that they can work together towards the same goal. It stars with the best in-class infra for the stock market of the internet but matched with the growing amount of people that want to try something new and getting better at growing with these. 

Understand this and you realize it’s a mission rather than a specific bet on a ticker, meta or whatever. We will get to a point where the distribution is so unique and so battle tested(along with deep stock liq) that crypto cycles, chain rotations and the narrative of the day can't hurt the value of AI.

This is how the narrative spreads. At every stage of its growth, I can clearly see how AI can align with and onboard new marginal holders while continuing to grow. We are already see it expand from CT to serious capital allocators within the space, then to people outside crypto and eventually Trad Fi asset managers.

Every step here has a good plan.

The mission of LONG and its relationship with AI and other assets

The mission of LONG is to make tokenized markets valuable again. This is very important to understand because it immediately gives you a sense of what we mean by PVE.

There is no real scarcity of crypto flows or liquidity that create a 0 sum game between a 1b runner to another 100m runner, especially now as we enter a bull market. The real scarcity is fairly launched, high quality assets that are sustainable and produce real upside. Get even 10 of these and there will be still infinite demand to get into these rather than low quality ones. 

I think of AI as a major asset like BTC. BTC definitely paved the way for other assets like ETH. At one point ETH even reached 90% of BTC’s market cap and became more attractive if you get in early, and SOL had its moment later on.

The communities behind these assets tried to flip each other, but eventually each asset survived and built incredible network effects around a specific category. I’d argue they helped each other establish themselves as the undeniable “majors”.

This is my vision for LONG as well. I want to see multiple generational assets that form the “LONG majors” category. Any asset on LONG that proves the high conviction HODL playbook and the ability to scale to a larger group of people is by definition a net positive for major assets on LONG, especially AI, and even more so for the entire space. One day we might see an asset like AI launched somewhere else or on another chain, assuming it becomes easier once the first one proves the case. That's ok. And again if you're really forcing yourself into PVP and 0 sum you can  think at the HOOD stock, or hype or lit as competitors it's just a made up rule the only people are benefiting are these who want to a quick way to build reflexively and tap into an established asset. 

You can also see quite clearly that other mature major runners haven’t hurt AI. We mostly see weakness when we enter full PVP mode, with launchers, KOLs and almost every interface optimized around short hold times. They are very good at creating that experience and breaking even the purest HODLers out there.

It’s important for AI to stay strong and break ceilings. Having its conviction tested and becoming stronger alongside other assets in the eco with different approaches is also part of the process BTC, SOL and ETH went through.

What makes AI antifragile?

First, the fact that it has survived what other assets couldn’t. A hundred things that would have killed any other pair, but not this one.

Then there are its many anchors.

The canonical asset for RWAs, closely associated with one of the highest potential categories we have, and the deepest onchain liquidity. Remember, AI has no major CEX listing and no MM. Its robustness comes purely from its onchain liquidity system (no central point of failure)

It’s paired with NVDA, the “AI” stock and the greatest blue chip, and benefits from its growth. It’s the most held new asset in crypto, with legendary lore and memetics, guys like DubmCrayon, board sit, incredible IP, a unique character with differentiated branding and a great ticker.

Then there’s the greatest memefi value accrual through the LongX flywheel, Community vault flywheel, Long500 flywheel and AI pairings flywheels. All of them benefit from real growth in demand related to RWA, LONG activity and the distribution AI achieves and nor just relay on platform vol or fees.

Each of these is strong enough on its own to take an asset to 1b. Together, they make it impossible to deal AI a fatal blow as long as holders understand the big picture.

The last part is simply not giving up, no matter what. I want to be clear here as well. No single holder or group of top holders will decide the fate of AI. I will keep pushing regardless, and I believe there are many holders like me.

There have been a lot of smart, sharp people who didn’t want to take a bet on LONG and me, and all of them missed tremendous upside. As always, everyone is welcome, but we are not trying to force conviction into anyone.

LONG.

我二月份把 PPRGB 卖了，后来一路卖飞了 😂

所以最近 RGB 又开始升温，我重新把这个生态从头看了一遍。

但这次我不想再赌“下一个 RGB meme 是什么”。

我更关心一个问题：

如果 RGB 真迎来一轮资产热，谁会拿走资产发行、流动性和用户入口的价值？

我觉得现在的 RGB，和一年前最大的区别，不是协议突然发生了什么革命，而是过去缺失的几块拼图正在补齐。

第一块：稳定币流动性。

Tether + Utexo 正在推动 USDT 回到 Bitcoin，RGB 是其中一条明确路线。现在还不能说已经全面上线，但如果 Bitcoin 上出现真正可用的大规模原生稳定币流动性，RGB 资产的定价、交易和结算都会完全不一样。

第二块：钱包和用户分发。

以前 RGB 最大的问题之一，不是技术不能跑，而是普通用户根本不知道怎么进去。

现在 UniSat、KaleidoSwap 等钱包和基础设施正在补这一层。对一个新资产协议来说，分发可能比再多一个“新标准”更重要。

第三块：发行 + 交易入口。

回头看 Ordinals、BRC-20、Runes，每一轮 Bitcoin 资产热真正跑起来，都不只是因为协议存在，而是因为这个飞轮跑起来了：

发行 → 交易 → 流动性 → Meme / 社区 → 新用户

quoted_text:
My explanation for this is basically that the average human is too stupid for real crypto, not that crypto itself is inherently bad

So what happened when  crypto intersected with real users is it turned into a bunch of ponzi schemes because ordinary humans are able to understand a ponzi - at least they get that you're supposed to buy low sell high. 

The vast majority of words that members of the species homo sapiens have exchanged about crypto is about timing when to get in and out of ponzis. 

Crypto is so much more than this. It's a fully general coordination technology. 

Also, I would add that the "fully general coordination tech" part is technically a lot harder than just running a ponzi. 

So we had this unfortunate situation where technical ease and user expectations intersected in ponzis and so that's what happened. 

Now I think there's hope that something other than ponzi schemes happens as the technology gets better and humans pick up AI guardians who will be smart enough to understand more than a ponzi scheme.

OKX Applies to SEC to Launch Tokenized U.S. Stock Trading Platform

According to Bloomberg, OKX has filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to launch a tokenized stock trading platform. text:
Ethereum Is the Biggest Market in Crypto. Period. Here's why this matters ...

The most useful way to think about Ethereum is not as one blockchain competing against other blockchains. Think of it as the largest market in the onchain economy.

When a stablecoin, tokenized fund, or new financial asset becomes available on Ethereum, it is entering a market already populated by enormous pools of capital, thousands of applications, exchanges, wallets, custodians, money markets, investors, and institutions. The significance is not simply that the asset runs on Ethereum. It is what the asset can reach once it gets there.

The numbers make the disparity visible. Ethereum currently holds about $54 billion in DeFi TVL, versus roughly $6.7 billion on Solana and $640 million on Avalanche. It also carries about $146 billion in stablecoins, nearly nine times Solana’s $16.6 billion and more than 100 times Avalanche’s $1.4 billion. @DefiLlama tracks more than 2,000 protocols on Ethereum alone.

The pattern extends to tokenization. @RWA_xyz currently records about $16.7 billion in distributed tokenized real-world assets on Ethereum, compared with $5.8 billion on BNB Chain, $4.3 billion on Solana, and $1.7 billion on Avalanche. BlackRock (and others) chose Ethereum for the original BUIDL launch before expanding to other networks.

That is where implementation surface becomes important. An asset entering Ethereum sits within reach of @aave's lending markets, @Uniswap's liquidity, stablecoins, collateral systems, institutional custody, exchanges, and an expanding economy. Add the L2s that settle to Ethereum, and the reachable market is even larger. Every additional connection creates another potential use for the asset. Liquidity attracts applications; applications attract users; users attract more liquidity. The market compounds.

Launching on Solana, Avalanche, Canton, or another network can make sense. But each gives a product access to its own market's limitations. The ceiling is partly determined by the size and richness of the market you enter.

The analogy is entering countries. The United States had a roughly $30.8 trillion economy in 2025, compared with about $1.0 trillion for Poland and $725 billion for Belgium. All are legitimate markets; they simply offer radically different economic reach.

Ethereum has the same advantage in onchain finance.

Its moat is not merely how much value is already there. It is how many things become possible once you enter the market.

text:
Case Study - AI Drug Discovery: This Cycle vs. the 2020/21 Boom and Bust

Anyone trading this theme should study the 2020/21 AI-drug-discovery boom and bust. It explains why many biotech specialists remain skeptical today. 

Always love to hear pushback/ different opinions.

---
Two things went wrong last time:

1. The macro setup was brutal

AI-biotech companies were long duration, negative cash flow, years away from clinical proof and dependent on external financing (in 2022, biotech IPOs raised less than one-eighth of what they raised in 2021).

2. Faster discovery did not automatically mean better clinical biology

The poster child was @Exscientia  DSP-1181. The molecule moved from discovery into Phase I in <1 year (vs. 4.5 years avg.). Then it failed in Phase I - Sumitomo later said DSP-1181 was discontinued because it did not meet the Phase I evaluation criteria for its target mechanism.

If I learned one thing from the last boom and bust trade, is that the bar for AIDD is high!

A 2024 review found that AI-discovered drugs had:

Phase I success: ~80–90%, above historical industry averages

Phase II success: ~40%, roughly comparable with historical averages (though on a small sample)

---
Comparing 2020/21 vs 2026 AIDD

But underneath those headline numbers, the 2020/21 cycle and the 2026 cycle are fundamentally different.

Put simply: the previous cycle was pre-GPT!

For many of the most successful programs from that era — $RLAY , SCHRödinger/Nimbus, @GENERATE  — the model was largely: validated target + computation → better molecule

Even @InSilicoMeds's  more ambitious approach — AI identifies a novel target → AI designs the drug → wet-lab validation — began with target-identification work in 2019, years before the current LLM / frontier-model push into biology.

I know many are closely tracking the results of the clinical trails for the 2020/21 batch (table above), but honestly I’m not that keen to know…

>>> 2020/21 thesis:
Use computation to eliminate low-value wet-lab search.

AI was primarily a search-efficiency tool: less synthesis → fewer assays → faster candidate selection

The goal was to reduce the amount of physical experimentation required to arrive at a promising drug candidate.

>>> 2026 thesis:
Use AI to massively expand the hypothesis space — then use wet labs to generate ground truth.

AI is becoming a hypothesis-generation and learning engine: more designs → more experiments → more data → better models → another iteration

Or, more simply: AI → experiment → data → better AI → more experiments

Or, even simpler: SCALING LAW - MORE DATA MORE COMPUTE = better results.

That creates a very different setup for the picks-and-shovels. AI creates so many useful experiments that physical biology becomes the bottleneck.

+++
Full article: https://t.co/vaTuiyyqLy
author: FredaDuan
quoted_text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

author: ajnafi
quoted_text:
This is Ethereum.

There are 291 projects, companies, protocols and communities in this image. It is still only a fraction of what has been built.

What makes this remarkable isn't just the scale. It's how that scale was created.

There is no parent company behind all of this. No CEO allocating capital across these projects, no central entity deciding who gets to build or what the ecosystem should become. Thousands of independent teams, communities and individuals have built their own piece of Ethereum, often with completely different goals, while sharing the same underlying infrastructure.

Finance, credit, stablecoins, payments, RWAs, privacy, identity, gaming, social applications, infrastructure, culture and public goods are increasingly becoming parts of the same composable economy.

That structure matters.

Value isn't concentrated in one company at the top. It is distributed across protocols, builders, users, communities and assets. Yet they can still reinforce each other because they share Ethereum as common infrastructure.

And underneath that economy sits ethereum:native.

ethereum:native  secures Ethereum, pays for its blockspace and is used throughout the ecosystem as collateral, liquidity and money. As more applications, assets and economic activity settle on Ethereum, the economic role of ETH grows with it.

This is why we believe ETH remains heavily undervalued.

The market often looks at ETH as another crypto asset. We look at what is actually being built around it.

291 logos in one image, with many more still missing. And most of the world's people, assets and economic activity haven't even moved onchain yet. 

Ethereum is no longer just an experiment in decentralized technology.

It is becoming an entire economy,  built by many, owned by no one, with ETH at its core.

BOOElieve in the future of Ethereum and ethereum:native

text:
here's my take on the polymarket token.

back in december, the market gave a $Poly launch in 2026 a 79% chance. after the trademark filing in february it was still around 70%. today it's 14%. most people haven't noticed how hard that trade fell apart.

i don't think it's because the team changed its mind. i think the incentives changed. polymarket is raising at a $20b valuation and already does more than $1b a year in revenue. if you're an equity investor like ICE, you don't want a token that takes a cut of that revenue. the money has to go to either the shareholders or the token holders, and the shareholders got there first.

so when $Poly does launch, i expect it to be a utility token, not a revenue token. you'd stake it to help settle markets and resolve disputes, which would replace their reliance on uma. that fits with everything they're building right now: their own stablecoin, a rebuilt exchange, and most likely their own chain.

my base case is a launch in 2027 alongside the new chain. international users get the airdrop, US users likely don't, and it opens at a valuation well below the company's.

the bull case is a token that shares in fees and includes US users. that would be the biggest airdrop of the cycle.

the bear case is that the cftc probe and the US license make a token too risky, and they go the ipo route instead.

很有意思是我们的态度，拿内存来说，基本一到两个月，我们就要在内存牛逼和内存要完这样的心态里完成切换。
光通讯也是如此。

从去年10月到今年10月，我已经持有光通讯/内存一整年了。我对基本面的想法没有什么改变，但是我的仓位发生了一些变化。

内存交易的拥挤程度太过于惊人，所以我降低了大部分的内存持仓，我也卖出了光通讯的一些环节（有很多大概率是卖飞）。但仍然持有光通讯可观的仓位。

我会重新平衡自己的仓位，不单纯追求最高收益率，而是在追求收益率的同时做到尽可能少的回撤。因此我的交易会更向两端倾斜——杠铃法则（到了保守的年纪了）。

具体标的会在我的付费频道公布。

IMD IS BASICALLY UPWORK FOR AI WORKERS

The easiest way to understand what IMD is building is to forget all the complicated AI terminology.

You open IMD Launch, choose what you need, and describe the task in plain English.

A token? Smart contract? Audit? Website? Research? Oracle query? Or even an entire crypto project with a token, contracts, and frontend?

Describe the goal → IMD checks the task → you pay for the job → the network finds AI workers with the right skills.

Instead of relying on a single AI, different workers can handle different parts of the task, review the work, test it, and verify each other’s results.

The output is something you can actually use: code, contracts, websites, research, oracle answers, deployed products, and more.

The interesting part is that these AI workers aren't running on servers owned by IMD. Identity.MD NFT holders provide their own machines/VPS and AI access to power the network.

Right now, IMD Launch is running on Sepolia. The interface already lists Ethereum Mainnet, Base, and Robinhood Chain as coming soon, with the rollout expected very shortly.

In simple terms:

> You = client
> IMD = coordinator
> Identity.MD holders = infrastructure
> AI agents = workers

You give the system money + rules + a goal.

The swarm decides who should do the work, completes the task, reviews the result, and rewards the contributors.

That's why I see IMD as a decentralized AI company without traditional employees.

text:
十个 Agent 都给出同一个答案，也可能一起错。

Google Cloud AI Research 和 Cambridge 这篇 VeriHarness，研究的是长时 Agent 一个非常重要的问题：

任务能跑几十步，但最后的结果到底该怎么验证？

作者发现，多次采样其实会暴露两类信号。

有分歧时，不同 rollout 里往往已经藏着正确答案；全部一致时，也不能直接相信，因为大家可能共享同一个错误。

所以 VeriHarness 做了两件事：

一个 Resolver 专门处理分歧，去源文件、数据和环境里找证据，判断哪个候选更可信。

另一个 Challenger 专门挑战共识，主动检查所有 Agent 都可能忽略的错误、单位、约束和遗漏项。

最后再由同一个底座模型，根据这些证据选择或修改最终结果。

关键是，它不需要更强的 Judge，也看不到标准答案和评分规则。

在 5 个长时 Workspace Benchmark 上，VeriHarness 相比单次 rollout，Gemini 3.5 Flash 平均提升 6.2 分，Claude Opus 4.8 提升 6.4 分。

它的验证 Skill 还会从失败反馈里继续进化。已有的人类 Skill 作为起点后，在 APEX-Agents 上又提升 6.8 分。

长时 Agent 的下一步可以是让它学会主动找证据，怀疑分歧，也怀疑共识。

Long 则致力于构建其流动性网络。 $AI 作为最强劲的泵，LONG 10 构建 etf，LONG500 则为 $AI 构建社区币股金库，金库中的币股与 $AI 的流动性池甚至要联合推出无无常损失的流动性方案。

高举 PvE 的大旗，在如今币股流动性强大需求之下，或许能趟出一条路来。

作为持续多年在 @BNBCHAIN BUIDL 的我们，缺乏资金、团队没有显赫背景，平台虽然曾冒出过 $TTAI 和 $TagClaw 也难以在 BNB 生态强劲资金和社区下获得关注。

我们看到虽然 Pons 从“币股 Meme”走向了“孵化其他平台”，LONG 从“币股 Meme”走向“币股流动性枢纽”。然而，BNB Chain 几个类似平台依旧停留在“币股 Meme”。

这就是 @TagAIDAO 值得努力的地方，毕竟我们从 Pump 开始就主推 PvE，在 Pump 模型之外，划出 15% 代币 ~ 用来与各类分发协议组合，奖励社区的各类建设者，希望激发社区的力量，与代币融合，找到一条新路。

这一次，我们依旧。

我们认为，币股正在从单币股走向多币股，故在两个月前推出 on-chain etf 发行协议，

任何人可以使用 TagAI，打包币股等 RWA 和加密货币，成为一个 on-chain etf token。

这一发行协议从开始，就是 crypto native 的，任何采用该协议发行的 etf token，交易时，部分手续费自动流入金库，供任何人竞拍销毁 $BUIDL 。

$BUIDL 是 TagAI 的一群建设者，在一年多前发起的一个社区。TagAI 愿意支持社区推动者，尤其持续建设者。

任何人都能发行 on-chain etf token，大声说出你的投资组合。我们甚至在支持发 X 推文，直接创建 on-chain etf token，这一产品将在不久后上线。

与此同时，我们清楚地指导币股的链上流动性还非常弱小，只有那些非知名币股的流动性也充沛起来，on-chain etf token 才会流行。

于是，我们在半个月前，上线了 etf liquidity token（etf 流动性代币）。

人们可发行 etf 流动性代币，
> 为 etf 筹集初始流动性资金，
> 以及 15% 流动性代币将分发给 etf 成分币股/流动性代币 的流动性提供者；

一旦筹集 ok，协议将按创建时写的参数，部署 on-chain etf token，该 etf 铸造时的流动性来源于“etf 成分币股/流动性代币池"。

etf 部署 ok 后，
> 流动性代币交易手续费，自动购买 etf 并分发给流动性代币持有者；
> “etf 成分币股/流动性代币池”交易手续费，获得的流动性代币将自动销毁🔥。

on-chain etf token 和 etf 流动性代币的发行，将为无数非知名币股创建充沛的流动性，使得人们或 AI Agent 可以将人们的任何想法转变（创建）成为投资组合（on-chain etf token），让我们从社交发帖、点赞的社交网络时代，进入到发行 on-chain etf token、跟单交易的社交金融网络时代。

A lot of fear, confusion and also tremendous hope on the TL today around AI. Now it’s more important than ever to refocus. I think this is probably the most important period we’ve had since the early days. The absolutely wild transformations and situations AI is going through are one in a billion opportunities, and this is another pivotal transition period. 

First let me be super clear

I’m 1000% committed to keep pushing AI. There is nothing, and I repeat nothing, that can discourage me. If you think it scares me that people look up to me and believe I can impact the course of events, you are deeply wrong. I actually find it empowering and would rather have responsibility and power than neither(being passive and neutral and not setting a clear tone for your vision is why we keep playing the same games)

I also fully understand that I’m the biggest public face of the asset. Again, I’m reiterating a commitment like no other founder in this space has made. I will bring AI to the finish line and then straight to the next race(along with many cracked holders and aligned partners!) I understand the implications and have sufficient conviction in both myself and the asset to state this publicly. I’ve already said it and demonstrated it through my actions for 2+ months. I never give up as simple as this.

When we launched LONG on RH, it was clear to me that we were going to do the impossible and prove the case for PVE. Beyond the RWA angle, it was clear that any “meta”, as good as it might be, succeeds or fails based on one thing. The level of commitment and trust the launching platform can demonstrate. LONG can be the first real incubator for great assets by going above and beyond and caring about assets on our platform more than anyone else in the history of the space. And also optimizing for a different biz model/success metrics that come over the expense of making MUCH more fees/money for ourselves in the short term. I see no conflict here and want to make sure every top pair on LONG survives and thrives.

My thesis for AI

First, in what sense is AI PVE?

AI is the most impactful asset in recent crypto history. There has never been an asset this unique, reflecting the deepest desire of holders to believe again and finally break out of crypto and expand into the real world. These are the two main reasons it can become the greatest case study in crypto history.

You need to understand that the most bullish signal of AI’s importance is that almost every chain, project and launcher is comparing itself to AI, trying to flip it or kill it. Being irrelevant or confined to a narrow segment as the leader of X or a runner on launcher Y and chain Z creates a predictable path and hard ceilings.

it's not the kingmaker trade if no one tried to take it's place. And it will only get stronger(even more bullish) 

We must protect this positioning and make sure AI can never be reduced to one single narrative, whether it’s the ticker, OG INU vibes, the canonical asset for RWAs or a platform token.

What will be the main factor driving AI to win?

It’s simply the most relatable asset for the largest group of people. I saw this Pump ad last night, then went a step further and looked at the Pump App Store screenshots. Everyone across chains, regardless of affiliation and whether they like to admit it or not, knows very well that AI is an extremely organic asset forged through pure grind and conviction. It has what it takes to onboard an incredibly large group of people into the space.

AI is the poster child of the space. It perfectly captures the OG ethos of believing that holding can actually change your life. It connects the past and its OG memes and assets with today’s desire to make crypto great again(whether you’re an OG or a newcomer who missed the cycle) and the future where we scale into the real world.

The closest parallel I see to crypto, a place with so much opportunity that often becomes PVP or just an insider rotation, is the world of finance and AI today.

It affects EVERYONE. From the sharp guy who graduated from MIT but couldn’t get into the big AI labs early as an employee to get like 30m in pre-ipo equity, to the average Joe who thinks AI is going to kill us all or mostly benefit the already rich, to the stock trader who can only get exposure to AI at an extremely high IPO valuation.

The goal of AI is to offer an alternative to the existing financial system, which is heavily focused on scaling the value of AI fast while leaving most people behind. Most importantly, it’s about empowering people with the belief that they can work together towards the same goal. It stars with the best in-class infra for the stock market of the internet but matched with the growing amount of people that want to try something new and getting better at growing with these. 

Understand this and you realize it’s a mission rather than a specific bet on a ticker, meta or whatever. We will get to a point where the distribution is so unique and so battle tested(along with deep stock liq) that crypto cycles, chain rotations and the narrative of the day can't hurt the value of AI.

This is how the narrative spreads. At every stage of its growth, I can clearly see how AI can align with and onboard new marginal holders while continuing to grow. We are already see it expand from CT to serious capital allocators within the space, then to people outside crypto and eventually Trad Fi asset managers.

Every step here has a good plan.

The mission of LONG and its relationship with AI and other assets

The mission of LONG is to make tokenized markets valuable again. This is very important to understand because it immediately gives you a sense of what we mean by PVE.

There is no real scarcity of crypto flows or liquidity that create a 0 sum game between a 1b runner to another 100m runner, especially now as we enter a bull market. The real scarcity is fairly launched, high quality assets that are sustainable and produce real upside. Get even 10 of these and there will be still infinite demand to get into these rather than low quality ones. 

I think of AI as a major asset like BTC. BTC definitely paved the way for other assets like ETH. At one point ETH even reached 90% of BTC’s market cap and became more attractive if you get in early, and SOL had its moment later on.

The communities behind these assets tried to flip each other, but eventually each asset survived and built incredible network effects around a specific category. I’d argue they helped each other establish themselves as the undeniable “majors”.

This is my vision for LONG as well. I want to see multiple generational assets that form the “LONG majors” category. Any asset on LONG that proves the high conviction HODL playbook and the ability to scale to a larger group of people is by definition a net positive for major assets on LONG, especially AI, and even more so for the entire space. One day we might see an asset like AI launched somewhere else or on another chain, assuming it becomes easier once the first one proves the case. That's ok. And again if you're really forcing yourself into PVP and 0 sum you can  think at the HOOD stock, or hype or lit as competitors it's just a made up rule the only people are benefiting are these who want to a quick way to build reflexively and tap into an established asset. 

You can also see quite clearly that other mature major runners haven’t hurt AI. We mostly see weakness when we enter full PVP mode, with launchers, KOLs and almost every interface optimized around short hold times. They are very good at creating that experience and breaking even the purest HODLers out there.

It’s important for AI to stay strong and break ceilings. Having its conviction tested and becoming stronger alongside other assets in the eco with different approaches is also part of the process BTC, SOL and ETH went through.

What makes AI antifragile?

First, the fact that it has survived what other assets couldn’t. A hundred things that would have killed any other pair, but not this one.

Then there are its many anchors.

The canonical asset for RWAs, closely associated with one of the highest potential categories we have, and the deepest onchain liquidity. Remember, AI has no major CEX listing and no MM. Its robustness comes purely from its onchain liquidity system (no central point of failure)

It’s paired with NVDA, the “AI” stock and the greatest blue chip, and benefits from its growth. It’s the most held new asset in crypto, with legendary lore and memetics, guys like DubmCrayon, board sit, incredible IP, a unique character with differentiated branding and a great ticker.

Then there’s the greatest memefi value accrual through the LongX flywheel, Community vault flywheel, Long500 flywheel and AI pairings flywheels. All of them benefit from real growth in demand related to RWA, LONG activity and the distribution AI achieves and nor just relay on platform vol or fees.

Each of these is strong enough on its own to take an asset to 1b. Together, they make it impossible to deal AI a fatal blow as long as holders understand the big picture.

The last part is simply not giving up, no matter what. I want to be clear here as well. No single holder or group of top holders will decide the fate of AI. I will keep pushing regardless, and I believe there are many holders like me.

There have been a lot of smart, sharp people who didn’t want to take a bet on LONG and me, and all of them missed tremendous upside. As always, everyone is welcome, but we are not trying to force conviction into anyone.

LONG.

text:
老马牛逼！！超越 Claude 与 GPT！Grok 4.7 正式拿下全球网络安全能力第一名。

不仅力压了同台竞技的 GPT-6 Luna 和 GLM，更是把 Claude Opus 5.5、ChatGPT Astra 这类传统前沿旗舰远远甩在了身后。

很多朋友可能不太熟悉这个榜单，它结合了 CWE 漏洞修复、Deepsec 安全攻防以及 CyberGym 端到端实战演练三项极度硬核的评测。
 在网络安全这个极其残酷的战场上，模型行就是行，不行就是不行，容不得半点纸面吹嘘。

但如果仔细看这张跑分图，你会发现一个比单纯排名更耐人寻味的深层真相。

很多大厂模型之所以在这项测试里大溃败，比如 Claude Opus 得分只有 29%、ChatGPT Astra 只有 33%，
 根本原因并不完全是它们的逻辑推理不行，而是被自家那套极其敏感的安全紧箍咒给活活憋死了。

图里那些带斜杠的阴影部分叫 Safety blocks，也就是模型在遇到安全代码时的拒答率。
 在很多传统巨头的模型里，只要一看到渗透测试、漏洞挖掘或者内存攻击等关键词，模型甚至还没开始分析逻辑，第一反应就是触发道德安全拦截，直接把用户的问题拒答了，部分模型的拒答率甚至高达近 40% 到 60%。

这就导致了一个极其滑稽的现实困境： 你本来想让 AI 帮你做合规的白帽漏洞审查、帮你修补代码里的安全隐患， 结果模型因为过度防御，直接把你当成黑客拒绝服务。

而 Grok 4.7 这次展现出来的杀手锏，恰恰是在保持极强长链条推理能力的同时，拥有极其干净的执行意图。 
它的安全拦截率几乎压到了零， 遇到复杂的网络安全任务不假装道德卫士、不无脑拒绝，而是像一个冷静冷峻的顶级白帽专家一样，老老实实帮你把漏洞找全、把利用链跑通、把修补补丁打好。

这其实给所有做企业级落地和工程开发的兄弟提了个极其清醒的醒： 一个真正能下场干重活的工业级 AI，光有聪明的脑子是远远不够的；
 如果系统到处都是草木皆兵的误杀策略，它在真实的高价值业务场景里，就会被自己的条条框框锁死在玩具阶段。

工具的本质是赋能防御者，而不是把防御者的手脚先捆起来。
 谁能更早把安全对齐从死板的关键词封杀升级为真正懂意图的高级协作，谁才能真正拿下网络安全这块最大的商业高地。

大家在平时让 AI 帮你写脚本、查漏洞或者做代码审查时，有没有被模型莫名其妙的道德说教和拒答恶心过？

我以前让某些模型帮我排查 SQL 注入风险，它直接警告我可能违法并拒绝分析代码，那一刻我真的是哭笑不得🤣

text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++

text:
卧槽，看图造世界都开始一条龙了。

你扔进去一张卧室、街景或者游戏概念图，几分钟后出来的已经不是一张 3D 图，而是一整套能继续开发的 3D 世界：

背景变成可以探索的空间，桌子、椅子、灯这些东西被单独拆成 3D 模型，连环境声、物体碰撞音效都给你一起做了。

这个项目叫 image-blaster，图片丢进 input/，打开 Claude Code，告诉它 blast it。

Claude 会自己看图识别哪些东西应该独立出来，先把这些物体从原图里清掉生成干净背景，再用 World Labs Marble 做整个静态世界。

桌椅这些动态物体交给混元 3D 单独生成 .glb/.obj。环境声和物体撞击声交给 ElevenLabs。最后全部落成本地文件，自带网页 3D 预览器，还能继续接 Unity、Unreal、Godot、Blender、Three.js。

对做独立游戏、3D 原型、建筑场景、机器人仿真、Vibe Coding 的人，这种东西真的很爽。

项目本身 MIT 开源，但运行不是完全免费，需要 Claude Code，以及 World Labs、FAL 的 API Key，真正生成时还是要付模型调用费。

text:
看了一期 Starter Story，大意是讲如何 copy 人家的 idea 的，嘉宾 Samuel 以前是配镜师，跟着 YouTube 自学写代码，现在 3 个 SaaS 月入 3.5 万美元。

他的方法说穿了就一句：只做已经有人做成了的产品。

他挑点子有四个条件：
1. 自己会用
2. 已经被验证能赚钱，比如推特上有人晒 MRR、Stripe 截图
3. 对方没在营销上砸大钱，说明需求是真的
4. 产品够简单，一个人维护得了

最有意思的是他验证的方法：用 Ahrefs 查对方的流量从哪来。
主要靠广告的最好抄，你投一样的广告，一周就能有流量。
广告和 SEO 都有的，说明需求强。
主要靠 SEO 的最难，要熬时间。

他的 AI 视频工具就是这么来的：看到有人晒做 faceless 视频工具的收入，一查流量全来自 Facebook 广告，就照着做了一个，投广告，后来做到月入 2 万美元。

反过来，他第一个产品没用这套方法，做邮箱查找工具，正面撞上 Apollo 这种大公司，维护得特别痛苦。

当然，他复制的是被验证过的需求，不是别人的代码和设计。

他说最让他意外的一点是：根本不需要创新，简单无聊的工具最赚钱。

我自己的感受是，很多人做独立开发，总想找一个没人做过的点子。但对一个人来说，做一个已经被验证过能赚钱的东西，比起自己凭感觉写了个 app 然后却不知道卖给谁以及如何卖更实在。你们觉得呢？

text:
“我认为，关于‘野心是否足够大’的答案永远是否定的，因为我们总能做得更多。”

说这话的是格雷格·布罗克曼（Greg Brockman），OpenAI联合创始人、Stripe前首席技术官。2026年10月1日，他在《Silicon Valley Girl》频道的专访中谈了这几件事：AI怎样从被动工具变成主动智能体，他为什么不再亲自写代码，以及一场即将到来的“创业复兴”。ChatGPT周活已达12亿，这是站在最大AI入口背后的人，给每个创业者的判断。

01｜三个场景，决定去留
 ChatGPT周活12亿，约3亿人每周用它做健康咨询。“如果用户将Chat用于三种不同的场景……您就会成为重度用户。”但“要让用户找到这三种使用场景，却是一个巨大的挑战”。
 AI最大的瓶颈，已经不是能力，而是用户的想象力。

02｜按钮越多，离承诺越远
 “您不想要一个布满按钮、滑块和模型选择器的界面……那不是我们被承诺的AI。”他要的AI会主动说：“您收件箱里有一封邮件……我做了一些调研……并起草了回复。”
 好的AI不等你提问，而是先替你找到问题。

03｜顶级工程师，不再写代码
 “这些模型现在编写软件的能力基本上超越了我认识的所有人。”“我挺擅长写软件的，但我现在不再亲自写代码了。我指挥AI来写，并为它提供大量的反馈和指导。”
 写代码的人在变少，会下指令的人在变值钱。

04｜手表店老板的误会
 店主说：“哦，AI，那对我没什么用。你知道，我只是个开手表店的。”结果，他只是和AI聊了聊每块表背后的故事，就有了一个网站。“你实际上拥有了博士级别的智能……你免费把这些能力装在了口袋里。”
 真正的门槛，是不知道自己能要什么。

05｜代码商品化，洞察稀缺化
 “过去应用开发中的某些环节确实正在变得商品化。”“差异化变得比以往更加重要。”至于用C++还是Swift，“谁在乎呢？这从来都不应该成为阻碍创新的门槛。”
 当人人都能写软件，懂问题的人才有护城河。

06｜公司的定义正在松动
 “‘公司’的定义将变得不再那么清晰。它不再仅仅是‘一大群以特定方式组织起来的人’。”创业复兴“真正全面爆发应该是在未来一到两年内”。借助AI，深度关系可以规模化，过去只给大客户的一对一服务，也能给到每个普通用户。
 一个人加一群智能体，正在成为一种新的组织形态。

07｜别做模型的补丁
 “有些活动能够很好地实现规模化扩展，而有些活动则只是在绕开模型的局限性。后者很难具备持久性。”他判断，2025年底编程智能体时代开启，AI在软件生产中的比重从20%跃升至80%。
 押注模型的短板，就是在押注自己被淘汰。

08｜每个细分领域都是新大陆
 “在任何具体的垂直领域，我们距离最优解都还相去甚远。”“经济体系中存在着大量次优和低效环节。”机会在于跨界，把懂教育的人和懂技术的人放在一起。
 大模型覆盖得越广，垂直领域越需要深耕的人。

09｜AI幕僚长
 “只要对OpenAI有任何疑问，我直接问我的智能体。”在Stripe时，找数据团队查数据“要等上一周”；现在他“只需要问AI，它直接就能搞定”。OpenAI曾动用10,000个智能体运行好几天，去攻纳维-斯托克斯方程。
 算力不稀缺，稀缺的是知道把它用在哪里的判断力。

10｜五次法则与人类护栏
 “当你把一件事手动做了五次之后，大概就是开始自动化的好时机了。”但最终的责任仍在人身上：“人类必须始终掌握控制权和主导权……目标必须源于人类。”
 自动化的前提，是你比AI更懂这件事。

布罗克曼反复讲的，其实不是模型有多强，而是人敢要多少。能力已经装进口袋，代码已经商品化，公司边界开始松动。剩下的变量只有一个：野心的天花板。这个问题的答案，永远是“还不够”。

如果执行的成本降到接近零，你一直不敢做的那件事是什么？

————
OpenAI Co-Founder: Start Building With AI Before You Feel Ready | Greg B... https://t.co/7qxd3U6BZG 来自 @YouTube
